  review_version: 0.1
  hero:
    asset: references/brown-sugar.jpg
    title: Brown sugar examples 1.jpg
    source_page: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Brown_sugar_examples_1.jpg
    source_file: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/03/Brown_sugar_examples_1.jpg
    creator: Moe Rubenzahl
    licence: CC BY-SA 4.0
    licence_url: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
    attribution_text: Brown sugar examples 1.jpg — Moe Rubenzahl
    alt: Light and dark brown sugar in separate piles.
    reviewed_at: 2026-10-11
    width: 960
    height: 720
    changes: Resized by Wikimedia Commons; full frame retained.
    caption: Light and dark brown sugar.
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Soft brown sugar is sugar with a molasses-associated colour and flavour, sold in light and dark styles.
        It sweetens baking, glazes and sauces.
      sources:
        - domino-faq
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: sensory
      role: sensory
      text: Light soft brown sugar offers a gentler molasses character; a dark style gives a stronger flavour.
        Choose according to the flavour wanted in the recipe.
      sources:
        - domino-faq
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: uses
      role: uses
      text: Soft brown sugars are used in baking, glazes and sweet-savoury sauces. Product and recipe differences
        matter when considering alternatives.
      sources:
        - domino-faq
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: storage
      role: storage
      text: Keep brown sugar tightly covered in a cool place. Moisture loss can harden it; hard lumps are not a
        reproducible packed measure.
      sources:
        - domino-storage
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: scope
      role: context
      text: UK product ranges distinguish light and dark soft brown sugar from muscovado and demerara. These sugars
        differ; do not assume equal cup measures or identical results.
      sources:
        - billingtons-range
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: packing
      role: context
      text: For a packed measure, spoon sugar into the vessel, press down, repeat to fill, and level the top.
        Packing describes how you fill the vessel; a quantity given in grams needs no packing conversion.
      sources:
        - ch-pack
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: process
    id: emulsify
  review_version: 0.1
  hero:
    asset: references/emulsify.jpg
    title: Homemade mayonnaise.jpg
    source_page: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Homemade_mayonnaise.jpg
    source_file: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/79/Homemade_mayonnaise.jpg
    creator: Jason Terk from Somerville, MA, US
    licence: CC BY 2.0
    licence_url: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0
    attribution_text: Homemade mayonnaise.jpg — Jason Terk from Somerville, MA, US
    alt: A whisk surrounded by thick, pale yellow homemade mayonnaise.
    reviewed_at: 2026-10-11
    width: 960
    height: 640
    changes: Resized by Wikimedia Commons; full frame retained.
    caption: A whisk and the texture of homemade mayonnaise.
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Emulsifying disperses droplets of one liquid through another liquid with which it does not readily mix.
        The result can be temporary or stabilised.
      sources:
        - aocs-emulsion
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: Use emulsification to distribute fat through a sauce or dressing and develop the desired texture.
        Mayonnaise is one example, not the definition of the process.
      sources:
        - cia-mayo
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Mechanical action breaks up droplets. Emulsifying components help resist their joining together again;
        egg yolk supplies such components in familiar sauces.
      sources:
        - exploratorium-emulsion
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: For a mayonnaise-like sauce, look for a uniform creamy mixture rather than free oil. Addition rate,
        formulation, tool and temperature matter; there is no universal duration or mixing speed.
      sources:
        - cia-mayo
        - exploratorium-emulsion
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes
      role: mistakes
      text: Do not assume more whisking repairs every separated sauce. Overheating an egg sauce may coagulate
        proteins as well as disrupt the emulsion.
      sources:
        - exploratorium-emulsion
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: neighbours
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Mixing and blending may produce emulsions but need not. Whisking can emulsify or aerate; whipping
        commonly concerns foam. These actions do not always produce an emulsion.
      sources:
        - aocs-emulsion
        - egg-foam
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-5-distinction
      role: context
      text: Mounting a sauce with butter is one finishing application of emulsification. It incorporates butter into
        the liquid rather than using flour to bind it, and the resulting sauce can separate if its emulsion is
        disrupted.
      sources:
        - b5-mount
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: aocs-emulsion
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: exploratorium-emulsion
      role: introduction
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: cia-mayo
      role: technique-demonstration
      order: 3
      note: Worked written example; not a universal recipe.
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:

      target:

        - aocs-emulsion

    attribution_text: Searing of a Steak.jpg — Flo2323
    alt: A browned steak searing over a hot grill with smoke and flame.
    reviewed_at: 2026-10-11
    width: 960
    height: 640
    changes: Resized by Wikimedia Commons; full frame retained.
    caption: "One example of searing: a browned steak on a grill."
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Searing is brief cooking over strong heat to brown a food’s surface. It may be one stage of a longer
        cooking method rather than sufficient cooking by itself.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Look for the intended browned surface and distinguish useful brown pan deposits from burnt, bitter
        residue. Adjust to the food, cookware and method; no single pan temperature or duration applies.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes
      role: mistakes
      text: Searing does not seal in juices. A browned exterior is neither a moisture barrier nor proof that the
        interior has reached the desired condition.
      sources:
        - sear-myth
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: neighbours
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Brown describes a wider colour/flavour outcome. Grilling and pan-frying are cooking methods that can
        produce a sear. Caramelisation concerns sugar transformations and should not be used as a blanket
        explanation for every browned surface.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
        - caramelisation
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:

    - id: materials

  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Tomato is an edible fruit commonly treated as a vegetable in cooking. It is eaten fresh and cooked into
        sauces, soups and other dishes.
      sources:
        - usu-tomato
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: storage
      role: storage
      text: Allow unripe tomatoes to ripen out of direct sunlight before refrigerating them. Refrigeration slows
        ripening; storage advice depends on how ripe the fruit already is.
      sources:
        - usu-tomato
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: uses
      role: uses
      text: Freezing softens tomato texture. Thawed tomatoes are useful in cooked dishes such as soups and
        casseroles, rather than where a firm fresh slice matters.
      sources:
        - usu-tomato
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: Reducing a purée removes water and concentrates it. Fresh tomato and concentrated tomato products
        therefore need different treatment in a recipe; they are not equal-volume replacements.
      sources:
        - usu-tomato
      review_version: 0.1

  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Chicken is the meat of the domestic chicken, sold whole or divided into cuts such as breast and thigh.
        It is roasted, braised and used in dishes and stocks, with the cut affecting the method.
      sources:
        - fsis-chicken
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: uses
      role: uses
      text: A whole bird and separate pieces need different handling and cooking checks. Do not use a time given for
        one cut as evidence that another is cooked through.

    - id: context

      sources:

      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes

  editorial:
    - id: summary

      text: Coriander is a plant whose leaves are used as a herb and whose seeds are used as a spice. The leaves,
        whole seeds and ground seeds give different flavours and textures in cooking.
      sources:
        - usu-coriander
        - rhs-coriander
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: US sources commonly call the leaves cilantro and the seeds coriander. UK herb guidance uses coriander
        for the plant and its leaves as well as discussing the seeds. Look for an explicit part or preparation
        when following a recipe from another region.
      sources:
        - usu-coriander
        - rhs-coriander
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: uses
      role: uses
      text: Fresh leaves are used as a herb; seeds are harvested separately and may be used whole or ground. Do not
        replace a handful of leaves with the same amount of seed spice.
      sources:
        - rhs-coriander
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: storage
      role: storage
      text: "The forms need different storage: harvested seeds can be dried and kept in sealed containers, while
        leaves may be used fresh or preserved by freezing or drying."
      sources:
        - usu-coriander
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: selection
      role: selection
      text: Before buying or measuring, establish which form the recipe means. A chopped garnish suggests a
        different preparation from a spice ground into a mixture; if the wording still leaves doubt, ask the
        author.
      sources:
        - usu-coriander
        - rhs-coriander
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:

      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: rhs-coriander
      role: specialist-reference
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1

      sources:
        - usu-coriander
      review_version: 0.1
    - relation: contrast-with

      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1

      role: summary
      text: Chop means to cut food into smaller pieces. Roughly chopped and finely chopped call for different
        results.

      text: The pieces need not be precise cubes. Follow any size instruction rather than treating chop, dice and
        mince as identical.

    - id: batch-3-distinction
      role: context
      text: Rough chopping still benefits from reasonably similar piece sizes when the pieces will cook together.
        Irregular outlines and wildly different sizes are separate issues; a rustic cut need not mean uneven
        doneness.

  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Roasting cooks food with dry heat, commonly in an oven. It is useful for larger pieces of meat and
        poultry as well as vegetables.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: The exposed surface can brown while the interior cooks. Choose the method for the food and desired
        finish rather than assuming a single oven setting.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Judge both the surface and the interior. For poultry, use the safe internal-temperature guidance rather
        than taking browned skin as proof of doneness.
      sources:
        - fsis-chicken
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: near-neighbours
      role: near-neighbours
      text: A covered braise includes cooking liquid; roasting normally gives the surface more exposure to dry heat.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Covering a roasting vessel changes how moisture escapes and introduces a trapped-steam environment.
        Browning an exposed surface and retaining moisture under a lid are different aims; a recipe may
        deliberately move between them.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1

- target:

    id: blanch
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Blanching briefly heats food in boiling water or steam. In vegetable freezing, it controls enzyme
        activity that would otherwise harm quality.
      sources:
        - nchfp-blanch
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Use the schedule for the vegetable and piece size. A single time for every vegetable is not reliable.
      sources:
        - nchfp-blanch
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes
      role: mistakes
      text: Too little blanching can leave troublesome enzyme activity; too much can damage texture and flavour.
        Blanching for freezing is a specific preparation step, not a complete meal-cooking instruction.
      sources:
        - nchfp-blanch
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: For freezing, cool the vegetables promptly after blanching to stop further cooking, then drain well.
        Other recipes may use the heated food immediately.
      sources:
        - nchfp-blanch
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-4-distinction
      role: context
      text: A lifting strainer can remove a batch of food while retaining the blanching water in the pot. This
        differs from draining the whole pot through a colander and can be useful when the recipe calls for
        successive batches.
      sources:
        - b4-spider
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: nchfp-blanch

- target:

    id: braise
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Braising cooks food gently with some liquid in a covered vessel. Tougher cuts can become tender during
        the longer cooking.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: Browning first can build flavour, but the covered cooking stage does different work from searing.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: For a meat braise, look for the tenderness the recipe describes and keep the liquid at a gentle simmer.
        Surface colour alone is not the finishing test.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: near-neighbours
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Stews commonly cover the ingredients with liquid; braises often use larger pieces only partly submerged.
        Follow the particular method rather than imposing a universal liquid ratio.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: context
      text: A covered cooking stage and an uncovered sauce-finishing stage can belong to the same dish. Removing the
        lid encourages evaporation; this explains why the sauce may be reduced separately after the food is
        tender.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: process
    id: ferment
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Food fermentation is a process in which microorganisms transform food ingredients under conditions
        chosen for the intended result. Bacteria, yeasts and moulds contribute in different culinary contexts.
      sources:
        - isapp-ferment
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: The changes can create characteristic flavours and textures. Bread dough, cultured milk and fermented
        vegetables are different culinary contexts, not variations of one interchangeable procedure.
      sources:
        - isapp-ferment
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: "Microorganisms transform components of the food. Some processes produce acids or gas. The culinary term
        is broader than a strict no-oxygen definition: koji and vinegar production also fall within
        food-fermentation practice."
      sources:
        - isapp-ferment
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: For lactic-acid vegetable fermentation, the produce, salt, temperature and contact with brine all
        matter. Use a tested method for the particular food; the linked vegetable guidance is not a method for
        meat, dairy or every other ferment.
      sources:
        - umn-ferment
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Follow the chosen method’s checks and completion criteria. Bubbles or a sour aroma can be observations,
        but do not establish safety or shelf stability on their own.
      sources:
        - umn-ferment
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes
      role: mistakes
      text: Do not casually reduce salt in a tested fermented-pickle recipe. Salt helps select the desired microbial
        activity as well as influencing texture and flavour. This page gives context, not a standalone
        preservation recipe.
      sources:
        - nchfp-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: near-neighbours
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Adding vinegar makes food acidic without necessarily fermenting it. Ferment and pickle overlap in some
        traditions and methods, but one does not always imply the other.
      sources:
        - nchfp-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: context
      text: Fermentation names the microbial transformation, not a promise that living organisms remain in the
        finished food. Later processing can change that. The process name alone does not establish a product’s
        storage conditions or a health benefit.
      sources:
        - isapp-ferment
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: isapp-ferment
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: umn-ferment

      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: process
    id: pickle
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Pickling is preservation by acidification, either through fermentation or by adding suitable acid. The
        chosen recipe determines the ingredients, acidity and storage method.
      sources:
        - nchfp-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: The method changes flavour and texture. Refrigerator pickles and products processed for shelf storage
        require different handling; the word pickled does not tell you how a jar should be stored.
      sources:
        - umn-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: In fermented vegetable pickles, microorganisms produce acid over time. Fresh-pack pickles use a prepared
        acidic mixture instead; they need not go through fermentation.
      sources:
        - nchfp-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: For preservation, use a research-tested recipe and its stated ingredient proportions, acid strength,
        preparation and processing instructions. Pleasant sourness is not a substitute for those controls.
      sources:
        - umn-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes
      role: mistakes
      text: Do not dilute the vinegar or change the food-to-liquid proportions of a tested canning recipe. A sealed
        lid by itself does not prove that improvised pickles are safe for the cupboard.
      sources:
        - nchfp-pickle
        - umn-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: Choose a method appropriate to the actual fruit or vegetable and intended storage. Keep refrigerator
        methods and shelf-stable canning procedures distinct. This overview does not supply a universal brine.
      sources:
        - umn-pickle
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:

      review_version: 0.1

- target:

  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A blender uses moving blades to combine or purée ingredients. Countertop jugs, personal containers and
        immersion tools suit different quantities and ways of working.
      sources:
        - kitchenaid-blenders
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: selection
      role: selection
      text: Choose for the food and batch size, not power claims alone. An immersion blender works in a suitable
        vessel; a countertop machine has its own jug and capacity limits.
      sources:
        - kitchenaid-blenders
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes
      role: mistakes
      text: Do not assume a sealed personal cup or any ordinary blender is suitable for hot liquid. Check the exact
        model’s temperature, fill and venting instructions before blending soup.
      sources:
        - kitchenaid-use
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: care
      role: care
      text: Disconnect power before handling blades or cleaning parts by hand, and follow the model’s disassembly
        and washing instructions. Dishwasher suitability is not universal.
      sources:
        - kitchenaid-use
        - kitchenaid-clean
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction

  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A pressure cooker holds steam under pressure to cook food. It needs cooking liquid and a properly
        functioning lid, seal and pressure-control system.
      sources:
        - presto-faq
        - presto-use
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: The cooking environment differs from an open saucepan. Establish and maintain pressure as the appliance
        instructions require; the time to reach pressure is distinct from the timed cooking stage.
      sources:
        - presto-use
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: selection
      role: selection
      text: Stovetop and electric models have different controls and operating procedures. Choose a size suited to
        the batch and follow that model’s minimum-liquid and maximum-fill instructions, including special
        limits for expanding foods.
      sources:
        - presto-faq
        - presto-manual
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Use the pressure indicator and release procedure specified for the appliance and recipe. Never force
        open a pressurised cooker. Quick release and natural cooling are not interchangeable for every food.
      sources:
        - presto-use
        - presto-manual
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: care
      role: care
      text: Check and maintain the seal, vent and safety devices according to the manual. A blocked vent or damaged
        component is a reason to stop using the cooker until the problem is corrected.
      sources:
        - presto-use
        - presto-manual
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: "Pressure cooking a meal is not the same as pressure canning. USDA/NCHFP canning schedules are not
        designed for small pressure cookers: vessel size and heating and cooling behaviour affect the
        process."
      sources:
        - nchfp-pressure
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mistakes
      role: mistakes
      text: Do not use an ordinary pressure-cooking programme as proof that sealed jars are safe for shelf storage.
        Use suitable canning equipment and a validated preservation procedure for that separate task.
      sources:
        - nchfp-pressure
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: near-neighbours
      text: A pressure-canner reference describes equipment and a validated jar-processing system. A pressure-cooker
        recipe describes cooking a meal. Similar pressure-related names do not transfer one system’s evidence
        to the other; choose the applicable documentation before treating them as substitutes.
      sources:
        - b2-canners
      review_version: 0.1

      text: Zesting keeps the coloured peel, whereas supreming citrus keeps the flesh and removes peel and segment
        membranes. These preparations use different parts of the fruit and should not be treated as alternate
        names for peeling.
      sources:
        - b3-citrus
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: usu-lemons
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: mash
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Mashing is breaking soft food down by pressing or crushing it.
      sources:
        - purdue-potato
        - oxo-masher
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Cook potatoes until tender before pressing them with a masher. Continue only to the texture required,
        whether pieces remain or the mixture is smoother.
      sources:
        - purdue-potato
        - oxo-masher
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: purdue-potato
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: oxo-masher
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: crush
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Crushing is breaking an ingredient by applying pressure.
      sources:
        - lc-mortar
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It can open spices or break herbs into a rough mixture. A mortar and pestle lets you work from coarse
        fragments towards a finer paste without requiring uniform knife cuts.
      sources:
        - lc-mortar
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: lc-mortar
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: strain
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Straining is passing a mixture through a perforated or mesh barrier to
        separate liquid from larger solids.
      sources:
        - cia-stock
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: uses
      role: uses
      text: For stock, strain the cooked liquid away from the bones and vegetables.
        Choose a finer barrier when smaller particles need to be held back.
      sources:
        - cia-stock
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: cocktail-context
      role: context
      text: In bar service, a primary strainer retains mixing ice. Fine straining adds
        a mesh stage when the spec calls for smaller fragments to be removed.
      sources:
        - cf-fine-strain
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-stock
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: cf-fine-strain
      role: specialist-reference
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: skim
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Skimming is lifting unwanted material from the surface of a liquid.
      sources:
        - cia-stock
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: In stock-making it removes surface foam or fat while retaining the liquid beneath. Work at the surface
        rather than stirring the material back through the stock.
      sources:
        - cia-stock
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-stock
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: fold
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Folding is gently combining mixtures by lifting and turning them together.
      sources:
        - kab-cake-mixing
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: In foam cakes it incorporates ingredients while preserving as much trapped air as possible. Stop once
        evenly combined instead of continuing to beat the mixture.
      sources:
        - kab-cake-mixing
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-3-distinction
      role: context
      text: Folding pastry into layers during lamination is a different context from gently folding a foam mixture.
        A recipe must supply that context; repeated pastry folds are not an instruction to beat or stir a
        foam.
      sources:
        - b2-laminate
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-cake-mixing
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: boil
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Boiling is heating a liquid until bubbles form throughout it and break vigorously at the surface.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It provides active moist heat for ingredients that can tolerate movement in the liquid.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: A rolling boil is more turbulent than a simmer. Delicate food may need gentler cooking even after the
        liquid has first been brought to the boil.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Boiling food immerses it in hot liquid; steaming exposes it to vapour above liquid. These are different
        heat-transfer arrangements even when both begin with boiling water. A steamer basket therefore does
        not make its contents boiled food.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-moist-heat
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: steam
      note: Boiling food immerses it in hot liquid; steaming exposes it to vapour above liquid. These are different
        heat-transfer arrangements even when both begin with boiling water. A steamer basket therefore does
        not make its contents boiled food.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: simmer
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Simmering is cooking in liquid held below a full boil, with gentle bubbling.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It cooks food with less agitation than boiling, useful for stocks and slow-cooked dishes.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Watch the liquid, not just the hob setting. Reduce the heat if the pan develops a vigorous rolling boil.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: context
      text: A simmer describes the liquid’s activity, while reduction describes losing liquid through evaporation. A
        covered simmer can cook food without the same reduction as an uncovered pan. State the desired
        consistency separately when a sauce must also concentrate.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-moist-heat
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: poach
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Poaching is cooking food gently in liquid below a full simmer.
      sources:
        - cia-poaching
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: The food may be partly or fully submerged. Keep the liquid gentle and use a pan that holds the portions
        without crowding.
      sources:
        - cia-poaching
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Fish and other delicate portions can break up under vigorous bubbling. Monitor the liquid and the food
        separately; the right liquid temperature does not alone establish that the centre is cooked.
      sources:
        - cia-poaching
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: uses
      text: Deep poaching fully surrounds the food with cooking liquid. The liquid can contribute flavour through
        stock, aromatics or wine, while a serving sauce may be prepared separately. Poaching does not require
        turning all of the cooking liquid into the final sauce.
      sources:
        - cia-poaching
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-poaching
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: steam
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Steaming is cooking food with steam rather than immersing it in the cooking water.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Hold the food above the liquid and cover the vessel so steam surrounds it.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Check the water supply during longer cooking so the vessel does not boil dry. The food’s size and
        arrangement affect how evenly it cooks.
      sources:
        - cia-moist-heat
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-4-distinction
      role: context
      text: A covered bamboo basket is one equipment arrangement for steaming. Its slatted base admits steam while
        holding the food; the basket is not immersed like the food in a pot of boiling water.
      sources:
        - b4-bamboo
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-moist-heat
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: stew
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Stewing is slow cooking of food in liquid, commonly with small pieces largely submerged.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It softens suitable ingredients while producing a cooking liquid served with them.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Keep the covered pan at a gentle simmer and judge tenderness before finishing the sauce.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-techniques
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: bake
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Baking is cooking food in an oven’s enclosed heat.
      sources:
        - kab-success
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It sets the structure of batters and doughs and can dry or brown their surfaces.
      sources:
        - kab-success
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: "Preheat as directed and use the specified pan size. Timing is a guide: combine the recipe’s colour,
        texture and doneness cues rather than assuming every oven finishes identically."
      sources:
        - kab-success
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-4-distinction
      role: context
      text: A cake’s surface colour, spring and interior crumb provide different cues. Inserting a tester inspects a
        small part of the crumb; read that result with the recipe’s other cues rather than treating one clean
        probe as a universal endpoint for every baked food.
      sources:
        - b4-test-cake
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-success
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: saute
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Sautéing is cooking food fairly quickly in a small amount of fat over relatively high heat.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It cooks and browns suitably sized pieces.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Leave space in the pan. Crowding releases enough moisture to hinder browning; cook batches when
        necessary.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-techniques
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: shallow-fry
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Shallow-frying is cooking food in a layer of hot fat that only partly submerges it.
      sources:
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Turn the food so each side contacts the oil. Keep similarly sized pieces together for more even cooking.
      sources:
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Adding too much food cools the oil and hinders browning. Leave space between pieces and use a suitable
        thermometer to monitor the oil.
      sources:
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-frying
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: deep-fry
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Deep-frying is cooking food submerged in hot fat.
      sources:
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: The oil surrounds the food, so the vessel needs room for both the food and bubbling oil. Do not fill it
        close to the rim.
      sources:
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Cook in batches to limit temperature drops and remove loose crumbs before they burn. Use equipment
        suitable for hot oil and monitor its temperature.
      sources:
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-frying
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: stir-fry
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Stir-frying is quickly cooking small pieces in a little oil while moving them around a hot pan.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Prepare everything first and add ingredients in an order that suits their cooking times.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Uniformly cut pieces cook more evenly; crowded batches can steam instead of frying.
      sources:
        - cia-techniques
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-4-distinction
      role: context
      text: Velveting can prepare a protein before the final stir-fry. The initial treatment and the later mixing
        with vegetables or sauce are separate stages; a finished stir-fry need not obtain all of its texture
        from the final toss in the wok.
      sources:
        - b4-velvet
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-techniques
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: knead
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Kneading is repeatedly working dough by pressing, folding or stretching it.
      sources:
        - kab-kneading
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: In wheat bread dough it develops a structure able to stretch and hold gas.
      sources:
        - kab-windowpane
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: A small piece that stretches thinly without tearing can indicate developed gluten. The windowpane test
        is useful for many doughs, but the desired development still depends on the recipe.
      sources:
        - kab-windowpane
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Kneading develops a dough’s structure; pastry lamination preserves distinct layers of dough and fat
        through rolling and folding. Both involve working dough, but continuous mixing is not a substitute for
        the layer-building operation.
      sources:
        - b2-laminate
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-5-distinction
      role: context
      text: Fraisage briefly smears pastry to bring its ingredients together. It should not be treated as a request
        for the sustained kneading used to develop a bread dough’s elasticity.
      sources:
        - b5-fraisage
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-kneading
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: kab-windowpane
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: laminate
      note: Kneading develops a dough’s structure; pastry lamination preserves distinct layers of dough and fat
        through rolling and folding. Both involve working dough, but continuous mixing is not a substitute for
        the layer-building operation.
      sources:
        - b2-laminate
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: prove
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Proving is allowing yeast dough to rise before baking.
      sources:
        - kab-prove
        - kab-yeast-guide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Fermentation produces gas while the dough rests. The recipe may distinguish an initial rise from the
        final rise after shaping.
      sources:
        - kab-prove
        - kab-yeast-guide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Look for the specified expansion and response to a gentle press. Dough temperature changes the timing; a
        clock alone cannot tell whether it is ready.
      sources:
        - kab-prove
        - kab-yeast-guide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-6-distinction
      role: context
      text: A couche supports shaped baguettes during the final rise and is followed by transfer to a baking
        surface. Supporting the dough during proofing is a separate function from containing it during baking.
      sources:
        - b6-couche
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-prove
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: kab-yeast-guide
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: cream
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Creaming is beating softened fat and sugar together in baking.
      sources:
        - kab-cream-method
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It incorporates air and distributes the sugar before other ingredients are added.
      sources:
        - kab-cream-method
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Look for the lighter, aerated texture described in the recipe. Melted butter cannot hold that structure
        in the same way, so melting is not equivalent to softening.
      sources:
        - kab-cream-method
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-cream-method
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: whip
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Whipping is beating a mixture to incorporate air and form a foam.
      sources:
        - kab-whip
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It increases volume and creates a lighter texture, as in whipped cream or egg whites.
      sources:
        - kab-whip
        - egg-foam
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: "Soft peaks bend; firmer peaks hold their shape more clearly. Stop at the stage the recipe requests:
        continuing to whip cream can make it grainy and eventually separate it."
      sources:
        - kab-whip
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-5-distinction
      role: context
      text: Ribbon stage describes an egg mixture falling in trails that linger briefly on its surface. It is not
        the same visual test as peaks formed by whipped whites or cream.
      sources:
        - b5-ribbon
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-6-distinction
      role: context
      text: French, Swiss and Italian meringues all use whipping, but place sugar and heat into the sequence
        differently. Whipping alone does not specify which meringue method is intended.
      sources:
        - b6-meringue
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-whip
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: blind-bake
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Blind-baking is baking a pastry case before adding its filling.
      sources:
        - kab-blind-bake
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It cooks or partly cooks a crust that would otherwise remain underdone beneath a filling.
      sources:
        - kab-blind-bake
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Line and weight the case when the method calls for it, then remove the weights to finish drying the
        base. A case for an uncooked filling needs a different endpoint from one that will return to the oven.
      sources:
        - kab-blind-bake
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Docking controls puffing by making small holes; blind-baking cooks an empty pastry case. They can occur
        together, but one is a preparation and the other a baking stage. Docking a crust does not mean that it
        has already been blind-baked.
      sources:
        - b2-dock
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-4-distinction
      role: context
      text: Par-baking also applies to foods such as bread rolls. Blind-baking describes the absence of the eventual
        filling, while par-baking describes an incomplete bake; an empty crust may be either partly or fully
        baked.
      sources:
        - b4-parbake
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-5-distinction
      role: context
      text: Weights need to support the pastry sides as well as restrain the base. A small pile in the middle can
        leave the walls free to slump; docking and weighting perform different jobs.
      sources:
        - b5-weights
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-blind-bake
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: dock
      note: Docking controls puffing by making small holes; blind-baking cooks an empty pastry case. They can occur
        together, but one is a preparation and the other a baking stage. Docking a crust does not mean that it
        has already been blind-baked.
      sources:
        - b2-dock
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: deglaze
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Deglazing is adding liquid to a cooked-in pan to loosen browned deposits.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It carries those deposits into a sauce or braising liquid.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Browned deposits contribute flavour; burned residues can make the result bitter. Judge the pan before
        adding the liquid rather than treating every dark patch as desirable.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-sear
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: reduce
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Reducing is cooking a liquid so evaporation decreases its volume.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It concentrates flavour and may thicken a sauce.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Cook uncovered when evaporation is wanted. Stop at the recipe’s consistency or volume cue; continuing
        can make a sauce too concentrated or thick.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Adding a thickener and evaporating water can both change consistency, but they do not do the same work.
        Reduction removes liquid rather than adding body to it. A recipe’s target volume and its texture cue
        should therefore be read together.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-5-distinction
      role: context
      text: "A roux thickens through cooked flour, whereas reduction concentrates liquid by evaporation. Choosing
        one does not silently authorise the other: reducing a sauce also changes its concentration."
      sources:
        - b5-roux
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-7-distinction
      role: context
      text: Adding a starch slurry thickens by introducing starch rather than by evaporating more liquid. A recipe
        may use either or both; a thickened sauce is not evidence that it has been reduced.
      sources:
        - b7-slurry
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-reduce
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: thicken
      note: Adding a thickener and evaporating water can both change consistency, but they do not do the same work.
        Reduction removes liquid rather than adding body to it. A recipe’s target volume and its texture cue
        should therefore be read together.
      sources:
        - cia-reduce
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: caramelise
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Caramelising is browning sugars through heating.
      sources:
        - caramelisation
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It develops colour and flavours ranging from gentle caramel to darker, more bitter notes.
      sources:
        - caramelisation
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: For caramel, the wet method starts with sugar and liquid; the dry method starts with sugar alone. The
        added water must evaporate before a wet caramel can brown substantially.
      sources:
        - kab-caramel
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Watch the changing colour closely as the syrup darkens. Have the next ingredients ready before starting,
        because a caramel can move past the wanted stage quickly.
      sources:
        - kab-caramel
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: near-neighbours
      role: near-neighbours
      text: Browning meat is principally associated with Maillard reactions, involving sugars and amino compounds.
        That is different from caramelising sugar, even though recipes sometimes use the same word loosely.
      sources:
        - cia-sear
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: process
    id: confit
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Confit, in the traditional duck preparation, is salt-curing followed by slow cooking under fat.
      sources:
        - cia-confit
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It makes the meat tender and provides a preparation that can later be reheated or crisped.
      sources:
        - cia-confit
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Cure the meat under refrigeration, then cook it gently in sufficient fat according to a reliable recipe.
        The fat should not be treated like a deep-frying bath.
      sources:
        - cia-confit
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Tender meat and crisp skin are separate goals. The slow cooking develops tenderness; a later pan or oven
        step can crisp the skin.
      sources:
        - cia-confit
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: The name has preservation origins, but a layer of fat does not make an arbitrary home preparation
        shelf-stable. The linked duck method uses refrigeration; do not infer room-temperature storage from
        the word confit.
      sources:
        - cia-confit
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-confit
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: deep-fry
      note: Both use fat, but traditional duck confit uses much gentler cooking.
      sources:
        - cia-confit
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: brine
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Brining is treating food with salt in a water solution; dry-brining applies salt directly.
      sources:
        - fsis-brine
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: For poultry, it seasons the meat and can reduce moisture loss during cooking.
      sources:
        - fsis-brine
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Salt affects muscle proteins and the way they retain water. In dry-brining, moisture drawn from the meat
        forms a brine at the surface.
      sources:
        - fsis-brine
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Use a recipe matched to the food and its size. Already salted or enhanced poultry needs particular
        attention to the label before adding more salt.
      sources:
        - fsis-brine
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: Keep poultry refrigerated during brining and cook it afterwards. Brining for a roast is not, by itself,
        a preservation or pathogen-killing process.
      sources:
        - fsis-brine
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: fsis-brine
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: smoke
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Smoking is exposing food to smoke from burning or smouldering material as part of its preparation.
      sources:
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It adds smoke flavour; in hot-smoking, heat also cooks the food.
      sources:
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: A smoker must control cooking heat as well as smoke. The chamber temperature and the food’s internal
        temperature answer different questions.
      sources:
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Use thermometers to check both the smoker and the food. Smoke colour or elapsed time cannot establish
        that meat or poultry has reached a safe internal temperature.
      sources:
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: The linked USDA guidance concerns cooking meat and poultry by hot-smoking. It does not validate a
        cold-smoking process, curing formula or room-temperature storage method.
      sources:
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: fsis-smoke
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: commonly-used-with
      target:
        kind: equipment
        id: thermometer
      note: Monitor the cooking environment and the food’s interior separately.
      sources:
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: sous-vide
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Sous-vide is cooking food in a sealed pouch within a controlled-temperature bath.
      sources:
        - baldwin-sous-vide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It allows close control of the food’s temperature and texture, with time adjusted to the particular food
        and portion.
      sources:
        - baldwin-sous-vide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: Heat must reach the centre before a holding period can have its intended effect. Thickness, starting
        temperature and the bath temperature therefore matter together.
      sources:
        - baldwin-sous-vide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Use a validated time-and-temperature process for the food. Reaching the bath’s set temperature is not
        the same as completing a pasteurisation schedule.
      sources:
        - baldwin-sous-vide
        - nsw-sous-vide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: Serving immediately and chilling for later use are different workflows. Sealing a pouch does not
        sterilise its contents; cooling and storage need their own controls.
      sources:
        - nsw-sous-vide
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: uses
      role: uses
      text: A brief final sear can add surface browning after the controlled bath. That finishing step should not be
        confused with the preceding cooking or safety process.
      sources:
        - baldwin-sous-vide
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: baldwin-sous-vide
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: nsw-sous-vide
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: temper-chocolate
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Tempering chocolate is controlling the crystallisation of its cocoa butter through temperature and
        handling.
      sources:
        - callebaut-temper
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It helps chocolate set with a firm, glossy finish and release cleanly from moulds.
      sources:
        - callebaut-temper
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: The chocolate is melted, cooled to encourage suitable crystals, then brought to its working condition.
        Different methods achieve this sequence in different ways.
      sources:
        - callebaut-temper
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: selection
      role: selection
      text: Use the curve for the chocolate being worked. Dark, milk, white and other formulations do not all share
        one temperature schedule.
      sources:
        - callebaut-temper
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Test a small sample before coating or moulding the full batch. Keep the working chocolate within its
        specified range; overheating can undo the crystal structure just established.
      sources:
        - callebaut-temper
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-6-distinction
      role: context
      text: Tabling cools and moves part of the chocolate on a worktop before recombining it. Seeding instead
        introduces already crystallised chocolate. These are method choices within tempering, not aliases for
        simply melting chocolate.
      sources:
        - b6-table
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: callebaut-temper
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: grill
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Grilling is cooking food with strong radiant heat, commonly over a heated grate.
      sources:
        - weber-zones
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: Direct heat can brown the surface quickly, especially on smaller, naturally tender portions.
      sources:
        - weber-zones
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: With direct grilling, food sits above the heat source. An adjacent indirect zone lets thicker pieces
        continue cooking with less intense surface heat.
      sources:
        - weber-zones
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Move food away from direct heat if the outside is browning faster than the centre cooks. A two-zone
        arrangement makes that adjustment possible without stopping the cooking.
      sources:
        - weber-zones
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: On charcoal equipment, fuel and airflow affect heat. Use the appliance’s vent guidance rather than
        treating one fixed vent position as suitable for every grill.
      sources:
        - weber-charcoal
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: weber-zones
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: weber-charcoal
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: barbecue
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Barbecuing is cooking on barbecue equipment, using direct or indirect heat according to the method.
      sources:
        - weber-charcoal
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: purpose
      role: purpose
      text: It can produce quick surface browning or slower cooking with smoke flavour. The intended result
        determines the fire arrangement.
      sources:
        - weber-zones
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: mechanism
      role: mechanism
      text: For indirect cooking, place the food away from the fire or active burners. A closed cooking chamber
        allows heat to circulate around it.
      sources:
        - weber-charcoal
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Manage airflow and fuel on a charcoal barbecue, and check the food’s temperature separately from the
        cooker’s. A dark exterior does not prove the centre is ready.
      sources:
        - weber-charcoal
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
      role: context
      text: "Usage varies: Weber’s UK guidance uses barbecue for several outdoor methods, while low-and-slow smoked
        meat is another common application. Follow the actual heat arrangement in a recipe rather than relying
        on the name alone."
      sources:
        - weber-charcoal
        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:

      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: weber-zones
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1

      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 3
      review_version: 0.1

      text: Instant-read probes, leave-in probes and appliance thermometers have different jobs. A thermometer
        suitable for checking food briefly is not automatically safe to leave in an oven.
      sources:
        - fsis-thermometers
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: judgement
      role: judgement
      text: Place the sensing area where the reading is needed, following the instrument’s instructions. A shallow
        insertion can miss the centre, while contact with bone or the pan can distort a food reading.
      sources:
        - fsis-thermometers
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-2-distinction
      role: context
      text: The measurement location matters as much as the display. An appliance thermometer describes the
        surrounding cooking environment; a food probe describes the region around its sensing area. These
        readings answer different questions, so an oven reading does not replace a measurement within the
        food.
      sources:
        - fsis-thermometers
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: batch-4-distinction
      role: context
      text: A stem thermometer may sense along a length of probe rather than only at its tip. The displayed number
        can therefore represent a region of food; follow the instrument’s sensing-area guidance instead of
        assuming that touching a point measures only that point.
      sources:
        - fsis-thermometers
      review_version: 0.1

      role: uses
      text: It suits braises, stews and oven cooking where a covered vessel is useful. Its substantial body retains
        heat after the heat source is reduced.

    - id: selection
      role: selection
      text: Bare seasoned iron and enamel-coated iron need different care. Dark interiors can be enamel too, so

      text: For Lodge enamel, heat gradually and avoid heating the pot empty on the hob. Protect the coating from
        harsh abrasion and sudden temperature changes.

      review_version: 0.1
    - id: context
