      text: A cover fitted over a cooking vessel. Covering can retain moisture during cooking; a glass lid also
        allows the contents to be observed without lifting it.
      sources: &a4
        - ep1-lid
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: A lid changes how a pan is used, including covered braising or poaching. Fit and heat compatibility
        belong to the particular lid and its handles; a cover is not automatically oven-safe or a
        pressure-cooking seal.
      sources: *a4
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-lid
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: container
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A receptacle for holding food; the intended use determines the suitable material and closure. For
        freezing, rigid containers and flexible packaging have different practical advantages.
      sources: &a5
        - nchfp-freezer-containers
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Freezer packaging needs resistance to moisture loss and low-temperature damage. Not every glass jar
        is designed for freezing. General container wording therefore does not establish freezer,
        microwave or other heating suitability.
      sources: *a5
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: nchfp-freezer-containers
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: strainer
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A perforated or mesh tool that lets liquid pass while holding back larger solids. Fine-mesh
        examples can rinse small produce or strain foods over another vessel.
      sources: &a6
        - ep1-strainer
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Opening size determines what is retained. A fine strainer and a coarse draining tool may serve
        related purposes but will not separate the same particles. Handles and support loops can help
        position a strainer over a bowl.
      sources: *a6
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-strainer
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: spatula
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Spatula covers several working shapes. A flexible silicone head can scrape a bowl or mix a batter;
        an offset metal blade is especially useful for spreading icing.
      sources: &a7
        - oxo-silicone-spatulas
        - b3-offset
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The offset blade raises the hand away from the working surface, while a flexible scraper follows a
        container wall. Select the shape for the task; the shared name does not make all spatulas
        equivalent in flexibility or heat tolerance.
      sources: *a7
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: oxo-silicone-spatulas
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: b3-offset
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: metal-griddle
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A broad, substantially flat metal cooking surface with very low sides, giving easy access for
        turning pancakes, eggs or sandwiches.
      sources: &a8
        - ep1-griddle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Compared with a skillet, the low edge leaves more room to approach food with a turner but contains
        liquids less readily. Griddles vary in material and heating arrangement; a cast-iron example does
        not establish every griddle's compatibility.
      sources: *a8
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-griddle
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: equipment
        id: frying-pan
      note: Low griddle edges give turning access; a frying pan has more enclosing sidewall.
      sources: *a8
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: baking-pan
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A vessel that supports and contains a bake in the oven. Its dimensions and material are part of the
        baking setup, not merely presentation choices.
      sources: &a9
        - kab-pans
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Metal and glass do not heat and cool identically. Substituting a different material or shape can
        change how the edges and centre bake; use the recipe's pan guidance rather than assuming equal
        capacity guarantees equal results.
      sources: *a9
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-pans
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: stove
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A cooking appliance that supplies heat at a cooktop, using arrangements such as gas burners,
        radiant electric elements or induction.
      sources: &a10
        - ep1-stove
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Induction works with compatible magnetic cookware bases, unlike direct flame or radiant heating.
        The heat source and the vessel must be considered together; the general word stove does not
        identify the burner technology.
      sources: *a10
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-stove
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: mixing-bowl
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: An open bowl used to combine ingredients, whisk eggs or hold a marinade. Its open shape gives
        access for a spoon, whisk or other mixing tool.
      sources: &a11
        - ep1-bowl
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Bowl sets offer different capacities for different tasks. Features such as a non-slip base, handle
        and pouring spout can assist vigorous mixing or transferring batter, but are options rather than
        requirements of a mixing bowl.
      sources: *a11
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-bowl
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: microwave-oven
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: An appliance used to heat and cook food with microwave energy. Heating can be uneven, so stirring
        or rotating food and following the recipe's standing instructions can matter.
      sources: &a12
        - fsis-microwave-wrap
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Use containers identified as suitable for microwave use and follow the appliance instructions.
        Power and food arrangement affect results; a setting or time from one preparation does not
        establish a universal cooking schedule.
      sources: *a12
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: fsis-microwave-wrap
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: work-surface
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: The area where a preparation is carried out. Knife work benefits from an organised layout for uncut
        food, prepared pieces and trimmings; pastry rolling needs a surface suited to dough.
      sources: &a13
        - cia-knives
        - ep1-pie
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "A floured surface or rolling mat can help manage pastry sticking. The term names a working area
        rather than specifying one material or tool: use the preparation method to choose the appropriate
        surface."
      sources: *a13
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-knives
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep1-pie
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: hotplate
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A compact countertop heat source used beneath a cooking vessel. A single electric burner is one
        example, with a heated plate and adjustable control.
      sources: &a14
        - ep1-hotplate
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: This heats a pan or pot rather than providing the exposed food-contact surface of a griddle.
        Designs vary, so vessel compatibility and operating limits must come from the particular
        appliance rather than the general name.
      sources: *a14
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-hotplate
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: equipment
        id: metal-griddle
      note: The burner supports a separate vessel; a griddle provides the food-contact surface.
      sources: *a14
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: meat-tenderizer
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A hand tool used to pound meat. A two-faced example provides a flat face for flattening and a
        textured face for mechanical tenderizing.
      sources: &a15
        - oxo-meat-tenderizer
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Flattening changes thickness; the textured face works the meat surface differently. Choose the face
        for the intended task. This equipment entry does not refer to an added tenderizing ingredient or
        imply that every tenderizer has the same construction.
      sources: *a15
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: oxo-meat-tenderizer
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: cook
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Apply heat to food using an appropriate cooking method. Moist-heat methods use water, another
        liquid or steam; dry-heat methods include heating in air or fat.
      sources: &a16
        - ep1-cook
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The broad instruction cook does not by itself choose boiling, steaming, roasting or frying. The
        surrounding recipe must supply the method and desired result; these methods expose food to heat
        in different ways.
      sources: *a16
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-cook
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: mix
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Bring ingredients together into a mixture. In baking, how and when they are combined can matter as
        much as whether the ingredients are distributed.
      sources: &a17
        - kab-cake-mixing
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Creaming butter and sugar can incorporate air, while folding flour into a foam aims to preserve air
        already present. A general mix instruction should not be taken as permission to substitute
        vigorous beating for a specified gentler method.
      sources: *a17
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-cake-mixing
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: cut
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "Divide food with a cutting tool. More specific instructions describe the intended pieces: dice
        makes cubes, mince makes much smaller pieces, while chopping allows less regular shapes."
      sources: &a18
        - cia-knives
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Relatively consistent pieces help food cook at a similar rate. Match the tool and cut to the
        ingredient and intended result; cut alone does not specify the size or shape of the finished
        pieces.
      sources: *a18
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-knives
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: season
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Add ingredients to bring out or adjust a preparation's flavour. Salt and pepper are common, but
        herbs, spices, aromatics, oils, acids and other condiments can also form a seasoning.
      sources: &a19
        - ep1-season
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The appropriate combination depends on the dish. Season describes a flavouring purpose rather than
        one fixed ingredient or quantity; it should not automatically be read as add salt or as a
        separate cooking method.
      sources: *a19
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-season
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: rest
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Leave a preparation undisturbed for a specified purpose. In pastry dough, resting can allow gluten
        to relax, making the dough easier to handle.
      sources: &a20
        - ep1-pie
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Rest and chill can happen together but describe different things: a pause allows time-dependent
        changes, while cooling also firms pastry fat. Rest does not by itself specify refrigeration or
        mean that a dough is undergoing a yeast rise."
      sources: *a20
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-pie
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: chill
      note: Rest describes a pause; chilling describes a temperature change.
      sources: *a20
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: fry
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Cook food using hot fat as the cooking medium. Pan-frying and deep-frying differ in how much of the
        food is surrounded by the fat.
      sources: &a21
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Crowding can lower the fat temperature and hinder the intended crisp result. Follow the specified
        frying method and load rather than treating every fry instruction as full immersion; draining on
        a rack can help avoid trapping steam beneath fried food.
      sources: *a21
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-frying
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: roll
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Shape by rolling, with the intended form supplied by the recipe. Dough can be rolled under the
        hands into a rope, or a filled sheet can be rolled up into a log.
      sources: &a22
        - ep1-bagel
        - ep1-babka
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: These are different shaping operations from rolling out a sheet to a specified thickness. Look for
        the stated shape and direction rather than assuming every roll instruction calls for a rolling
        pin.
      sources: *a22
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-bagel
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep1-babka
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: roll-out
      note: Rolling a rope or log differs from flattening dough into a sheet.
      sources: *a22
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: soak
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Leave food in a liquid so it can take up moisture. With dried beans, soaking begins rehydration
        before the subsequent cooking stage.
      sources: &a23
        - ep1-soak
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Soaking is not the same operation as cooking the beans. Methods differ, so use the instructions
        appropriate to the ingredient; the word soak alone does not provide a universal duration or
        establish that the food is ready to eat.
      sources: *a23
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-soak
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: chill
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Lower a preparation's temperature. In cookie dough, chilling firms the fat and can reduce spreading
        during baking.
      sources: &a24
        - ep1-chill
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The example concerns cookie dough, not every food. A resting period can also change dough
        independently of temperature; chill identifies the cooling goal and does not itself supply a
        storage-life or preservation instruction.
      sources: *a24
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-chill
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: rest
      note: Cooling and time at rest can affect dough in different ways.
      sources: *a24
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: roll-out
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Flatten dough into a sheet with a rolling pin, aiming for the thickness and dimensions needed by
        the recipe.
      sources: &a25
        - ep1-pie
        - ep1-babka
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Pastry that springs back may need a rest before more rolling. A lightly floured surface or rolling
        mat helps manage sticking. Rolling out changes a sheet's dimensions; rolling it up into a filled
        log is a separate shaping step.
      sources: *a25
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-pie
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep1-babka
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: roll
      note: A sheet-forming operation is distinct from rolling that sheet into a log.
      sources: *a25
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: juice
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Extract liquid from fruit. For citrus, pressing the cut fruit against a reamer releases juice; a
        built-in strainer can catch seeds and larger pulp.
      sources: &a26
        - ep1-juice
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Extraction and straining are separate functions even when one tool performs both. The desired
        amount of pulp determines whether further straining is useful; this action concerns the juice
        rather than removing zest from the peel.
      sources: *a26
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-juice
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: sieve
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Pass material through a mesh. For dry baking ingredients such as flour, cocoa or powdered sugar,
        sifting can break up lumps and loosen the powder.
      sources: &a27
        - ep1-sieve
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: This can help dry ingredients combine with a delicate foam without excessive mixing. Whisking may
        loosen a powder but does not separate particles through a mesh, so it is not identical to sieving
        when lumps must be removed.
      sources: *a27
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-sieve
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pan-fry
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Fry food in a pan with fat reaching only partway up the food, turning as needed to cook the other
        side.
      sources: &a28
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Unlike deep-frying, the food is not surrounded by fat throughout. Batch size matters because adding
        too much food can cool the fat; follow the recipe's method rather than treating pan-frying and
        deep-frying as interchangeable.
      sources: *a28
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-frying
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: deep-fry
      note: Partial fat immersion differs from surrounding food with fat.
      sources: *a28
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: thicken
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Increase the body or consistency of a liquid preparation. Culinary liaisons can use flour, starch
        or other ingredients such as egg yolk and cream.
      sources: &a29
        - b7-slurry
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: These approaches are not one interchangeable technique. A starch dispersed in cold liquid before
        adding it to a hot preparation is different from an egg-based liaison; follow the method
        appropriate to the thickener rather than just adding any available powder.
      sources: *a29
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: b7-slurry
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: scramble
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Cook beaten eggs while moving the setting mixture with a utensil, drawing and folding it into
        curds.
      sources: &a30
        - ep1-scramble
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Beating combines the raw egg; scrambling also involves heat and the movement of the setting egg.
        The size and texture of the curds depend on that handling, so an instruction to beat eggs alone
        does not describe scrambling.
      sources: *a30
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-scramble
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: beat
      note: Beating combines raw egg; scrambling forms curds during heating.
      sources: *a30
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: plate
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A shallow piece of tableware for presenting individual portions. Side plates suit smaller servings
        or sandwiches, while deeper plate forms can hold saucier foods.
      sources: &a1
        - ep2-plate
        - ep2-soup-plate
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Consider the usable surface and depth, not just the outside diameter. A broad rim reduces the
        central serving area, and a flat plate contains liquid differently from a soup plate. Materials
        and sizes vary; plate alone does not specify bakeware.
      sources: *a1
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-plate
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep2-soup-plate
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: equipment
        id: soup-plate
      note: A soup plate provides a deeper central well for liquid-containing foods.
      sources: *a1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: dish
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "A broad term for a vessel used to hold, prepare or present food. A baking dish is one particular
        form: its sides contain layered mixtures and liquids during oven cooking."
      sources: &a2
        - ep2-dish
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Some purpose-made baking dishes also serve for marinating, breading or taking a bake to the table.
        Those capabilities belong to the particular vessel. The unqualified word dish does not tell you
        its depth, capacity or compatibility with direct heat.
      sources: *a2
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-dish
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: jar
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "A container with an opening that can be closed with a lid. The mouth affects access: wide-mouth
        canning jars are easier to fill and empty than narrower examples."
      sources: &a3
        - ep2-jars
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Closure design matters independently of capacity. A screw band, lid and sealing surface work
        together on a purpose-made canning jar; an ordinary storage jar is not evidence of suitability
        for a heat-processing recipe.
      sources: *a3
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-jars
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: cloth
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A flexible fabric used as a preparation aid. In strudel making, a cloth spread over the work area
        supports the thin dough and can help lift and roll it around the filling.
      sources: &a4
        - ep2-cloth
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "This use relies on a broad flexible support rather than a rigid board. Other food-contact tasks
        require different fabric properties: a cloth used to guide dough is not automatically a fine
        straining cloth. Choose it for the operation described."
      sources: *a4
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-cloth
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: baking-mold
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A baking vessel whose cavity gives the bake its form. A shaped cake pan illustrates how the
        finished surface follows the details of the mold.
      sources: &a5
        - ep2-mold
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Release is part of the preparation: grease or otherwise prepare the cavity as directed for that
        recipe and material. Intricate shapes need attention to recesses, and batter needs room to
        expand. Do not assume a non-stick surface removes every preparation step."
      sources: *a5
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-mold
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: squeeze-bottle
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A squeezable container that dispenses liquid through a tip, allowing one-handed application.
        Typical uses include adding oil to a pan or drawing sauce lines over a finished dish.
      sources: &a6
        - ep2-squeeze
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The tip controls the stream; a fine tip favours a narrow drizzle. The cited bottle has an attached
        cap, but closures and materials vary. Dispensing convenience does not establish suitability for
        heating the bottle or for long-term storage.
      sources: *a6
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-squeeze
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: gridiron
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: An open framework of metal bars used to support food over heat. Historical hearth examples held
        meat or fish above hot coals.
      sources: &a7
        - ep2-gridiron
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Gaps between the bars distinguish it from a solid griddle surface. Food rests on the bars rather
        than on a continuous plate; a museum example documents this construction without making every
        gridiron a complete barbecue appliance.
      sources: *a7
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-gridiron
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: equipment
        id: metal-griddle
      note: An open barred surface differs from a continuous cooking plate.
      sources: *a7
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: cup
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A small open vessel for drinking or holding a portion. Coffee and tea cups are sold in different
        capacities, sometimes with matching saucers.
      sources: &a8
        - ep2-cup
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "A cup chosen for serving is not necessarily a measuring cup. Its capacity belongs to that vessel:
        the equipment name cannot establish a standard recipe volume or a conversion basis for a quantity
        written in cups."
      sources: *a8
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-cup
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: soup-plate
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A deep plate whose recessed centre can hold soup or other foods with liquid. It sits between a flat
        plate and a bowl in serving form.
      sources: &a9
        - ep2-soup-plate
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The depth is useful for saucy dishes as well as soup, but capacity still varies by design. A recipe
        using a soup plate names a vessel shape; it does not establish a standard portion size or show
        that a modern example can go in the oven.
      sources: *a9
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-soup-plate
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: clay-casserole
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A casserole vessel made from clay-based ceramic, used for preparations such as stews or oven bakes
        when the vessel is designed for that heat source.
      sources: &a10
        - ep2-clay
        - ep2-dish
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Ceramic cookware is not one compatibility class. The cited Emile Henry stewpot has its own
        gradual-heating instructions, while Le Creuset stoneware baking dishes exclude stovetop use.
        Follow the particular vessel instructions rather than assuming clay means flame-safe; sudden
        temperature changes also need care.
      sources: *a10
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-clay
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep2-dish
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: glass-jars
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Glass containers with closable mouths, used to hold food. For home canning, purpose-made threaded
        jars and compatible lids provide a defined sealing arrangement.
      sources: &a11
        - ep2-jars
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Check the jar as well as its closure. Scratches or damaged sealing surfaces can matter during
        processing, and washing an empty jar does not itself sterilize it. This material description is
        not a canning schedule or proof that a reused commercial jar is suitable.
      sources: *a11
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-jars
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: tray
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A broad, relatively shallow support used to gather, carry or arrange items. Serving trays may have
        handles to help move several items together.
      sources: &a12
        - ep2-tray
        - ep2-mold
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: A carrying tray and a baking sheet share a broad shape but differ in intended use. Where a recipe
        puts a tray in the oven, select an oven-suitable baking tray; a serving tray with coated surfaces
        or wooden handles does not establish that capability.
      sources: *a12
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-tray
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep2-mold
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: teaspoon
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A small spoon used for stirring tea or coffee and for handling small portions, including desserts.
        It is a table utensil with a bowl and handle.
      sources: &a13
        - ep2-teaspoon
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Its shape gives access to a cup or a small amount of food. Here teaspoon identifies equipment, not
        a calibrated measuring spoon: the name alone does not make a spoonful an exact recipe quantity."
      sources: *a13
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-teaspoon
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: equipment
        id: measuring-spoon
      note: A small table utensil does not establish calibrated capacity.
      sources: *a13
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: platter
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A broad serving dish used to present food for sharing. Some designs include a separate central
        space for dip surrounded by room for vegetables, cheese or other small foods.
      sources: &a14
        - ep2-platter
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Choose the arrangement for the food being served: an uninterrupted surface and a divided dip
        platter do different jobs. Product-specific heat ratings do not make every platter oven-safe, and
        a serving form is not a substitute for a specified baking vessel."
      sources: *a14
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-platter
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: pitcher
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A vessel for holding and pouring drinks into smaller servings. Pitchers can serve a batch of
        lemonade or other mixed drinks rather than one individual portion.
      sources: &a15
        - ep2-pitcher
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Capacity, material and opening affect how it is used. The cited stoneware pitcher is designed for
        hot or cold drinks, but that product capability should not be assumed for every pitcher; check
        the vessel when serving hot liquids.
      sources: *a15
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-pitcher
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: refrigerate
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Place food in a refrigerator to keep it chilled. Refrigeration slows bacterial growth; it is a
        storage condition rather than a cooking or freezing step.
      sources: &a16
        - fda-refrigerator
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Cold air needs room to circulate, so avoid tightly overpacking the appliance. Covered containers
        help keep stored foods separated, and an appliance thermometer checks the actual temperature.
        Follow food-specific storage guidance: the verb refrigerate alone does not specify a safe storage
        life."
      sources: *a16
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: fda-refrigerator
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: press
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Apply pressure to food or a mixture for a stated result. Pressing shortbread dough into a pan
        shapes an even layer; pressing cut tomatoes can release pulp and seeds.
      sources: &a17
        - b2-dock
        - b3-concasse
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The object and direction determine the task. Shaping dough, attaching a coating and forcing food
        through a sieve are not interchangeable instructions. Use the recipe's endpoint rather than
        treating press as a fixed force or a request to puree everything.
      sources: *a17
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: b2-dock
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: b3-concasse
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: turn
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Change which side of a piece of food faces the heat or cooking surface. In frying, turning exposes
        another surface for cooking and browning.
      sources: &a18
        - cia-frying
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Use a suitable utensil to move the piece without unnecessarily piercing its crust. How often to
        turn depends on the method; the handling appropriate to pan-frying is not automatically the same
        as for food immersed in fat.
      sources: *a18
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: cia-frying
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: wash
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Clean the surface of food using an appropriate washing method. For fresh produce, FDA guidance uses
        running water; firm produce can also be rubbed or scrubbed with a clean produce brush.
      sources: &a19
        - ep2-wash
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Produce washing is not sterilization, and soap or detergent is not recommended on fruits and
        vegetables. Ready-to-eat produce labelled as pre-washed can be used without another wash. These
        produce instructions should not be generalized to every food.
      sources: *a19
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-wash
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: seal
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Close an opening or join edges so the contents are held in place. In a hand pie, pressing the
        pastry edges together with a fork helps keep filling from escaping at the seam.
      sources: &a20
        - ep2-seal
        - ep2-jars
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "In storage instructions, seal may instead refer to closing a bag or container. The object
        determines the operation: a pastry seam is not a vacuum seal, and closing a lid does not by
        itself establish a safe preservation process."
      sources: *a20
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-seal
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep2-jars
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: separate
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Divide components so they can be handled independently. Separating an egg keeps the yolk apart from
        the white, allowing each to be used where the recipe needs it.
      sources: &a21
        - ep2-separate
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: An egg separator lets the white pass through while retaining the yolk. Elsewhere the recipe may ask
        to separate cloves or pieces of food; those are different physical tasks. Read what must be
        separated rather than assuming the verb always means egg separation.
      sources: *a21
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-separate
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: wrap
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Enclose food or a preparation in a flexible covering. Pastry disks may be wrapped before chilling
        so they can rest as individual prepared pieces.
      sources: &a22
        - ep1-pie
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The material must suit the next step. A wrapper used while chilling is not automatically suitable
        for baking or other heating. Wrapping also differs from simply laying a loose cover over a bowl;
        follow the recipe's instruction about what is enclosed.
      sources: *a22
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-pie
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pat-dry
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Blot surface moisture with a clean absorbent cloth or paper towel. After washing produce, drying
        removes water remaining on the outside.
      sources: &a23
        - ep2-wash
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Gentle contact targets surface droplets rather than squeezing liquid out of the food or dehydrating
        it throughout. FDA produce guidance specifies a clean cloth or paper towel; reusing a soiled
        cloth defeats that handling step.
      sources: *a23
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-wash
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: slow-cook
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Cook with gentle heat over an extended period. A covered electric slow cooker is one
        implementation, combining heat from the pot with moisture and steam inside the vessel.
      sources: &a24
        - fsis-slow-cooker
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: High and low settings change the cooking rate, and lifting the lid loses heat. Use a recipe and
        loading guidance suited to the appliance; the general instruction slow-cook does not justify an
        arbitrary low setting or a universal duration for every food.
      sources: *a24
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: fsis-slow-cooker
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: skin
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Remove the skin of an ingredient. For tomatoes, brief exposure to hot water followed by rapid
        cooling can loosen the skin so it can be peeled away.
      sources: &a25
        - ep2-skin
        - ep2-fish-preparation
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The method depends on the food: removing skin from a fish is different from loosening tomato skin.
        Descaling removes scales from a fish surface and is a separate operation; skin does not prescribe
        one knife technique for every ingredient."
      sources: *a25
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-skin
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep2-fish-preparation
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: descale
      note: Removing the skin differs from removing scales attached to it.
      sources: *a25
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: descale
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Remove scales from the surface of a fish using a scaler or an appropriate knife action. The scales
        are detached from the skin rather than the whole skin being removed.
      sources: &a26
        - ep2-descale
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Descaling is one preparatory task among others such as trimming fins or gutting. Whether it is
        needed depends on the species and intended preparation; it should not be treated as a synonym for
        filleting or skinning.
      sources: *a26
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-descale
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: skin
      note: Descaling need not remove the skin itself.
      sources: *a26
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: temper-spices
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Heat spices in hot oil or ghee so their flavour passes into the fat. In Indian cooking, the
        flavoured fat may start a dish or be added near the end as a finishing step.
      sources: &a27
        - ep2-spices
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The sequence matters because different spices and aromatics cook at different rates. This is
        distinct from dry-roasting spices, and from tempering chocolate or eggs. Tadka is one relevant
        culinary context, not a universal replacement name for every practice involving spices and fat.
      sources: *a27
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-spices
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: shock
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Cool food rapidly, often immediately after a hot-water or steam treatment. Plunging blanched
        vegetables into cold or ice water interrupts continued cooking.
      sources: &a28
        - nchfp-blanch
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Blanching supplies the heat; shocking supplies the rapid cooling. They can be consecutive steps
        without being the same action. In the cited vegetable-freezing guidance, the vegetables are then
        drained thoroughly; chilling slowly in a refrigerator is a different cooling approach.
      sources: *a28
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: nchfp-blanch
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: blanch
      note: Rapid cooling follows the heat treatment as a distinct step.
      sources: *a28
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: butter
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Apply or incorporate butter as the preparation requires. Buttering a mold coats its surface to help
        release the bake; buttering bread spreads butter onto the food itself.
      sources: &a29
        - ep2-butter
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The object matters. Adding butter to a sauce is different from coating a pan, and a buttered mold
        may still need flour or another lining. Follow the specified preparation rather than assuming
        butter alone makes every bake release cleanly.
      sources: *a29
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-butter
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: flour
      note: A mold may be buttered and then floured; these are separate coatings.
      sources: *a29
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: flour
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Coat or dust a surface with flour. On a buttered baking mold, moving the mold spreads flour over
        the base and sides; tapping removes the excess.
      sources: &a30
        - ep2-flour
        - ep1-pie
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: On a pastry work surface, a light dusting helps control sticking during rolling. Both uses put
        flour on a surface rather than treating it as a measured ingredient to mix in. The amount and
        surface preparation depend on the recipe.
      sources: *a30
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-flour
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep1-pie
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: cauldron
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A substantial cooking pot associated with hearth cooking. Historical examples used legs to stand
        over a fire, handles for suspension, or both. These features supported cooking in a vessel above
        the heat rather than directly on a flat hob.
      sources: &a1
        - ep3-cauldron
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Cauldrons varied in size and use. The cited medieval example explains a hearth arrangement, not a
        universal modern design: the name alone does not establish material, capacity or compatibility
        with an induction hob. Read the recipe and the actual vessel together."
      sources: *a1
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-cauldron
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: bottle
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A container with a relatively narrow opening, commonly used to hold and pour liquids. A stopper or
        cap closes the mouth; the cited swing-top example combines a glass body with a separate seal and
        fastening.
      sources: &a2
        - ep3-bottle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The opening affects filling and access for cleaning. In Corpus, a bottle is also named as a rolling
        aid, but that particular use does not redefine the general container. A closure alone establishes
        neither a measuring scale nor suitability for cooking.
      sources: *a2
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-bottle
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: serving-bowl
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A bowl used to present food at the table, from salad to shared side dishes. Serving bowls come in
        different sizes and materials; a deep interior contains foods that would spread across a flat
        plate.
      sources: &a3
        - ep3-bowl
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Choose the shape and capacity for the portion being presented. Serving use does not imply oven
        use: the cited glass bowl has its own food-temperature limit. A bowl that looks like a mixing or
        baking bowl need not share its heat tolerance."
      sources: *a3
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-bowl
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: towel
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: An absorbent material used to take up surface moisture. For washed produce, FDA guidance specifies
        a clean cloth or paper towel for drying the outside.
      sources: &a4
        - ep2-wash
        - ep3-squeeze
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Blotting water from a surface is different from wrapping shredded vegetables and squeezing out
        liquid. The unqualified word towel does not specify paper versus fabric or establish heat
        protection; use the material and condition required by the recipe.
      sources: *a4
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-wash
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ep3-squeeze
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: board
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:

      role: summary
      text: A flat support for food preparation. When used for cutting, a board provides a dedicated work

        - b3-boards
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Cleaning and condition matter more than the generic name. USDA guidance separates raw-meat work
        from ready-to-eat preparation and calls for replacing boards with hard-to-clean grooves. Board
        does not itself specify material or prove that every flat serving board suits every preparation
        task.
      sources: *a5
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: b3-boards
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: kitchen-towel
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A towel used for kitchen preparation and drying tasks. A clean fabric towel can gather shredded
        zucchini or cucumber into a bundle so pressure removes excess water while keeping the pieces
        together.
      sources: &a6
        - ep3-squeeze
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "This is more than patting the outside dry: liquid is pressed out of the vegetable mass. The cited
        technique uses a clean dish towel. Match the towel to the task rather than assuming a cloth used
        for wiping surfaces is ready for direct food contact."
      sources: *a6
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-squeeze
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: rubber-band
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: An elastic loop used to hold something in place. One culinary use is securing a clean cloth or
        coffee filter around the mouth of a container.
      sources: &a7
        - ep3-band
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Virginia Cooperative Extension illustrates this fastening in kombucha preparation, where air
        remains available through the cover. The band holds the covering; it is not an airtight lid and
        does not establish a fermentation method, storage life or suitability for heating.
      sources: *a7
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-band
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: glass-bottles
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Bottles with glass bodies, used to hold and serve liquids. A resealable example has a stopper with
        its own seal and fastening; these components are separate from the glass body.
      sources: &a8
        - ep3-bottle
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Follow the specific bottle instructions for filling and temperature changes. Glass plus a tight
        closure does not by itself establish pressure tolerance or suitability for a fermenting drink.
        The existing plural identity describes equipment, not a validated bottling procedure.
      sources: *a8
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-bottle
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: glass-container
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A glass vessel used to contain food during preparation, storage or serving. Some purpose-made food
        containers also allow reheating, but that capability depends on the product.
      sources: &a9
        - ep3-glass
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Check the body and closure separately. The cited container has a heat-resistant glass body and a
        plastic lid: its oven suitability explicitly excludes the lid. The words glass container alone do
        not establish oven, hob or microwave compatibility for the assembled item."
      sources: *a9
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-glass
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: gloves
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Hand coverings selected for a particular kitchen task. In pretzel preparation involving lye, the
        purpose is protection from contact with the chemical, rather than simply keeping food off the
        hands.
      sources: &a10
        - ep3-gloves
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The cited baking guidance calls for gloves alongside eye and skin protection. Gloves is therefore
        incomplete as a safety specification: follow the chemical and protective-equipment instructions
        for the actual task. A generic food-handling glove or oven glove is not evidence of appropriate
        chemical protection."
      sources: *a10
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-gloves
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: razor-blade
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A very thin, sharp blade used in bread making to cut the dough surface before baking. A blade
        mounted in a baker’s lame gives a controlled cutting edge for these incisions.
      sources: &a11
        - ep3-score
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Compared with a thicker kitchen knife, a sharp thin blade can enter the surface with less pressure
        and drag. The cut should serve the loaf’s scoring plan; possessing a razor blade does not
        determine the correct depth, angle or pattern for every dough.
      sources: *a11
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-score
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: used-for
      target:
        kind: process
        id: slash
      note: A sharp thin blade can make a bread-surface incision.
      sources: *a11
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: scissors
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A pair of pivoting blades used to cut by closing them together. Kitchen versions can snip herbs,
        cut food into pieces and trim kitchen twine without working like a knife against a board.
      sources: &a12
        - ep3-scissors
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Features vary: the cited kitchen scissors have micro-serrated edges and blades that separate for
        cleaning. Those details belong to that design, not every pair. General kitchen scissors should
        not be assumed to have the bone-cutting capability of specialised poultry shears."
      sources: *a12
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-scissors
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: soup-pan
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A cooking pan used to prepare soup, holding liquid and solids together while they heat. The recipe
        needs usable capacity for its batch and access for stirring.
      sources: &a13
        - ep3-pot
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Soup vessels are not one standard geometry. A manufacturer’s rounded soup-pot design favours
        stirring around the sides, but soup-pan alone does not prescribe that shape, a particular handle
        arrangement or a material. Select the actual pan for the heat source and quantity in the recipe.
      sources: *a13
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-pot
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: soup-pot
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A pot used for cooking soup and similar liquid-based dishes. Its sides contain broth and
        ingredients; capacity should suit the whole batch rather than just the liquid measure.
      sources: &a14
        - ep3-pot
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Some designs have curved sides that make stirring easier around the bottom. The cited cast-iron
        example is one such form, not a rule that every soup pot is cast iron or a Dutch oven. Material,
        weight, lid and heat-source compatibility still belong to the individual pot.
      sources: *a14
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-pot
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: baking-vessel
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A vessel designed to hold food during baking. For bread, a lidded pot or cloche can retain steam
        released by the dough during the early part of the bake.
      sources: &a15
        - ep3-bake
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Removing the lid later allows the loaf to finish in a drier environment. This technique does not
        make every container suitable for high-temperature baking or empty preheating: material and
        manufacturer instructions matter, particularly for ceramic or enamelled vessels vulnerable to
        thermal shock."
      sources: *a15
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-bake
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: top
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Put an ingredient on the upper surface of a preparation. A drizzle of oil over hummus is a
        finishing example; other recipes add a topping before further cooking.
      sources: &a16
        - ep3-hummus
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The instruction describes placement, not a single application method. Read the named topping and
        the next step to decide whether to sprinkle, spoon or pour it; topping does not mean mixing it
        throughout.
      sources: *a16
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-hummus
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: break
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Divide food into smaller pieces by pressure or disruption. In the Corpus meat-sauce examples,
        breaking up ground meat separates clumps while leaving pieces rather than turning the mixture
        into a paste.
      sources: &a17
        - ep3-break
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "A spoon or an appropriate meat-breaking tool can combine this work with stirring. The desired
        piece size comes from the recipe: break does not automatically mean mince, crumble finely or
        puree, and the same verb can act on ingredients with very different textures."
      sources: *a17
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-break
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: process
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Work ingredients in a food processor to obtain the requested texture. The blade or disc and the way
        the machine runs determine whether the result is chopped, mixed, sliced or shredded.
      sources: &a18
        - ep3-processor
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Short pulses offer opportunities to check progress; continuous running can produce a finer result.
        Follow the equipment instructions and recipe endpoint instead of treating process as a synonym
        for puree. Equally sized starting pieces can help a chopping operation produce a more even
        result.
      sources: *a18
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-processor
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: rub
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Move the hand or a suitable implement over an ingredient’s surface to distribute something across
        it. Rubbing a seasoning mixture onto chicken spreads it over the skin and into irregular areas.
      sources: &a19
        - ep3-rub
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Here the purpose is surface coverage, not soaking the food in a liquid marinade. Elsewhere rub can
        describe a different task, so read what is being rubbed and with what. This action alone does not
        state a resting time or guarantee flavour penetration.
      sources: *a19
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-rub
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: scrape
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Draw a utensil edge along a surface to gather or remove material. Scraping the sides and bottom of
        a mixing bowl brings clinging ingredients back into the mixture.
      sources: &a20
        - ep3-challah
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "This reaches material that ordinary stirring can leave behind. Stop the mixer before working
        around its attachment, as in the cited dough method. Other recipes scrape away an excess coating
        instead of returning it: the object and destination determine whether material is kept or
        discarded."
      sources: *a20
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-challah
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pierce
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Make small holes in a surface with a pointed implement. Pricking shortbread dough with a fork
        allows steam to escape and helps prevent bubbling during baking.
      sources: &a21
        - b2-dock
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: This docking example uses multiple small punctures rather than the longer incision of a slash.
        Other foods and methods may call for different tools or hole patterns; pierce alone does not
        establish how deeply or how often to puncture.
      sources: *a21
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: b2-dock
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: slash
      note: Fork punctures and a longer surface cut serve different patterns.
      sources: *a21
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: oil
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Apply oil to the specified surface. Preparing a crepe pan can involve spreading oil and wiping away
        excess so a thin film remains.
      sources: &a22
        - ep3-oil
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: A surface coating is different from filling a pan with oil for frying. The appropriate amount and
        application depend on the recipe and cookware; oil does not itself mean season the pan
        permanently or convert any surface into non-stick cookware.
      sources: *a22
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-oil
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: space
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Leave gaps between pieces when arranging them. Cookie dough needs room for the individual portions
        to spread without running together during baking.
      sources: &a23
        - ep3-space
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The needed clearance depends on the dough and portion size. A test cookie can show how much that
        particular mixture spreads. Even spacing is a layout instruction, not a universal distance:
        ravioli filling, for example, leaves room for seams rather than cookie expansion."
      sources: *a23
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-space
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: spoon
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Transfer a mixture with a spoon, usually in controlled portions. Cookie dough can be spooned from
        the bowl onto a baking sheet; a scoop is another portioning tool in that example.
      sources: &a24
        - ep3-spoon
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The verb does not specify a measured tablespoon or teaspoon unless the recipe gives one. It
        describes how the mixture is moved, while the required portion size, spacing or filling level
        must come from the surrounding instruction.
      sources: *a24
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-spoon
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: tie
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Fasten ingredients or a wrapper with string or kitchen twine. Tying an aromatic herb bundle keeps
        its components together so they can flavour a liquid and then be removed.
      sources: &a25
        - ep3-tie
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The object determines the purpose: holding a bouquet together is different from shaping a roast.
        Use the recipe’s fastening arrangement rather than assuming one knot, tension or bundle
        composition applies to every instruction to tie."
      sources: *a25
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-tie
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: thin
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Make a mixture less thick by adding the specified liquid. In hummus, small additions of water can
        move a stiff paste toward a spoonable consistency.
      sources: &a26
        - ep3-hummus
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Add gradually and reassess after mixing. Thinning changes how the mixture flows; it is not the same
        as processing away coarse particles. The recipe must identify a suitable liquid and endpoint,
        rather than thin implying water in every dish.
      sources: *a26
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-hummus
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: smooth
      note: Changing flow by adding liquid differs from evening the top surface.
      sources: *a26
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pinch
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Press a small area between the fingers to join or shape it. Pinching the ends of dough ropes
        together anchors them before braiding a challah.
      sources: &a27
        - ep3-challah
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The pressure is local to the join rather than a kneading action applied throughout the dough. In
        this process sense, pinch describes handling; a pinch of salt is a quantity expression and does
        not tell you how to form a dough seam.
      sources: *a27
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-challah
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: slash
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Make an incision in the surface of food. For bread, slashing the dough before baking creates an
        opening that helps direct expansion as the loaf heats.
      sources: &a28
        - ep3-score
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: A sharp blade limits dragging through the dough. Placement, angle and depth depend on the loaf and
        intended result, so a decorative mark and a functional expansion cut need not be identical. This
        is different from piercing many small holes with a fork.
      sources: *a28
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-score
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: pierce
      note: An incision differs from a set of small punctures.
      sources: *a28
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: smooth
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Even out the surface of a preparation. The back of a spoon can shape the top of hummus, reducing
        ridges or making an intentional swirl before finishing.
      sources: &a29
        - ep3-hummus
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Smoothing the surface does not necessarily make the mixture inside finer. Blending a coarse puree
        changes its internal texture; moving a spoon across the top mainly changes its presentation.
        Follow the object named in the recipe.
      sources: *a29
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-hummus
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: lay
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Place something onto a supporting surface in the arrangement required. In Wellington assembly,
        slices of prosciutto are laid onto cling film with slight overlaps to form a layer.
      sources: &a30
        - ep3-lay
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The instruction concerns position: overlap, orientation and coverage come from its context. Laying
        out the layer is separate from wrapping it around the filling, and a temporary support used in
        assembly is not automatically intended to remain during cooking."
      sources: *a30
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-lay
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
  associations:
    - relation: contrast-with
      target:
        kind: process
        id: wrap
      note: Positioning a layer precedes enclosing a filling in it.
      sources: *a30
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: beater
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "A mixing tool or attachment that moves through ingredients to combine them. The broad name does

    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: KitchenAid distinguishes flat-beater mixing from wire-whip aeration. Select the attachment for the

      sources: *a1
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ka-beaters
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: cooking-wood
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Wood used as a source of cooking heat or smoke flavour rather than as a utensil. Smoking guidance

        - fsis-smoke
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The recipe and appliance determine the fuel arrangement. A named wood does not establish a smoking
        schedule or safe cooking endpoint. Follow the smoker instructions rather than treating any wooden
