      sources: *a2
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: fsis-smoke
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: cover
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Something placed over a vessel or food to form a barrier. In covered bread baking, a fitted lid
        helps retain moisture released by the dough during the early bake.
      sources: &a3
        - ep3-bake
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "A later uncovered stage allows a different surface environment. Match the covering to the task:

      sources: *a3
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-bake
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: grease-pan
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: An existing source-specific equipment label. In the recorded crème brûlée recipe, the grease pan
        holds the filled ramekins and surrounding water during baking, serving as the outer vessel of a

        - ep4-brulee
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: This explains the documented arrangement without establishing grease-pan as a standard synonym for

      sources: *a4
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-brulee
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1

  editorial:

      text: An explicit choice of portioning tools, not a single hybrid utensil. In the chocolate-chip-cookie

- target:
    kind: equipment

  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: An explicit choice between tools for a particular mixing step. The recorded cookie recipe uses
        melted butter with sugar, egg and other wet ingredients before the dry ingredients are added.
      sources: &a6
        - ep4-choice
        - ka-beaters
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "That context explains why a whisk is offered alongside a mixer. It does not make the tools
        universally interchangeable: thick mixtures and different attachments impose different demands.
        Read the recipe stage rather than applying this choice to all dough mixing."
      sources: *a6
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-choice
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
    - resource: ka-beaters
      role: deeper-explanation
      order: 2
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: vessel
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A broad term for a container used during preparation. Its shape and material are supplied by
        context rather than by the word itself. The pretzel recipe qualifies its vessel as heat-safe and
        chemically non-reactive.
      sources: &a7
        - ep3-gloves
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Those qualifications matter independently of capacity. Guidance for lye pretzels specifies suitable
        equipment and protective measures; a container that holds ordinary ingredients is not thereby
        suitable for that task. This page does not supply a chemical-handling procedure.
      sources: *a7
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-gloves
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: equipment
    id: cutter
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: A tool used to cut food or dough into a required shape. A round biscuit cutter is one example; the
        retained legacy usage specifies a round cutter with a particular diameter.
      sources: &a8
        - ep4-cutter
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "Shape and size affect the resulting pieces, so read the qualifier rather than assuming all cutters
        are round. Baking guidance also shows cutting dough with a knife: that illustrates alternative
        shapes, not a universal replacement for the specified tool."
      sources: *a8
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-cutter
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: prepare
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "Get ingredients, equipment or a cooking setup ready for the next operation. The instruction is
        broad: gathering and measuring cookie ingredients is one example, while a recipe may instead be
        referring to its oven or fire."
      sources: &a9
        - ep3-spoon
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Look for the object and qualifying words. Prepare does not itself specify a heating method,
        temperature or complete sequence. More precise operations in the surrounding recipe explain what
        readiness means for that particular stage.
      sources: *a9
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-spoon
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: submerge
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Put something beneath the surface of a liquid. In vegetable blanching, moving the vegetables into
        an ice-water bath is an example where immersion serves cooling rather than cooking.
      sources: &a10
        - ep4-submerge
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The liquid, temperature and duration belong to the recipe context. Submerging does not necessarily
        mean soaking for a long time, and it does not establish that the liquid is hot. Keep any chemical
        or food-safety requirements attached to the actual method.
      sources: *a10
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-submerge
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: lay-out
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Arrange items on a surface in readiness for assembly or use. For Wellington, overlapping slices on
        a temporary sheet create a layer that will later surround the filling.
      sources: &a11
        - ep3-lay
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Spacing, orientation and overlap are separate choices supplied by the recipe. Laying out a layer is
        not yet wrapping it, and a temporary supporting sheet is not necessarily intended to remain
        during cooking.
      sources: *a11
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-lay
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pack
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Press material together into a confined space to reduce gaps. Packing brown sugar into a measuring
        cup illustrates how compression changes the amount held compared with a loosely filled cup.
      sources: &a12
        - ch-pack
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Other recipes use the word for filling a jar or compacting a mixture. The degree of pressure comes
        from the task; packing food into a container does not by itself establish preservation,
        fermentation or storage safety.
      sources: *a12
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ch-pack
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pat
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Apply light repeated pressure with the hand or a suitable material. When drying washed produce, a
        clean cloth or paper towel takes up surface moisture without requiring a rubbing action.
      sources: &a13
        - ep2-wash
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The object and desired result matter: patting dry is not squeezing liquid from inside a mass. Use
        the recipe qualifier to distinguish moisture removal from shaping or pressing; the general word
        does not specify force or duration."
      sources: *a13
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-wash
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: release
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Allow something previously held or contained to escape. In covered bread baking, uncovering the
        vessel releases the moist environment retained around the loaf so the later bake proceeds
        differently.
      sources: &a14
        - ep3-bake
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The object must be read from context: steam release is not the same as removing bread from a tin.
        This bread example is not a pressure-cooker venting procedure; equipment-specific instructions
        govern pressurised appliances."
      sources: *a14
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-bake
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: unwrap
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Remove a wrapping from around food. In Wellington preparation, temporary film helps shape the
        assembled filling and is taken away before the next wrapping or cooking stage.
      sources: &a15
        - ep3-lay
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Identify which layer the instruction refers to. Removing temporary film is different from stripping
        off an edible pastry layer, and the presence of a wrapping during assembly does not establish
        that it can withstand cooking.
      sources: *a15
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-lay
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: enclose
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Surround food with a covering so it is held inside. Foil parcels illustrate folding the sides and
        ends around a filling, creating a contained cooking arrangement rather than simply placing a
        sheet underneath it.
      sources: &a16
        - ep4-parcel
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The recipe determines the covering and how it closes. A parcel is not a pressure-rated container;
        when opening a cooked parcel, account for escaping steam. Enclosing food alone says nothing about
        its cooking endpoint.
      sources: *a16
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-parcel
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: fan
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Spread adjacent slices so they overlap while opening out into a visible pattern. An apple tart can
        use a sliced section kept together and then gently spread across the pastry.
      sources: &a17
        - ep4-fan
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The purpose here is arrangement, not air movement. Slice thickness and overlap follow the
        presentation being made; the term does not refer to a fan-assisted oven or require a particular
        decorative shape.
      sources: *a17
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-fan
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: fold-and-tuck
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Fold an edge back and secure it underneath or against the surrounding material. In pie making,
        excess pastry around the rim can be folded under itself to form an edge ready for finishing.
      sources: &a18
        - b4-pie
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: This is a shaping instruction rather than folding ingredients through a mixture. The amount of
        overhang and final crimp depend on the pie; folding and tucking do not supply a universal crust
        thickness or baking schedule.
      sources: *a18
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: b4-pie
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: immerse
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Place food into a body of liquid. Water blanching illustrates lowering vegetables into boiling
        water; subsequent cooling uses another liquid environment for a different purpose.
      sources: &a19
        - nchfp-blanch
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Read the named liquid and stage rather than assuming every immersion cooks the food. Immersion
        describes placement; temperature, exposure time and any later draining are separate instructions.
        This page does not impose a new distinction between immerse and submerge.
      sources: *a19
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: nchfp-blanch
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: microwave
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Heat food using a microwave oven. Heating can be uneven, so the shape, quantity and distribution of
        food affect how a dish warms; stirring or rotating can help redistribute heat.
      sources: &a20
        - ep4-leftovers
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Use microwave-suitable containers and follow the appliance and food instructions. For leftovers,
        USDA guidance includes covering with an appropriate vent and checking temperature in several
        places. A recipe duration alone is not proof that every portion reached the required endpoint.
      sources: *a20
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-leftovers
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pull-apart
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Separate a tender food into pieces by pulling rather than making a series of knife cuts. Cooked
        lamb breast provides an example where the meat is pulled apart after braising.
      sources: &a21
        - ep4-pull
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The action follows the texture already achieved; it does not create tenderness in tough meat or
        establish that cooking was safe. Piece size depends on the serving purpose, and pulling apart
        need not mean reducing everything to fine shreds.
      sources: *a21
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-pull
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: skewer
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Thread pieces of food onto a skewer so they can be handled together. Chicken skewers illustrate
        arranging pieces along the support before cooking and turning the assembled portions.
      sources: &a22
        - ep4-skewer
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Match the skewer and spacing to the recipe and heat source. Threading is a preparation step, not a
        cooking method or a guarantee of even doneness; material-specific preparation and the food
        endpoint remain separate requirements.
      sources: *a22
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-skewer
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: soften
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "Make an ingredient less firm without necessarily turning it into a liquid. Butter for creaming is
        a useful example: it should yield to pressure while retaining structure rather than becoming
        greasy or fully melted."
      sources: &a23
        - ep4-soften
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The required softness depends on the next operation. Softened and melted butter behave differently
        in mixing, so they are not automatic substitutes. Follow the recipe endpoint rather than treating
        any warming method or fixed time as equivalent.
      sources: *a23
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-soften
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: steam-dry
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Let residual heat drive off moisture after draining. For mashed potatoes, the cooked pieces can
        return to the warm pan so remaining surface water evaporates before mashing.
      sources: &a24
        - ep4-steam
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: This is different from cooking the potatoes in steam. The aim is to reduce excess water at this
        stage, not to dehydrate the food completely. Time depends on the amount and condition of the
        drained food.
      sources: *a24
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-steam
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: stretch
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Extend dough by drawing parts away from one another. A windowpane test illustrates stretching a
        small piece until its centre becomes thin enough to reveal how the dough holds together.
      sources: &a25
        - kab-windowpane
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Resistance and tearing depend on the dough and its development. Stretching is not simply flattening
        with pressure, and not every bread requires the same thin membrane. Use the recipe purpose rather
        than treating one test as a universal endpoint.
      sources: *a25
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: kab-windowpane
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: stuff
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Put a filling inside a cavity or hollowed food. Stuffed squash illustrates using the shell to hold
        a prepared mixture, rather than spreading that mixture only over the outside.
      sources: &a26
        - ep4-stuff
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The food and filling may need different preparation stages. The instruction to stuff describes
        assembly, not whether either component is cooked or safe to eat; follow the complete method for
        the particular ingredients.
      sources: *a26
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-stuff
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: sweeten
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Add an ingredient to increase perceived sweetness. Chai finished with sugar to taste illustrates
        adjusting a drink after its other flavours have been developed.
      sources: &a27
        - ep4-sweet
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The desired balance depends on the recipe and the eater. Different sweeteners can also change
        flavour or consistency, so this general instruction does not establish equivalent substitution
        amounts. Sweetening a dish is not evidence that it has been preserved.
      sources: *a27
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-sweet
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: tap
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Give a brief light knock to a vessel or food. Tapping a filled cake pan is used to help release
        trapped air pockets before baking.
      sources: &a28
        - ep2-mold
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: This is a controlled handling step rather than prolonged beating or mixing. The recipe determines
        when it is appropriate; tapping cannot correct every batter problem, and the vessel should be
        handled in accordance with its material and construction.
      sources: *a28
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-mold
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: wipe
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Pass a cloth or paper over a surface to remove or redistribute material. In crepe preparation,
        wiping an oiled pan can leave a thin film rather than a pool of oil.
      sources: &a29
        - ep3-oil
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: "The intended result comes from the context: wiping off moisture is different from spreading fat.
        Wiping alone is not the same as washing or sanitising, and a material suitable for one surface
        need not suit a hot pan."
      sources: *a29
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep3-oil
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: work-together
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Manipulate ingredients until they combine into the texture required. Pie dough offers an example of
        bringing flour, fat and liquid together while checking whether the mixture holds when pressed.
      sources: &a30
        - ep1-pie
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The phrase does not automatically mean vigorous kneading or a long mixing time. Read the stated
        endpoint and the kind of mixture; a cohesive pastry dough and a developed bread dough do not
        demand the same handling.
      sources: *a30
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep1-pie
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: level-surface
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Even the top of a mixture so it lies more uniformly in its container. Smoothing filled cake batter
        illustrates distributing the mixture across the pan before baking.
      sources: &a31
        - ep2-mold
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Work on the surface specified by the recipe without assuming the whole mixture needs further
        beating. Levelling batter is distinct from cutting a baked cake flat; this existing action page
        does not collapse those different operations.
      sources: *a31
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep2-mold
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: pour-over
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Direct a flowing liquid onto the food or surface named. A sauce poured over fish in a parcel
        illustrates the direction of transfer before the parcel is closed.
      sources: &a32
        - ep4-parcel
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The instruction describes where the liquid goes, not a fixed quantity or rate. It need not refer to
        coffee brewing, and pouring over food does not establish that the liquid fully covers or
        submerges it.
      sources: *a32
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-parcel
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: warm-through
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Heat food beyond its outer surface so the interior also becomes warm. This describes the intended
        distribution of heat rather than merely warming the container or briefly touching the outside to
        a heat source.
      sources: &a33
        - ep4-leftovers
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: It is not a validated reheating endpoint by itself. For leftovers, follow applicable food-safety
        guidance and check the food rather than relying on surface warmth; microwave heating especially
        can leave areas at different temperatures.
      sources: *a33
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-leftovers
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: store
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "Keep food under conditions chosen for its later use. Refrigerated storage is one case: container
        coverage, the actual refrigerator temperature and room for cold air to circulate all matter."
      sources: &a34
        - fda-refrigerator
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The word alone does not specify a location, duration or shelf life. Different foods need different
        conditions, so use the recipe and appropriate storage guidance rather than assuming a closed
        container makes every food safe at room temperature.
      sources: *a34
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: fda-refrigerator
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: age
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Hold a food under controlled conditions so its characteristics develop over time. Cheddar
        illustrates maturation changing flavour and texture, with rind or packaging arrangements
        affecting moisture and the cheese surface.
      sources: &a35
        - dairy-cheddar
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: Age is not simply an instruction to leave food unattended. Conditions depend on the product and
        method; a cheese example does not establish a safe home maturation process, a universal
        temperature or a schedule for other foods.
      sources: *a35
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: dairy-cheddar
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: brush-tops
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Apply a thin coating to the upper surfaces with a brush. Egg washing a pastry border is one example
        where the intended surface matters as much as the coating itself.
      sources: &a36
        - ep4-fan
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: For laminated pastry, the cited tart method avoids the cut edges so the wash does not bind the
        layers there. That qualification belongs to this use; brushing tops does not mean coating every
        side or supplying a universal glaze recipe.
      sources: *a36
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-fan
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: remove-from-soup
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Take a specified item out of the soup while leaving the surrounding soup behind. A chicken soup can
        call for removing meat to shred and return, while aromatic herbs are taken out and discarded.
      sources: &a37
        - ep4-soup
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: What happens next depends on the object. Removing something from soup is not necessarily draining
        the whole pot or discarding the item; read the following instruction before deciding whether it
        is reserved, processed, returned or thrown away.
      sources: *a37
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-soup
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1
- target:
    kind: process
    id: separate-layers
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: "Ease existing layers apart rather than cutting additional ones. Onion rings illustrate the
        distinction: after crosswise slicing, the concentric rings are separated for individual
        handling."
      sources: &a38
        - ep4-layers
      review_version: 0.1
    - id: practical-context
      role: context
      text: The food named in the recipe determines which layers are intended and how gently to work. This
        example does not identify an unknown historical ingredient or describe creating laminated pastry
        layers; it explains separation of a structure already present.
      sources: *a38
      review_version: 0.1
  resources:
    - resource: ep4-layers
      role: introduction
      order: 1
      review_version: 0.1

- target:
    kind: ingredient
    id: chicken-breast
  review_version: 0.1
  editorial:
    - id: summary
      role: summary
      text: Meat from the breast of a chicken, sold in forms that can differ in bone, skin and portion size. A
        boneless breast and a bone-in breast half are not the same prepared piece.
      sources: &a1
        - fsis-chicken
      review_version: 0.1

Bun itself is MIT-licensed.

## JavaScriptCore

Bun statically links JavaScriptCore (and WebKit) which is LGPL-2 licensed. WebCore files from WebKit are also licensed under LGPL2. Per LGPL2:

> (1) If you statically link against an LGPL’d library, you must also provide your application in an object (not necessarily source) format, so that a user has the opportunity to modify the library and relink the application.

You can find the patched version of WebKit used by Bun here: <https://github.com/oven-sh/webkit>. If you would like to relink Bun with changes:

- `git clone https://github.com/oven-sh/WebKit vendor/WebKit`
- `bun sync-webkit-source` (checks out the version pinned in `WEBKIT_VERSION` in `scripts/build/deps/webkit.ts`)
- `bun run build:local`

This compiles JavaScriptCore, compiles Bun’s `.cpp` bindings for JavaScriptCore (which are the object files using JavaScriptCore) and outputs a new `bun` binary with your changes.

| `bun lint` has ports of parts of [`@eslint/plugin-kit`, `@eslint/config-array`, `@eslint/config-helpers` and `@eslint/compat`](https://github.com/eslint/rewrite) | Apache 2.0 |
| `bun lint` and `bun fmt` have a port of the pattern-to-regular-expression table of [`ignore`](https://github.com/kaelzhang/node-ignore) | MIT |
| `bun lint` and `bun fmt` have ports of [`is-glob`](https://github.com/micromatch/is-glob) and [`is-extglob`](https://github.com/jonschlinkert/is-extglob) | MIT |
| `bun lint` and `bun fmt` have a port of [`glob-parent`](https://github.com/gulpjs/glob-parent) | ISC |
| The `react-hooks`, `import`, `n`, `react` and `prettier` rules in `bun lint` are ports of the rules in [`eslint-plugin-react-hooks`](https://github.com/facebook/react/tree/main/packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks), [`eslint-plugin-import`](https://github.com/import-js/eslint-plugin-import), [`eslint-plugin-n`](https://github.com/eslint-community/eslint-plugin-n), [`eslint-plugin-es-x`](https://github.com/eslint-community/eslint-plugin-es-x), [`eslint-plugin-react`](https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-react) and [`eslint-plugin-prettier`](https://github.com/prettier/eslint-plugin-prettier), with the same rule names, options and messages. | `bun fmt` has ports of [`jest-docblock`](https://github.com/jestjs/jest/tree/main/packages/jest-docblock) and the crates [`sort-package-json`](https://crates.io/crates/sort-package-json) and [`oxc-toml`](https://crates.io/crates/oxc-toml) (a fork of taplo), and of parts of [`@babel/generator`](https://github.com/babel/babel), [`micromark`](https://github.com/micromark/micromark) and [`editorconfig-without-wasm`](https://github.com/fisker/editorconfig-core-js-without-wasm). ### equipment: oven

Priority: Most-used unenriched equipment; mode distinctions matter. Corpus occurrences: 286.

An enclosed heated space used for baking and roasting. A convection setting adds circulating air; it is a mode of heat delivery, not a different recipe method.

Moving air can change browning and the rate of baking. Fan strength and oven design vary, so a convection setting is not a universal improvement or a fixed temperature conversion for every bake.

Sources: [Convection oven baking: Why this baker is a fan](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2025/03/19/convection-oven-baking).

### equipment: pan

Priority: Very frequent broad vessel term needing qualification. Corpus occurrences: 256.

A broad cookware term whose practical meaning depends on the vessel. A shallow skillet offers access for turning and searing; a deeper saucepan holds liquids more readily.

Choose by the operation, usable surface area and sides rather than the word pan alone. A wide braising vessel and a small saucepan are not interchangeable merely because both can be covered and heated.

Sources: [How to Build a Cookware Collection](https://www.lecreuset.com/blog/how-to-build-a-cookware-collection.html).

A cooking vessel commonly used to contain liquids and substantial quantities of food. A stockpot has tall sides suited to stock, soup or boiling pasta.

Capacity and shape matter together: a tall pot contains liquid differently from a shallow skillet. Read the recipe for the intended batch size and operation instead of assuming that every pot is suitable for every cooking task.

Sources: [How to Build a Cookware Collection](https://www.lecreuset.com/blog/how-to-build-a-cookware-collection.html).

A lid changes how a pan is used, including covered braising or poaching. Fit and heat compatibility belong to the particular lid and its handles; a cover is not automatically oven-safe or a pressure-cooking seal.

Bring ingredients together into a mixture. In baking, how and when they are combined can matter as much as whether the ingredients are distributed.

Leave a preparation undisturbed for a specified purpose. In pastry dough, resting can allow gluten to relax, making the dough easier to handle.

Rest and chill can happen together but describe different things: a pause allows time-dependent changes, while cooling also firms pastry fat. Rest does not by itself specify refrigeration or mean that a dough is undergoing a yeast rise.

### equipment: plate

Priority: Most-used remaining equipment; explain serving shape. Corpus occurrences: 58.

A shallow piece of tableware for presenting individual portions. Side plates suit smaller servings or sandwiches, while deeper plate forms can hold saucier foods.

Consider the usable surface and depth, not just the outside diameter. A broad rim reduces the central serving area, and a flat plate contains liquid differently from a soup plate. Materials and sizes vary; plate alone does not specify bakeware.

Sources: [Salad & side plates](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/cat/side-plates-18863/); [Deep plates](https://www.ikea.com/ch/en/cat/deep-plates-18862/).

Qualification: No universal dimensions, material or oven suitability inferred. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### equipment: dish

Priority: Common broad container word; avoid conflating serving and baking. Corpus occurrences: 14.

A broad term for a vessel used to hold, prepare or present food. A baking dish is one particular form: its sides contain layered mixtures and liquids during oven cooking.

Some purpose-made baking dishes also serve for marinating, breading or taking a bake to the table. Those capabilities belong to the particular vessel. The unqualified word dish does not tell you its depth, capacity or compatibility with direct heat.

Sources: [Baking Dishes](https://www.lecreuset.ca/en_CA/bakeware/baking-dishes).

Qualification: Generic dish remains broader than a baking dish or platter. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### equipment: jar

Priority: Frequently used container with mouth and closure distinctions. Corpus occurrences: 14.

A container with an opening that can be closed with a lid. The mouth affects access: wide-mouth canning jars are easier to fill and empty than narrower examples.

Closure design matters independently of capacity. A screw band, lid and sealing surface work together on a purpose-made canning jar; an ordinary storage jar is not evidence of suitability for a heat-processing recipe.

Sources: [Recommended Jars and Lids](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/can/general-canning-information/recommended-jars-and-lids/).

Qualification: No canning method or storage life supplied. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### equipment: cloth

Priority: Preparation material with useful handling example. Corpus occurrences: 6.

A flexible fabric used as a preparation aid. In strudel making, a cloth spread over the work area supports the thin dough and can help lift and roll it around the filling.

This use relies on a broad flexible support rather than a rigid board. Other food-contact tasks require different fabric properties: a cloth used to guide dough is not automatically a fine straining cloth. Choose it for the operation described.

Sources: [Homemade Strudel](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2017/01/19/homemade-strudel).

Qualification: No equivalence with cheesecloth or universal fabric suitability proposed. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### equipment: baking-mold

Priority: Useful distinction between shaping and merely containing. Corpus occurrences: 4.

A baking vessel whose cavity gives the bake its form. A shaped cake pan illustrates how the finished surface follows the details of the mold.

Release is part of the preparation: grease or otherwise prepare the cavity as directed for that recipe and material. Intricate shapes need attention to recesses, and batter needs room to expand. Do not assume a non-stick surface removes every preparation step.

Sources: [Bundt Cake](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/guides/bundt-cake).

Qualification: No fixed fill level or release procedure generalized to all molds. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### equipment: squeeze-bottle

A squeezable container that dispenses liquid through a tip, allowing one-handed application. Typical uses include adding oil to a pan or drawing sauce lines over a finished dish.

The tip controls the stream; a fine tip favours a narrow drizzle. The cited bottle has an attached cap, but closures and materials vary. Dispensing convenience does not establish suitability for heating the bottle or for long-term storage.

Sources: [OXO Chef's Squeeze Bottles - 12 ounces](https://www.oxo.com/chef-s-squeeze-bottles-6-ounces-1-3613-0.html).

Qualification: Product example only; heat and storage limits are not inferred. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

An open framework of metal bars used to support food over heat. Historical hearth examples held meat or fish above hot coals.

Gaps between the bars distinguish it from a solid griddle surface. Food rests on the bars rather than on a continuous plate; a museum example documents this construction without making every gridiron a complete barbecue appliance.

Sources: [Gridiron (dated 1708)](https://www.manuscriptcookbookssurvey.org/collection/Detail/utensils/1162).

### equipment: soup-plate

A deep plate whose recessed centre can hold soup or other foods with liquid. It sits between a flat plate and a bowl in serving form.

The depth is useful for saucy dishes as well as soup, but capacity still varies by design. A recipe using a soup plate names a vessel shape; it does not establish a standard portion size or show that a modern example can go in the oven.

### equipment: clay-casserole

Priority: Material-specific vessel with important heat-source distinction. Corpus occurrences: 10.

A casserole vessel made from clay-based ceramic, used for preparations such as stews or oven bakes when the vessel is designed for that heat source.

Ceramic cookware is not one compatibility class. The cited Emile Henry stewpot has its own gradual-heating instructions, while Le Creuset stoneware baking dishes exclude stovetop use. Follow the particular vessel instructions rather than assuming clay means flame-safe; sudden temperature changes also need care.

### equipment: glass-jars

Priority: Repeated preservation vessel; retain distinct indexed identity. Corpus occurrences: 8.

Glass containers with closable mouths, used to hold food. For home canning, purpose-made threaded jars and compatible lids provide a defined sealing arrangement.

Check the jar as well as its closure. Scratches or damaged sealing surfaces can matter during processing, and washing an empty jar does not itself sterilize it. This material description is not a canning schedule or proof that a reused commercial jar is suitable.

Sources: [Recommended Jars and Lids](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/can/general-canning-information/recommended-jars-and-lids/).

Qualification: Existing glass-jars and jar identities retained; no consolidation or processing advice. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### equipment: tray

Priority: Broad term spans carrying and baking contexts. Corpus occurrences: 6.

A broad, relatively shallow support used to gather, carry or arrange items. Serving trays may have handles to help move several items together.

A carrying tray and a baking sheet share a broad shape but differ in intended use. Where a recipe puts a tray in the oven, select an oven-suitable baking tray; a serving tray with coated surfaces or wooden handles does not establish that capability.

A small spoon used for stirring tea or coffee and for handling small portions, including desserts. It is a table utensil with a bowl and handle.

Its shape gives access to a cup or a small amount of food. Here teaspoon identifies equipment, not a calibrated measuring spoon: the name alone does not make a spoonful an exact recipe quantity.

### equipment: platter

Priority: Serving vessel distinction complements plate and dish. Corpus occurrences: 3.

A broad serving dish used to present food for sharing. Some designs include a separate central space for dip surrounded by room for vegetables, cheese or other small foods.

Choose the arrangement for the food being served: an uninterrupted surface and a divided dip platter do different jobs. Product-specific heat ratings do not make every platter oven-safe, and a serving form is not a substitute for a specified baking vessel.

### equipment: pitcher

Priority: Useful beverage service tool beyond individual cups. Corpus occurrences: 3.

A vessel for holding and pouring drinks into smaller servings. Pitchers can serve a batch of lemonade or other mixed drinks rather than one individual portion.

Capacity, material and opening affect how it is used. The cited stoneware pitcher is designed for hot or cold drinks, but that product capability should not be assumed for every pitcher; check the vessel when serving hot liquids.

Sources: [Signature Pitcher](https://www.lecreuset.com/signature-pitcher/70901US.html).

Qualification: No universal temperature resistance or measuring accuracy inferred. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: refrigerate

Priority: Most-used remaining process; distinguish controlled cold storage. Corpus occurrences: 30.

Place food in a refrigerator to keep it chilled. Refrigeration slows bacterial growth; it is a storage condition rather than a cooking or freezing step.

Cold air needs room to circulate, so avoid tightly overpacking the appliance. Covered containers help keep stored foods separated, and an appliance thermometer checks the actual temperature. Follow food-specific storage guidance: the verb refrigerate alone does not specify a safe storage life.

Sources: [Refrigerator Thermometers: Cold Facts about Food Safety](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/refrigerator-thermometers-cold-facts-about-food-safety).

Qualification: No universal shelf life or preservation guarantee. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: press

Priority: Frequent broad mechanical action with distinct purposes. Corpus occurrences: 17.

Apply pressure to food or a mixture for a stated result. Pressing shortbread dough into a pan shapes an even layer; pressing cut tomatoes can release pulp and seeds.

The object and direction determine the task. Shaping dough, attaching a coating and forcing food through a sieve are not interchangeable instructions. Use the recipe's endpoint rather than treating press as a fixed force or a request to puree everything.

Sources: [Shortbread Cookies](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/recipes/shortbread-cookies-recipe); [Epépiner et concasser une tomate](https://chefsimon.com/gourmets/chef-simon/recettes/epepiner-et-concasser-une-tomate).

Qualification: Broad action retained; coating and sieve contexts are directly observed Corpus usage. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: turn

Priority: Frequent action important for exposing another surface to heat. Corpus occurrences: 16.

Change which side of a piece of food faces the heat or cooking surface. In frying, turning exposes another surface for cooking and browning.

Use a suitable utensil to move the piece without unnecessarily piercing its crust. How often to turn depends on the method; the handling appropriate to pan-frying is not automatically the same as for food immersed in fat.

Sources: [Tips for Frying on the Stove](https://www.ciafoodies.com/tips-for-frying-on-the-stove/).

Qualification: No universal turning interval or number of turns. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: wash

Priority: Frequent instruction needs ingredient-specific treatment. Corpus occurrences: 16.

Clean the surface of food using an appropriate washing method. For fresh produce, FDA guidance uses running water; firm produce can also be rubbed or scrubbed with a clean produce brush.

Produce washing is not sterilization, and soap or detergent is not recommended on fruits and vegetables. Ready-to-eat produce labelled as pre-washed can be used without another wash. These produce instructions should not be generalized to every food.

Sources: [Selecting and Serving Produce Safely](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/selecting-and-serving-produce-safely).

Qualification: Produce-scoped example; no instruction to wash raw meat or poultry. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: seal

Priority: Common action with pastry and container contexts. Corpus occurrences: 9.

Close an opening or join edges so the contents are held in place. In a hand pie, pressing the pastry edges together with a fork helps keep filling from escaping at the seam.

In storage instructions, seal may instead refer to closing a bag or container. The object determines the operation: a pastry seam is not a vacuum seal, and closing a lid does not by itself establish a safe preservation process.

Sources: [The return of hand pies](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2018/07/02/the-return-of-hand-pies); [Recommended Jars and Lids](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/can/general-canning-information/recommended-jars-and-lids/).

Qualification: No preservation claim; pastry and packaging senses remain context-dependent. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: separate

Priority: Existing broad action; egg example must not narrow identity. Corpus occurrences: 9.

Divide components so they can be handled independently. Separating an egg keeps the yolk apart from the white, allowing each to be used where the recipe needs it.

An egg separator lets the white pass through while retaining the yolk. Elsewhere the recipe may ask to separate cloves or pieces of food; those are different physical tasks. Read what must be separated rather than assuming the verb always means egg separation.

Sources: [Important Food Safety Information](https://www.incredibleegg.org/egg-handling-storage-tips/).

Qualification: Clove and food-piece contexts are retained from Corpus; no egg-only scope. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: wrap

Priority: Common enclosing action; distinguish storage wrapper from cooking parcel. Corpus occurrences: 9.

Enclose food or a preparation in a flexible covering. Pastry disks may be wrapped before chilling so they can rest as individual prepared pieces.

The material must suit the next step. A wrapper used while chilling is not automatically suitable for baking or other heating. Wrapping also differs from simply laying a loose cover over a bowl; follow the recipe's instruction about what is enclosed.

Sources: [Pie crust](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/guides/pie-crust).

Qualification: No inference that storage wrap is heat-safe or airtight. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: pat-dry

Priority: Surface preparation distinct from thorough dehydration. Corpus occurrences: 4.

Blot surface moisture with a clean absorbent cloth or paper towel. After washing produce, drying removes water remaining on the outside.

Gentle contact targets surface droplets rather than squeezing liquid out of the food or dehydrating it throughout. FDA produce guidance specifies a clean cloth or paper towel; reusing a soiled cloth defeats that handling step.

Sources: [Selecting and Serving Produce Safely](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/selecting-and-serving-produce-safely).

Qualification: Produce example only; no preservation or shelf-stability implication. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: slow-cook

Priority: Useful heat-method distinction backed by appliance guidance. Corpus occurrences: 4.

Cook with gentle heat over an extended period. A covered electric slow cooker is one implementation, combining heat from the pot with moisture and steam inside the vessel.

High and low settings change the cooking rate, and lifting the lid loses heat. Use a recipe and loading guidance suited to the appliance; the general instruction slow-cook does not justify an arbitrary low setting or a universal duration for every food.

Sources: [Slow Cookers and Food Safety](https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/slow-cookers-and-food-safety).

Qualification: Electric-cooker example is not an exclusive definition; no universal safety schedule. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: skin

Priority: Ingredient-specific removal task; distinguish fish scales. Corpus occurrences: 3.

Remove the skin of an ingredient. For tomatoes, brief exposure to hot water followed by rapid cooling can loosen the skin so it can be peeled away.

The method depends on the food: removing skin from a fish is different from loosening tomato skin. Descaling removes scales from a fish surface and is a separate operation; skin does not prescribe one knife technique for every ingredient.

Sources: [Monder](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-monder); [Techniques appliquees a la preparation des poissons](https://chefsimon.com/articles/sommaire-techniques-appliquees-a-la-preparation-des-poissons).

Qualification: Tomato example does not generalize to all nuts, fish or poultry. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: descale

Priority: Low-frequency but clear fish-preparation distinction. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Remove scales from the surface of a fish using a scaler or an appropriate knife action. The scales are detached from the skin rather than the whole skin being removed.

Descaling is one preparatory task among others such as trimming fins or gutting. Whether it is needed depends on the species and intended preparation; it should not be treated as a synonym for filleting or skinning.

Sources: [Ecailler un poisson portion](https://chefsimon.com/gourmets/chef-simon/recettes/ecailler-un-poisson-portion).

Qualification: Species-dependent; no freshness or safety test inferred from appearance. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: temper-spices

Priority: Zero literal uses but useful existing culturally scoped method. Corpus occurrences: 0.

Heat spices in hot oil or ghee so their flavour passes into the fat. In Indian cooking, the flavoured fat may start a dish or be added near the end as a finishing step.

The sequence matters because different spices and aromatics cook at different rates. This is distinct from dry-roasting spices, and from tempering chocolate or eggs. Tadka is one relevant culinary context, not a universal replacement name for every practice involving spices and fat.

Sources: [Cinnamon Kitchen: The Cookbook — Tempering (p. 27)](https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781472934932_A29775035/preview-9781472934932_A29775035.pdf).

Qualification: Regional practices vary; no new aliases or fixed time/temperature instructions. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: shock

Priority: Useful distinct cooling step already eligible for a page. Corpus occurrences: 0.

Cool food rapidly, often immediately after a hot-water or steam treatment. Plunging blanched vegetables into cold or ice water interrupts continued cooking.

Blanching supplies the heat; shocking supplies the rapid cooling. They can be consecutive steps without being the same action. In the cited vegetable-freezing guidance, the vegetables are then drained thoroughly; chilling slowly in a refrigerator is a different cooling approach.

Sources: [Blanching Vegetables](https://nchfp.uga.edu/how/freeze/freeze-general-information/blanching-vegetables/).

Qualification: Vegetable example; no full freezing or preservation procedure supplied. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: butter

Priority: Common instruction whose object changes its purpose. Corpus occurrences: 9.

Apply or incorporate butter as the preparation requires. Buttering a mold coats its surface to help release the bake; buttering bread spreads butter onto the food itself.

The object matters. Adding butter to a sauce is different from coating a pan, and a buttered mold may still need flour or another lining. Follow the specified preparation rather than assuming butter alone makes every bake release cleanly.

Sources: [Beurrer](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-beurrer).

Qualification: No universal substitution or release guarantee. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: flour

Priority: Useful surface-coating action distinct from adding flour to a mixture. Corpus occurrences: 3.

Coat or dust a surface with flour. On a buttered baking mold, moving the mold spreads flour over the base and sides; tapping removes the excess.

On a pastry work surface, a light dusting helps control sticking during rolling. Both uses put flour on a surface rather than treating it as a measured ingredient to mix in. The amount and surface preparation depend on the recipe.

Sources: [Chemiser un moule](https://chefsimon.com/gourmets/chef-simon/recettes/chemiser-un-moule); [Pie crust](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/guides/pie-crust).

Qualification: No fixed flour quantity or universal pan-preparation rule. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### equipment: cauldron

Priority: Most-used remaining equipment; give historical construction context. Corpus occurrences: 11.

A substantial cooking pot associated with hearth cooking. Historical examples used legs to stand over a fire, handles for suspension, or both. These features supported cooking in a vessel above the heat rather than directly on a flat hob.

Cauldrons varied in size and use. The cited medieval example explains a hearth arrangement, not a universal modern design: the name alone does not establish material, capacity or compatibility with an induction hob. Read the recipe and the actual vessel together.

Sources: [Caldron (13th or 14th century)](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/471343).

Qualification: Historical example does not equate all cauldrons with a specific modern kazan or Dutch oven. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

A container with a relatively narrow opening, commonly used to hold and pour liquids. A stopper or cap closes the mouth; the cited swing-top example combines a glass body with a separate seal and fastening.

The opening affects filling and access for cleaning. In Corpus, a bottle is also named as a rolling aid, but that particular use does not redefine the general container. A closure alone establishes neither a measuring scale nor suitability for cooking.

### process: spoon

Priority: Observed portion-transfer action, not a quantity unit. Corpus occurrences: 4.

Transfer a mixture with a spoon, usually in controlled portions. Cookie dough can be spooned from the bowl onto a baking sheet; a scoop is another portioning tool in that example.

The verb does not specify a measured tablespoon or teaspoon unless the recipe gives one. It describes how the mixture is moved, while the required portion size, spacing or filling level must come from the surrounding instruction.

Sources: [Metric Kitchen: Chocolate Chip Cookies](https://www.nist.gov/pml/owm/metric-si/metric-kitchen/metric-kitchen-recipe-gallery/metric-kitchen-chocolate-chip-cookies).

Qualification: No standard spoon volume inferred. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: tie

Priority: Useful fastening action; distinguish purpose from a knot prescription. Corpus occurrences: 4.

Fasten ingredients or a wrapper with string or kitchen twine. Tying an aromatic herb bundle keeps its components together so they can flavour a liquid and then be removed.

The object determines the purpose: holding a bouquet together is different from shaping a roast. Use the recipe’s fastening arrangement rather than assuming one knot, tension or bundle composition applies to every instruction to tie.

Sources: [Bouquet Garni — The French Laundry Cookbook](https://app.ckbk.com/recipe/fren57567c02s001ss001r003/bouquet-garni/).

Qualification: Herb-bundle evidence supports the example; no trussing method or new alias added. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: thin

Priority: Consistency adjustment distinct from smoothing lumps. Corpus occurrences: 3.

Make a mixture less thick by adding the specified liquid. In hummus, small additions of water can move a stiff paste toward a spoonable consistency.

Add gradually and reassess after mixing. Thinning changes how the mixture flows; it is not the same as processing away coarse particles. The recipe must identify a suitable liquid and endpoint, rather than thin implying water in every dish.

Sources: [How to make hummus](https://www.bbcgoodfoodme.com/video-recipe/how-to-make-hummus/).

Qualification: No universal dilution ratio or substitution rule. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: pinch

Priority: Observed dough-joining action distinct from the quantity word. Corpus occurrences: 2.

Press a small area between the fingers to join or shape it. Pinching the ends of dough ropes together anchors them before braiding a challah.

The pressure is local to the join rather than a kneading action applied throughout the dough. In this process sense, pinch describes handling; a pinch of salt is a quantity expression and does not tell you how to form a dough seam.

Sources: [Classic Challah — Uri Scheft](https://www.jewishfoodsociety.org/recipes/classic-challah).

Qualification: No quantity semantics or dough formula altered. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: slash

Priority: Useful bread-surface distinction; paired with existing scoring knowledge. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Make an incision in the surface of food. For bread, slashing the dough before baking creates an opening that helps direct expansion as the loaf heats.

A sharp blade limits dragging through the dough. Placement, angle and depth depend on the loaf and intended result, so a decorative mark and a functional expansion cut need not be identical. This is different from piercing many small holes with a fork.

Sources: [Baking trials: Just how much does scoring impact bread?](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2024/05/30/scoring-bread-dough).

Qualification: Bread-focused example, not a universal score/slash identity merge. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: smooth

Priority: Observed hummus presentation step; distinguish surface from internal texture. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Even out the surface of a preparation. The back of a spoon can shape the top of hummus, reducing ridges or making an intentional swirl before finishing.

Smoothing the surface does not necessarily make the mixture inside finer. Blending a coarse puree changes its internal texture; moving a spoon across the top mainly changes its presentation. Follow the object named in the recipe.

Sources: [How to make hummus](https://www.bbcgoodfoodme.com/video-recipe/how-to-make-hummus/).

Qualification: Surface sense reflects Corpus; no new puree alias. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: lay

Priority: Common assembly action with a useful layering example. Corpus occurrences: 6.

Place something onto a supporting surface in the arrangement required. In Wellington assembly, slices of prosciutto are laid onto cling film with slight overlaps to form a layer.

The instruction concerns position: overlap, orientation and coverage come from its context. Laying out the layer is separate from wrapping it around the filling, and a temporary support used in assembly is not automatically intended to remain during cooking.

Sources: [Beef wellington — Gordon Ramsay](https://tollbit.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/beef-wellington).

Qualification: No universal overlap amount; temporary film is removed in the cited method. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

Separate a tender food into pieces by pulling rather than making a series of knife cuts. Cooked lamb breast provides an example where the meat is pulled apart after braising.

The action follows the texture already achieved; it does not create tenderness in tough meat or establish that cooking was safe. Piece size depends on the serving purpose, and pulling apart need not mean reducing everything to fine shreds.

Sources: [Great British Menu — Peter Sanchez-Iglesias](https://downloads.bbc.co.uk/tv/greatbritishmenu/petersanchez-iglesias-GBM-week5.pdf).

Qualification: Preparation example only; no doneness test or braising schedule. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: skewer

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Thread pieces of food onto a skewer so they can be handled together. Chicken skewers illustrate arranging pieces along the support before cooking and turning the assembled portions.

Match the skewer and spacing to the recipe and heat source. Threading is a preparation step, not a cooking method or a guarantee of even doneness; material-specific preparation and the food endpoint remain separate requirements.

### process: soften

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Make an ingredient less firm without necessarily turning it into a liquid. Butter for creaming is a useful example: it should yield to pressure while retaining structure rather than becoming greasy or fully melted.

The required softness depends on the next operation. Softened and melted butter behave differently in mixing, so they are not automatic substitutes. Follow the recipe endpoint rather than treating any warming method or fixed time as equivalent.

Sources: [How to soften butter quickly](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2023/10/05/soften-butter-quickly).

Qualification: Butter example does not impose one endpoint on all foods. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: steam-dry

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Let residual heat drive off moisture after draining. For mashed potatoes, the cooked pieces can return to the warm pan so remaining surface water evaporates before mashing.

This is different from cooking the potatoes in steam. The aim is to reduce excess water at this stage, not to dehydrate the food completely. Time depends on the amount and condition of the drained food.

Sources: [Best ever creamy mashed potatoes](https://tollbit.bbcgoodfood.com/recipes/best-ever-creamy-mashed-potatoes).

Qualification: No universal time or shelf-stability implication. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: stretch

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Extend dough by drawing parts away from one another. A windowpane test illustrates stretching a small piece until its centre becomes thin enough to reveal how the dough holds together.

Resistance and tearing depend on the dough and its development. Stretching is not simply flattening with pressure, and not every bread requires the same thin membrane. Use the recipe purpose rather than treating one test as a universal endpoint.

Sources: [What is the windowpane test for bread dough?](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2022/10/14/what-is-the-windowpane-test-for-bread-dough).

Qualification: Windowpane example does not prescribe a test for every dough. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: stuff

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Put a filling inside a cavity or hollowed food. Stuffed squash illustrates using the shell to hold a prepared mixture, rather than spreading that mixture only over the outside.

The food and filling may need different preparation stages. The instruction to stuff describes assembly, not whether either component is cooked or safe to eat; follow the complete method for the particular ingredients.

Sources: [Cheesy stuffed squash](https://www.bbcgoodfoodme.com/recipes/cheesy-stuffed-squash/).

### process: tap

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Give a brief light knock to a vessel or food. Tapping a filled cake pan is used to help release trapped air pockets before baking.

This is a controlled handling step rather than prolonged beating or mixing. The recipe determines when it is appropriate; tapping cannot correct every batter problem, and the vessel should be handled in accordance with its material and construction.

Sources: [Bundt Cake](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/guides/bundt-cake).

Qualification: Cake-pan example; no universal force or repetition count. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: wipe

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Pass a cloth or paper over a surface to remove or redistribute material. In crepe preparation, wiping an oiled pan can leave a thin film rather than a pool of oil.

The intended result comes from the context: wiping off moisture is different from spreading fat. Wiping alone is not the same as washing or sanitising, and a material suitable for one surface need not suit a hot pan.

Sources: [Crepes Two Ways](https://www.pbs.org/video/crepes-two-ways-Zwiatp/).

Qualification: Transcript supports oil-film example; no sanitation or heat-protection claim. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: work-together

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 1.

Manipulate ingredients until they combine into the texture required. Pie dough offers an example of bringing flour, fat and liquid together while checking whether the mixture holds when pressed.

The phrase does not automatically mean vigorous kneading or a long mixing time. Read the stated endpoint and the kind of mixture; a cohesive pastry dough and a developed bread dough do not demand the same handling.

Sources: [Pie crust](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/guides/pie-crust).

Qualification: No fixed intensity or new kneading equivalence. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: level-surface

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 0.

Even the top of a mixture so it lies more uniformly in its container. Smoothing filled cake batter illustrates distributing the mixture across the pan before baking.

Work on the surface specified by the recipe without assuming the whole mixture needs further beating. Levelling batter is distinct from cutting a baked cake flat; this existing action page does not collapse those different operations.

Sources: [Bundt Cake](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/guides/bundt-cake).

Qualification: Legacy action interpreted as surface evening, not cake trimming. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### process: pour-over

Direct a flowing liquid onto the food or surface named. A sauce poured over fish in a parcel illustrates the direction of transfer before the parcel is closed.

### process: warm-through

Priority: Complete remaining eligible process coverage with a scoped practical explanation. Corpus occurrences: 0.

Heat food beyond its outer surface so the interior also becomes warm. This describes the intended distribution of heat rather than merely warming the container or briefly touching the outside to a heat source.

## Completed pages

### chicken-breast

Priority: Frequently used cut; clarify preparation qualifiers. Corpus occurrences: 73.

Meat from the breast of a chicken, sold in forms that can differ in bone, skin and portion size. A boneless breast and a bone-in breast half are not the same prepared piece.

Match the cut to the recipe before applying its method. Size and preparation affect cooking, so appearance or a fixed time alone cannot establish doneness; use appropriate poultry guidance and a food thermometer. The ingredient name does not imply that the meat is already cooked.

Sources: [Chicken from Farm to Table](https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/poultry/chicken-farm-table).

Qualification: No universal portion size, cooking time or automatic bone/skin removal. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### paprika

Priority: High-use spice with important variety differences. Corpus occurrences: 61.

A red ground spice made from dried peppers. It contributes colour and pepper flavour, but its heat varies with the peppers used; sweet, hot and smoked versions are not identical.

Read the qualifier when a recipe names a particular paprika. A smoked version adds a smoke character that an unsmoked sweet paprika does not supply. The generic name alone establishes neither a fixed heat level nor a universal substitution for cayenne.

Sources: [About Paprika Uses, Pairings and Recipes](https://www.mccormick.com/blogs/how-to/about-paprika-uses-pairings-and-recipes).

Qualification: No assumption that paprika is always mild or smoked; existing identities retained. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### cumin

Priority: High-use seasoning; distinguish form from flavour. Corpus occurrences: 46.

An aromatic spice used whole or ground; ground cumin is made from the seeds. Its warm, earthy flavour appears in meat rubs, bean dishes, vegetable preparations and numerous spice mixtures.

The form matters to handling: a ground spice disperses differently from intact seeds. Follow the recipe’s whole or ground instruction rather than assuming the same spoonful gives the same result. Cumin is an ingredient in some blends, not another name for the complete blend.

Sources: [Ground Cumin](https://www.mccormick.com/products/mccormick-ground-cumin-1-5-oz).

Qualification: Ground product illustrates use; no fixed whole-to-ground conversion. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### nutmeg

Priority: Frequent spice needing a savoury-use explanation. Corpus occurrences: 46.

A strongly aromatic spice from the nutmeg kernel, with a warm flavour often perceived as sweet. It is used in baking and desserts, but also in savoury vegetables, meat dishes and spinach fillings.

The sweetness describes aroma and flavour rather than added sugar. Follow the recipe quantity and specified form: the same ingredient may be grated or supplied ground. A little seasoning has a different role from a bulk ingredient, and no universal amount suits every dish.

Sources: [Nutmeg](https://www.mccormickscienceinstitute.com/resources/culinary-spices/herbs-spices/nutmeg).

Qualification: Culinary use only; no medicinal claims or dose advice. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### pasta

Priority: Frequent broad ingredient with shape-dependent use. Corpus occurrences: 46.

A family of shaped foods rather than one fixed shape. Spaghetti is a long-strand example; other forms include tubes, shells and filled shapes, which create different ways of carrying a sauce or filling.

The recipe and package identify the particular pasta being used. A cooking time for one dried spaghetti product is not a rule for every shape or preparation. Choosing a shape and cooking it are separate decisions; this general page does not redefine all pasta as spaghetti.

Sources: [Spaghetti Pasta](https://www.barilla.com/en-us/products/pasta/classic-blue-box/spaghetti).

Qualification: Broad scope retained; one manufacturer’s semolina product is not universal composition. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### coriander-leaves

Priority: Common herb; keep leaves distinct from seed spice. Corpus occurrences: 39.

The leafy herb from the coriander plant, often called cilantro. The same plant is also grown for its seeds, but harvesting the leaves and collecting mature seed are different uses.

Read the part named in the recipe: a request for leaves is not a request for ground coriander seed. Leaves can be used fresh or preserved, but this page does not establish a fresh-to-dried conversion or make the two plant parts interchangeable.

Sources: [Cilantro/Coriander in the Garden](https://extension.usu.edu/yardandgarden/research/cilantro-coriander-in-the-garden).

Qualification: Leaf identity preserved; no seed substitution or storage-life prescription. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### cayenne-pepper

Priority: Common heat seasoning; distinguish from mild paprika. Corpus occurrences: 38.

A hot chilli seasoning commonly supplied as a fine red powder. Ground cayenne contributes pungent heat to sauces, rubs and marinades, rather than merely adding a red colour.

Add it with the intended heat level in mind. A red powder is not automatically equivalent to cayenne: paprika and mixed chilli seasonings may bring different heat and flavour. The cited product illustrates ground cayenne, not a guaranteed heat rating for every jar.

Sources: [Culinary Ground Cayenne Pepper](https://www.mccormick.com/collections/all-mccormick-for-chefs-foodservice-products/products/mccormick-culinary-ground-cayenne-pepper-14-oz).

Qualification: No universal heat rating or blend equivalence. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### spring-onion

Priority: Frequent fresh allium with useful part distinctions. Corpus occurrences: 35.

An onion used with its green tops and pale lower section. Both parts are edible, and the ingredient can be used raw or cooked; the lower section may be narrow or show a more developed bulb.

Trim the root and damaged ends, then cut the parts required by the recipe. Regional use of spring onion, green onion and scallion is not perfectly uniform. Existing project names are retained without claiming that every regional market makes the same botanical or harvest distinction.

Sources: [Spring onion](https://tollbit.bbcgoodfood.com/glossary/spring-onion-glossary); [Onion, green onion, scallion — FoodLink](https://www.extension.purdue.edu/foodlink/food.php?food=onion%2C+green+onion%2C+scallion).

Qualification: Regional naming is qualified, not changed. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### spaghetti

Priority: Common pasta shape deserving more than a generic pasta label. Corpus occurrences: 31.

A long, cord-like pasta shape. It is used with tomato, oil-based and other sauces; the strands are the defining practical distinction from short tubes or filled pasta.

Match cooking to the actual product and desired texture. The cited semolina spaghetti has its own package instructions, which should not be transferred to every thickness or formulation. Sauce choice can vary without changing the identity of the pasta shape.

Sources: [Spaghetti Pasta](https://www.barilla.com/en-us/products/pasta/classic-blue-box/spaghetti).
