### sweet-pepper

Priority: Useful distinction from hot peppers and single colour names. Corpus occurrences: 30.

A fleshy pepper used as a vegetable, with varieties that differ in shape and colour. Bell peppers are one familiar form, but sweet peppers also include elongated and smaller shapes.

They can be sliced for raw dishes or cooked, including roasting. Choose firm peppers and prepare the stem, seeds and flesh as directed. The general name does not require a red bell pepper or establish that all colours and varieties have identical flavour.

Sources: [Sweet pepper — FoodLink](https://extension.purdue.edu/foodlink/food.php?food=sweet+pepper).

Qualification: No identity merge with bell-pepper or specific colour entries. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### garlic-powder

Priority: Common dry seasoning; explain texture difference from fresh garlic. Corpus occurrences: 29.

A powdered garlic ingredient that adds garlic flavour without pieces of chopped clove. Its fine texture makes it useful in seasoning mixtures, sauces, soups and rubs where even distribution is wanted.

It is not the same as garlic salt or a multi-ingredient seasoning. Check the product and recipe rather than assuming a blend is plain powder. Replacing fresh garlic also changes the texture of the dish; no general fresh-to-powder ratio is established here.

Sources: [Garlic Powder](https://www.mccormick.com/products/mccormick-garlic-powder-5-37-oz?pr_rd_page=1).

Qualification: No conversion ratio or product-wide additive guarantee. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### extra-virgin-olive-oil

Priority: Common qualified oil; explain why the full name matters. Corpus occurrences: 28.

A category of virgin olive oil obtained through mechanical or physical processing and meeting specified quality characteristics. Extra virgin is a defined category, not simply a decorative description for any olive oil.

The International Olive Council distinguishes it from refined olive oil and blends of refined and virgin oils. Read the full label when the recipe specifies extra virgin. This classification does not by itself give a universal smoke point, cooking temperature or flavour intensity.

Sources: [Olive oils](https://www.internationaloliveoil.org/olive-world/olive-oil/).

Qualification: No numeric standard encoded, health claim or universal heating limit. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### chicken-stock

Priority: Common cooking liquid; distinguish body from a fixed formula. Corpus occurrences: 25.

A chicken-based cooking liquid often made with bones, connective tissue and aromatic ingredients. Extracted gelatin can contribute body, making stock useful as a foundation for sauces and soups.

The Culinary Institute of America describes practical overlap between stock and broth when meat remains on the bones. The name is not a guarantee of one formula or strength. Follow the actual preparation or product rather than treating stock and broth as rigidly separated by a single ingredient.

Sources: [A No-Rules Guide for Rich Chicken Stock](https://www.ciafoodies.com/a-no-rules-guide-for-rich-chicken-stock/).

Qualification: No forced identity merge, cooking schedule or universal salt assumption. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### mustard

Priority: Observed prepared-condiment use with Dijon/yellow qualifiers. Corpus occurrences: 25.

In these recipe uses, mustard is a prepared condiment made from mustard seed and liquid. Smooth Dijon is one example, while other preparations differ in texture, acidity and flavour.

A qualifier such as Dijon or yellow matters to the result. Prepared mustard contributes moisture as well as seasoning, so dry mustard powder is not automatically an equal-volume substitute. The cited Dijon formulation illustrates one product rather than defining every mustard sold under this broad name.

Sources: [Dijon Original Mustard](https://www.maille.com/us/en/p/maille-dijon-original-mustard-7-5-oz.html/00871256666689).

Qualification: Prepared-condiment context retained; no narrowing to Dijon or new seed/powder equivalence. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### tomato-sauce

Priority: Frequent prepared ingredient with regional formulation ambiguity. Corpus occurrences: 24.

A tomato-based sauce used to bring tomato flavour and liquid to a dish. The cited canned example is simmered with salt and spices; it illustrates a cooking ingredient rather than a single universal sauce recipe.

Read the recipe context and product label. Seasoning, sweetness and consistency vary, so tomato sauce should not silently be treated as concentrated paste or ketchup. This page preserves the broad existing term without declaring one regional packaged product to be its only meaning.

Sources: [Tomato Sauce](https://www.hunts.com/tomato-sauce-and-paste/tomato-sauce).

Qualification: Regional scope remains explicit; no universal sugar or seasoning formulation. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### mayonnaise

Priority: Common sauce; explain the mixing structure. Corpus occurrences: 23.

A thick emulsified sauce made by dispersing oil into an egg-yolk mixture with acidic ingredients. Its texture comes from the combined mixture rather than from oil alone.

The Culinary Institute of America method adds oil gradually while whisking. That example explains the structure, not a guarantee that every commercial or egg-free alternative has the same formulation. Use a suitable recipe and handling guidance rather than deriving a storage life from the name mayonnaise.

Sources: [Mayonnaise](https://www.ciafoodies.com/mayonnaise/).

Qualification: No preservation claim or universal ingredient/allergen guarantee. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### mushrooms

Priority: Common broad food; avoid collapsing species. Corpus occurrences: 23.

Edible fungi used in many forms and species. Common cultivated examples include button, crimini, portobello and shiitake; the general word does not identify a single mushroom variety.

The variety and preparation affect the dish, so follow a named type when one is specified. This ingredient page is not a wild-mushroom identification guide. Use mushrooms supplied as edible food, and do not infer that an unfamiliar specimen is safe from a superficial resemblance.

Sources: [Mushroom — FoodLink](https://www.extension.purdue.edu/foodlink/food.php?food=mushroom).

Qualification: No foraging identification, universal raw-use permission or species merge. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### red-onion

Priority: Frequent colour-specific allium; qualify flavour expectations. Corpus occurrences: 21.

A red-coloured bulb onion used raw or cooked. Colour is one way onions are described, alongside shape and pungency; it does not fully specify the onion’s flavour.

Choose a sound, firm bulb and cut it for the intended dish. Some bulb onions are sweeter and others stronger, so red does not guarantee mildness. This entry remains distinct from the broader onion page and does not prescribe an equal-volume substitute for every allium.

Sources: [Onion, green onion, scallion — FoodLink](https://www.extension.purdue.edu/foodlink/food.php?food=onion%2C+green+onion%2C+scallion).

Qualification: Colour is not a universal sweetness rating. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### turmeric

Priority: Frequent spice; keep culinary claims separate from health claims. Corpus occurrences: 20.

A seasoning known for its strong yellow colour and earthy flavour. Ground turmeric is used in rice, vegetable preparations, pickles and other dishes where both colour and seasoning matter.

The cited ground product illustrates a common cooking form. Read the recipe’s form and quantity rather than assuming that fresh material and powder behave identically. Its contribution is not merely decorative, and this page makes no medicinal claim or fresh-to-ground conversion.

Sources: [Ground Turmeric](https://www.mccormickasia.com/products/turmeric-ground).

Qualification: Generic turmeric identity not narrowed to the separate turmeric-powder entry. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### chicken-broth

Priority: Common liquid; explain use without imposing rigid stock boundaries. Corpus occurrences: 19.

A chicken-flavoured cooking liquid used in soups and to add flavour and moisture to other dishes. Broth commonly includes meat and aromatics simmered in water, though formulations vary.

Stock often emphasises bones and body, but the terms overlap in practice. Use the actual product or preparation specified by the recipe; the label alone does not guarantee a particular concentration, seasoning level or cooking duration. No automatic substitution ratio follows from the comparison.

Sources: [Broth vs. Stock vs. Bone Broth](https://www.campbells.com/swanson/broth-vs-stock-vs-bone-broth/); [A No-Rules Guide for Rich Chicken Stock](https://www.ciafoodies.com/a-no-rules-guide-for-rich-chicken-stock/).

Qualification: Stock/broth distinction is practical, not a new strict identity rule. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### sour-cream

Priority: Common dairy ingredient; distinguish tang from whipping cream. Corpus occurrences: 19.

Cream cultured to develop a tangy flavour and a spoonable texture. It is used in dips, dressings and as a topping, adding acidity as well as dairy richness.

Reduced-fat versions may have a different consistency. Sour cream is not simply another name for unsoured whipping cream, so a replacement can change both texture and flavour. The cited dairy guide explains the product family rather than prescribing a home fermentation process.

Sources: [Cream](https://www.dairy.com.au/products-and-recipes/dairy-products/cream).

Qualification: No fermentation schedule, universal fat percentage or substitution guarantee. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### worcestershire-sauce

Priority: Common compound condiment; qualify product ingredients. Corpus occurrences: 19.

A concentrated seasoning sauce combining savoury, acidic and sweet flavours. The cited Lea & Perrins example includes vinegar, molasses, tamarind and anchovies, and is used in marinades and other savoury preparations.

Check the actual product when ingredients matter: the familiar name does not guarantee an anchovy-free or otherwise identical formulation. Small additions season a dish rather than supplying its main liquid. This product example does not make the generic entry brand-specific.

Sources: [The Original Worcestershire Sauce](https://www.kraftheinz.com/lea-perrins/products/00051600000037-the-original-worcestershire-sauce).

Qualification: Product example only; no universal allergen or dietary suitability assertion. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### heavy-cream

Priority: Common cream label; explain whipping behaviour. Corpus occurrences: 18.

A rich dairy cream used as a liquid ingredient and for whipping. Beating it incorporates air to make a topping or a lighter component for desserts; the liquid and whipped forms occupy different volumes.

Begin with cold cream for whipping and watch its texture as it thickens. Further beating can take it beyond the intended stage. The name alone does not make every regional cream product equivalent, and a measure of liquid cream is not a measure of finished whipped cream.

Sources: [How to make whipped cream](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2015/07/19/how-to-whip-cream).

Qualification: No regional fat-percentage mapping or automatic volume conversion. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### puff-pastry

Priority: Common prepared dough; explain lamination and handling. Corpus occurrences: 18.

A layered pastry in which dough and fat are repeatedly folded and rolled. During baking, steam helps separate those layers, producing the characteristic lifted, flaky structure.

Handle thawed pastry while it is still cold and pliable. Compressing cut edges can interfere with the rise. Commercial sheets may use different fats and dimensions, so follow the product and recipe rather than assuming every puff pastry is all-butter or the same size.

### sesame

Priority: Frequently used seed with whole and ground forms. Corpus occurrences: 5.

Small seeds used for their nutty flavour and texture. Whole sesame adds a fine crunch to breads, coatings and garnishes, while ground sesame contributes a different texture.

Toasting develops the seed’s aroma. Keep whole, toasted and ground instructions distinct: a scattering of seeds does not behave like a smooth paste. The general name does not establish whether the seeds are hulled or specify one particular colour.

Sources: [About Sesame Seeds Uses, Pairings and Recipes](https://www.mccormick.com/blogs/how-to/about-sesame-seeds-uses-pairings-and-recipes).

Qualification: No whole-to-paste conversion or fixed colour. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

### vegetable-oil

Priority: Frequent generic cooking fat; product composition matters. Corpus occurrences: 5.

An oil made from plant ingredients, commonly sold as a liquid cooking fat. The cited vegetable oil is soybean oil, illustrating one product rather than defining the whole category.

Read the bottle when a recipe needs a particular flavour or cooking application. Vegetable oil is not a promise of one plant source or one blend. A measured liquid oil also behaves differently from a solid fat when mixed into dough or batter.

Sources: [Pure Vegetable Oil](https://crisco.com/products/pure-vegetable-oil/).

Qualification: Manufacturer example does not establish universal composition. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

A prepared dry seasoning mixture. The cited example combines salt, garlic, pepper and herbs or spices for seasoning meat and vegetables.

This pantry use of adobo describes a blend, not a single spice. Check the actual formula and its salt contribution before adding further seasoning. Adobo seasoning should not be assumed to supply the liquid or texture of an adobo sauce, or to define every dish called adobo.

A term used for broth and for concentrated products that supply broth-like flavour. Pantry forms include cubes, powders and pastes; the cited producer makes concentrated bases.

Identify the form before measuring. A spoonful of concentrate is not a spoonful of prepared broth, and products may contribute substantial seasoning as well as flavour. Follow the recipe and product’s dilution instructions rather than treating all bouillon as ready-to-use liquid.

Sources: [About Better Than Bouillon](https://www.betterthanbouillon.com/about-us/).

Qualification: No fixed dilution, salt content or strict broth boundary. Review: provisional 0.1; no human review.

The outer covering of a lemon. The coloured outer layer supplies aromatic zest, while the white pith beneath it can contribute bitterness.

Sources: [Fruit and Vegetable Guide: lemons](https://extension.usu.edu/nutrition/research/lemons).

A fat used to help produce tender or flaky baked textures. In contemporary pantry use, shortening commonly refers to a solid vegetable-fat product, though the culinary term has a broader history.

Corn harvested for eating as a vegetable, with kernels that may be yellow, white or a mixture. It can be prepared on the cob or as loose kernels.

          "value": "<p>Organic broccoli from Tuscarora Organic Growers (TOG) was delivered to Each Peach Market in the Washington, D.C., on Tuesday Aug 2, 2016. # Knowledge Images — Batch 1

Date: 24 October 2026. Local content-only image tranche.

Thirty existing ingredient reference pages gain their first photograph. Image-bearing knowledge pages increase from 19 to 49; 862 of the 911 independently enrichable pages remain without images. All 911 retain their existing editorial enrichment. No identities, aliases, recipes, source text, parser behaviour or renderer styling changed.

## Selection and licensing

The first batch favours recognisable produce and herbs. Each selected Commons image has image-specific licence metadata, creator credit, source-page and original-file URLs, and an acquisition URL recorded in the [decision ledger](knowledge-images-batch-1.json). Credits render visibly through the existing reference renderer and are also retained in [image attribution](../assets/references/ATTRIBUTION.md). CC BY-SA derivatives retain their source licence; photographs are not relicensed under the knowledge-data CC0 grant. Public-domain USDA images retain their agency/source credit; the green-bean source does not identify an individual photographer.

All selected full frames were visually inspected. Rejected search candidates included leek flowers, a musician named Scallions, non-bell peppers, and ambiguous bean imagery. No restricted noncommercial or GFDL-only option was selected. Existing 19 images and their credits remain intact.

## Optimisation

Progressive JPEG, quality 82, optimised encoding, no crop, maximum 960 pixels on the longest edge, no upscaling. Embedded metadata is removed while attribution is retained separately. New image bytes: **3,912,715** (about 3.91 MB; average 130 KB). The largest is below 300 KB. Original-resolution masters and rejected candidates are not added to the repository.

        "ImageDescription": {
          "value": "A star anise with a seed on cinnamon sticks. \"Illicium verum is a medium-sized evergreen tree native to northeast Vietnam and southwest China. A spice commonly called star anise, staranise, star anise seed, Chinese star anise, or badian that closely resembles anise in flavor is obtained from the star-shaped pericarps of the fruit of I. verum which are harvested just before ripening. Star anise oil is a highly fragrant oil used in cooking, perfumery, soaps, toothpastes, mouthwashes, and skin creams. About 90% of the world's star anise crop is used for extraction of shikimic acid, a chemical intermediate used in the synthesis of oseltamivir (Tamiflu).  Star anise contains anethole, the same compound that gives the unrelated anise its flavor. Recently, star anise has come into use in the West as a less expensive substitute for anise in baking, as well as in liquor production, most distinctively in the production of the liqueur Galliano.Star anise enhances the flavour of meat.  It is used as a spice in preparation of biryani and masala chai all over the Indian subcontinent. It is widely used in Chinese cuisine, and in Malay and Indonesian cuisines. It is widely grown for commercial use in China, India, and most other countries in Asia. Star anise is an ingredient of the traditional five-spice powder of Chinese cooking. It is also a major ingredient in the making of phở, a Vietnamese noodle soup.  It is also used in the French recipe of mulled wine, called vin chaud (hot wine). If allowed to steep in coffee, it deepens and enriches the flavor. The pods can be used in this manner multiple times by the pot-full or cup, as the ease of extraction of the taste components increases with the permeation of hot water.\" (Wikipedia)",

# Knowledge images — batch 2

100 existing ingredient pages now have reviewed, locally hosted photographs. Coverage rises from 49 to **149 of 911 enriched pages**, leaving **762** without images. No recipe, canonical identity, relationship, resource or knowledge prose was changed.

The new assets total **11,293,827 bytes (10.8 MiB)**. Each is an optimised progressive JPEG, quality 82, at most 960 pixels on its longest edge and below 350 KB. Full frames are retained without upscaling. Sources are Wikimedia Commons file records with public-domain, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA licensing; exact versions and ports are preserved. Creator credit, original source, licence link, caption, dimensions, derivative notice and checksum are recorded for every image in [the ledger](knowledge-images-batch-2.json) and [asset attribution](../assets/references/ATTRIBUTION.md).

## Selection and limitations

All 100 selected frames were inspected. Misleading search results were rejected, including decorative milk glass, a band logo for cream, an unsuitable bean variety, a different herb returned for oregano, a black-and-white art photograph for green bell pepper, and noodles merely served with egg. The chosen egg-noodle photograph is a prepared dish, labelled accordingly. Botanical herb photographs show flowering plants where appropriate; captions do not claim to show detached culinary leaves. The salmon photograph shows drying sockeye fillets; the mushroom assortment is explicitly not an identification guide. Photographs illustrate the captioned subject, not every variety or preparation represented by an identity.

No licence is inferred from a search-result title. File-specific Commons metadata is retained in the ledger. Public-domain records without a separate licence URL link to their source licensing section. Existing uncertain historical creator attribution is retained rather than invented. Embedded image metadata is removed, while credit remains visible on the page and in the ledger.

## Validation

- Core: type checking, build, 1,288 tests, documentation links and quality audit passed. The existing 10 sample quality findings remain unchanged.
- Corpus: 395 tests and 490 recipe parses passed; no Corpus source changes.
- Site: type checking, 128 tests, build and validation passed: 1,667 pages, 1,973 files, 66,611 internal links and 2,450 fragments.
- Regression tests pin all 100 image checksums and metadata, preserve the complete previous enrichment registry after removing only these new hero fields, and verify all canonical files, resources and previous image files remain unchanged. Historical batch expectations retain their original snapshots.
- Clean-source export audit passed: 1,389 files, 969 knowledge entries and 14 samples; unrelated user files and ignored archives excluded.
- Ordinary localhost HTTP audit passed: all 1,667 HTML pages matched built bytes; all 100 new image URLs returned 200, image/jpeg and exact SHA-256 content, with captions and credits verified. Transient connection resets required bounded transport-only retries; no status/content assertion was relaxed.
- Documentation checks (30 documents) and Git whitespace checks passed. Core and Site changes are locally committed on codex/knowledge-images-batch-2; no merge, push or deployment.
- Visual review: contact sheets of all selections, plus an ordinary in-app browser spot-check of coconut showing its image, caption and expanded licence/credit. This is not a full browser suite or mobile/theme matrix.

# Knowledge images — batch 3

100 existing equipment pages receive reviewed, locally hosted photographs. Coverage rises from 149 to **249 of 911 enriched pages**, leaving **662** without images. Together, batches 2 and 3 add 200 images: 100 ingredient pages and 100 equipment pages. No recipe, canonical identity, relationship, resource or knowledge prose was changed.

The new equipment images total **9,304,362 bytes (8.9 MiB)**; both batches total **20,598,189 bytes (19.6 MiB)**. Images are full-frame progressive JPEGs at quality 82, at most 960 pixels on the longest edge, without upscaling and below 350 KB each. Embedded metadata is removed; attribution remains in the page, [asset credits](../assets/references/ATTRIBUTION.md) and [machine-readable ledger](knowledge-images-batch-3.json). File-specific Commons metadata records creator, original file, source page and exact licence version/port. Only public-domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA images were selected.

## Selection and limitations

All 100 images were visually inspected. Wikipedia lead-image discovery was only a starting point; the Commons file record supplies licensing and each image was checked for the actual equipment. Rejected candidates included an unrelated herb/seed grinder for coffee, a champagne flute for a coupe, laboratory sieves, ordinary scissors for kitchen shears, a dish of pasta for a pasta machine, and a blender search result showing only a jug and drinks. An ice-cube-tray image lacking creator metadata was replaced with an attributed photograph.

Some photographs show tools in use rather than isolated product views: a rolling pin working flatbread, a mallet flattening pork, a fillet knife separating fish, a wok cooking noodles, and a ricer pressing potato. Captions state those contexts. The springform image illustrates its latch; the commercial ice-cream machine illustrates one scale of equipment; neither is presented as every version of the item. Brand markings visible within photographs are incidental, not endorsements. No additional cropping or artwork generation was used.

## Preservation and validation

Tests pin all 100 new images and their metadata, compare the complete prior enrichment registry after removing only these additions, and check canonical files, resources and all previous image bytes. Earlier batch tests retain their original historical counts and hashes through explicit later-batch projections.

- Core: type checking, build, 1,389 tests, documentation checks (31 documents) and quality audit passed. The existing 10 sample quality findings remain unchanged.
- Corpus: 395 tests and all 490 recipe parses passed; Corpus sources unchanged.
- Site: type checking, 128 tests, build and validation passed: 1,667 pages, 2,073 files, 66,711 internal links and 2,450 fragments.
- Clean-source audit passed: 1,492 files, 969 knowledge entries and 14 samples. Unrelated user files and ignored archives were excluded and left untouched.
- Ordinary localhost HTTP audit passed: all 1,667 pages matched built HTML; all 100 equipment image URLs returned 200, image/jpeg and exact saved SHA-256 bytes, with captions and attribution verified. One transient connection reset was retried without relaxing any assertion.
- All selected images were visually reviewed. An in-app browser spot-check of mortar and pestle confirmed the image, caption and expanded credit/licence disclosure. This is not a full browser suite or mobile/theme matrix.
- Git whitespace checks passed. Core and Site changes are locally committed on codex/knowledge-images-batch-3; no merge, push or deployment.

# Knowledge images — batch 4

100 more existing ingredient pages now have locally hosted, attributed images. Coverage rises from 249 to **349 of 911 enriched pages**, leaving **562** without images. This batch changes image metadata and assets only: no recipe, canonical identity, relationship, resource or knowledge prose changes.

The new files total **11,440,568 bytes (10.9 MiB)**. Each is an optimised progressive JPEG at quality 82, at most 960 pixels on its longest edge, without upscaling and below 350 KB. Full source frames are retained. Embedded metadata is removed; credits remain visible on the page and in the [asset attribution](../assets/references/ATTRIBUTION.md) and [batch ledger](knowledge-images-batch-4.json).

## Curation

All selected images were inspected visually. Wikimedia Commons file-specific metadata records the creator, source page, original file URL, exact licence version and jurisdiction where applicable. Licences are public domain, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA. Public-domain files without a separate licence URL link to the source licensing section. Wikipedia article lead images were only a discovery aid, not sufficient evidence of subject suitability or licensing.

Unsuitable lead images were rejected, including chemical structures for baking soda/sugar, an ear of rye for rye flour, bread for sourdough starter, whole chickens for specific chicken cuts, live animals for meat cuts and finished curry for curry paste. One Shaoxing-wine download remained rate-limited after bounded retries; that page was deferred and an already downloaded, reviewed crab-meat photograph was selected instead. No access restriction was bypassed.

# Culinary knowledge

Knowledge connects authored recipe words to shared culinary concepts without changing the recipe source. Ingredients, equipment and processes have stable IDs. The files in knowledge/ are grouped by domain; each index.yaml explicitly identifies canonical entries. Unindexed legacy files are evidence, not additional runtime concepts.

## Identity and names

An entry has `id`, `kind` and locale-keyed `names`, with optional `canonical_name`, `plural_names` and explicit `aliases`. Aliases can be strings or named records with locale/evidence. Only explicit aliases participate in resolution. Observed phrases, qualifiers and parameters are evidence, never aliases merely because they occurred in a recipe. Prefer a small number of meaningful concepts over duplicate IDs, while retaining useful names.

`curation.origin` describes manual/generated provenance; `curation.review` describes checked/unchecked review. These axes are independent. Retain sources and qualify uncertainty. Quantitative values require units, basis and source context; do not invent nutrition, density or typical mass from incidental recipes.

## Relationships, parts and states

`type_of` expresses an explicit semantic subtype relationship for ingredients/equipment. It is not a browsing category. Parent and child concepts remain distinct; aliases are not a substitute for relations. Relationships must target valid concepts and must not form cycles.

Ingredient `parts` may nest. Part paths keep the parent context; `part_groups` describe named groupings and associated processes. A reference to egg yolk targets the egg concept and its yolk anchor, not an invented separate ingredient. Unknown suffixes remain authored text.

Preparation `states` annotate explicitly recognised authored qualifiers. They do not create implicit transformations, nutritional equivalence or automatic transitions. Parts, types and preparation are different concepts. Ordinary descriptive qualifiers remain text.

Equipment subtype relationships express identity, not suitability guarantees. Processes resolve action heads while retaining authored context; nested ingredient/equipment/result references belong to that context. Do not absorb whole instructions into canonical names.

## Reference eligibility and local roles

`reference: false` preserves a known concept without giving it a shared reference page. Local ingredient roles/choices can remain unresolved and still have ingredient semantics. Colour follows semantic role; links and underline require an actual shared target. Reference eligibility is separate from vocabulary membership.

## Contributing data

Follow the adjacent entries and the typed model in src/vocabulary/index.ts for exact field shapes; tests exercise validation and rendering. Keep IDs stable, update the domain index deliberately and run core checks. The Node loader takes the directory containing ingredients/equipment/processes; pass knowledge/ in this repository. Its generic root contract is unchanged.

Ingredients, processes and equipment may have optional multi-valued `categories` for human browsing. The shared registry in src/vocabulary/categories.ts defines stable IDs, domain eligibility, display names, descriptions and display order. Unknown, cross-domain and duplicate assignments are rejected; missing or empty categories remain valid. Categories never supply aliases, inheritance, type_of, substitution, regional equivalence, parser legality or inferred recipe usage. Processes may also have a concise `scope` explanation. A public process page may have discovery value or explanation value, including regional or contextual ambiguity. Bare temper and proof remain unaliased because resolution is not context-scoped.

Historical evidence paths inside unchanged knowledge records are corpus-relative provenance identifiers. Resolve examples/public-domain-recipes paths against the full corpus project, not the curated core sample. The extraction deliberately does not rewrite evidence or identities.

## Ingredient naming, authoring locale and identity

Canonical English ingredient names use UK culinary English by default where genuinely competing English names exist: aubergine, courgette and icing sugar. This is an editorial convention, not an automatic rename rule. Culturally specific names such as gochujang, miso and paneer retain their natural names.

Optional `locale: en-GB` or `locale: en-US` belongs in `::recipe`. The model retains the authored locale and source text; resolution uses the locale without changing spelling. Invalid or repeated locale metadata produces a warning and is not applied. Absent locale preserves legacy resolution. Reader locale is a separate, future global presentation preference; no reader UI or automatic translation is introduced.

Ingredient entries may add scoped exact names:

```yaml
exact_names:
  - name: powdered sugar
    locale: en-US
    scope: Exact regional culinary name.
```

An omitted locale accepts the name everywhere. A language scope such as en includes en-GB and en-US; a regional scope such as en-US does not include en-GB. Scope prose is editorial, not a matching predicate. Without authoring locale, all potentially matching exact names are considered: multiple identities remain ambiguous rather than selecting by order. Existing names, plural names and aliases retain their historical unscoped matching, including locale-keyed display labels. Use exact_names for new interpretation-sensitive regional names. Canonical IDs remain stable lookup keys.

The resolver API accepts locale as the fourth argument to `resolveIngredient(name, variant, parts, locale)` (or the third to `resolve(term, kind, locale)`). Cilantro continues to identify coriander leaves only, never seeds or roots.

### Regional comparisons are not aliases

`regional_mappings` records comparisons separately. Each record has a name, relation, optional locale, scope, canonical ingredient target and sources (citation plus optional URL, accessed date and note). Relations are directional from this entry to the named target: exact, broader, narrower, overlapping, or approximate-equivalent. An approximate equivalent is a practical culinary comparison, not identical composition or an automatic substitution instruction. It may eventually display as ~.

All mapping records are descriptive and non-resolving, including research-only exact comparisons. Promote reviewed exact wording to exact_names to enable resolution. Broader, narrower, overlapping and approximate-equivalent mappings never supply aliases. The focused tests demonstrate separate UK/US sirloin concepts and a plain-flour/all-purpose-flour comparison; they are model fixtures, not an authoritative cut crosswalk or a claim of exact flour formulation equivalence.

Self-rising flour remains accepted for backwards compatibility with existing authored recipes. Its former en-US display-name entry is now an explicit legacy alias carrying a warning; recipe resolution reports INGREDIENT_COMPATIBILITY. A separate approximate-equivalent mapping records the regional comparison with formulation equivalence unestablished. This grandfathered resolver exception must not be used as a precedent for adding new non-exact aliases. Self-raising flour and the old unhyphenated spelling remain unchanged.

### Promoted names and nested parts

The retained egg-yolk and egg-white entries declare `canonical_target: { ingredient: egg, parts: [yolk] }` (or white). Semantic ingredient resolution normalises both the compound name and structured part syntax to egg plus the same part path. Authored names and parts are unchanged. Targets must reference an existing canonical part path; chains and cycles are rejected.

Low-level entry lookup retains the old IDs for compatibility, but recipe links and usage analytics use the normalised egg-part target. Reference projections expose canonicalTarget; compatibility pages project the same part backlinks, while egg retains nested-part navigation. This preserves old accepted forms without maintaining two independent semantic targets. exactNames and regionalMappings are also available in the reference data projection; presentation is left to consumers.

## Reference enrichment

Optional knowledge/enrichment.yaml contains content records targeting existing canonical kind/ID pairs; knowledge/resources.yaml stores shared sources once. The six initial exemplars are brown-sugar, egg, emulsify, sear, chef-knife and frying-pan. These registries do not alter the domain indexes or resolver identities. The Node loader reads them from the supplied knowledge root and still accepts legacy roots without them. Programmatic consumers can use `new Vocabulary(entries, {resources, enrichments})`; transport all three collections when enrichment is needed.

An enrichment record contains review_version and optional editorial, resources, associations and measurements arrays. Plain-text editorial blocks have stable IDs and typed roles (summary, purpose, mechanism, sensory, uses, storage, judgement, mistakes, selection, care, context and near-neighbours), optional source IDs and their own review_version. Rendering escapes text, uses the fixed role order, preserves authored order within a role and omits empty sections. It never executes authored HTML or interprets prose as parser rules. Existing observation evidence stays separate.

### Writing and selection guidance

Before research, verify canonical existence, public-reference eligibility, absence of duplicate enrichment and fit with the current model. A canonical entry with reference:false is not a candidate public page.

As editorial guidance, ingredient ::about openings use two sentences: first identify what the ingredient is, then explain its culinary use. Process ::about starts with a direct definition; ::purpose explains the intended result and ::how it works explains the mechanism or method. Equipment ::about should identify the object, then explain its common use in a second sentence. Existing pages may not yet follow this convention. Use original, source-supported prose rather than copied definitions. Keep identity separate from advice and avoid taxonomy that does not help the cook.

Depth follows explanatory need. Short concepts stay short; complex methods need useful distinctions and scoped evidence. Do not pad pages to match a template. Every new statement retains review_version 0.1 and appropriate sources; generated content is not human reviewed. Check source scope and publication eligibility before investing in optional images. Images may be omitted when finding a suitable, clearly licensed example would dominate the work.

### Content maturity

review_version is content maturity, not edit count, schema version, Git revision or publication version. Values from 0 inclusive to below 1 are draft/generated; 1 means basic human review, 2 deeper subject/source review, and 3 mature/expert review. Other values are rejected. Integer advancement requires explicit human review; an edit or automated check is not that review. Current enrichment is 0.1 throughout, displayed as “Version 0.1 — machine generated, not yet human reviewed”. The 1/2/3 levels describe future reviewed maturity, not a claim that such pages currently exist. An entry's enrichment maturity is independent of existing canonical identity curation. Evidence-bearing blocks, resource attachments, associations and measurements carry their own maturity; optional reviewed_at uses an ISO calendar date. Display labels are derived, not stored as a second maturity enum.

### Sources and contextual links

Resources have stable ID, title, HTTPS URL, publisher, type, checked_at and review_scope; optional notes, commercial context and known video duration retain limitations. A landing-page check does not mean a video was watched. Omit unknown duration. URLs reject credentials, whitespace, backslashes and non-HTTPS schemes. Resources are attached with learning role, explicit order, contextual note and review_version. Multiple roles/resources are allowed; ties retain authored order. Educational ordering is not an affiliate ranking. No external media is copied.

Associations support commonly-used-with, used-for and contrast-with. Targets contain kind, canonical id and optional canonical ingredient parts. All targets and source IDs are validated. Use egg plus [yolk] or [white], not legacy compatibility IDs, for new evidence-bearing targets. These discovery links do not create aliases, family inheritance, mandatory dependencies, substitutions or recipe backlinks. Actual usage still comes only from resolved recipe tokens in the supplied index. A 14-recipe core sample must not be represented as the full corpus.

### Culinary measurement observations

Measurement records preserve a stable ID, canonical ingredient target, optional product_scope, condition, original source observation, source ID and optional locator/accessed date. Condition describes measuring practice (for example packed), separately from an ingredient preparation state. The unit for a normalised culinary/bulk density is g/mL. value is optional until justified; approximate, uncertainty.basis, normalisation, review_version and conversion_eligible are explicit. Optional positive lower/upper bounds must contain the representative value and have a stated non-unknown basis. Unknown uncertainty has no invented zero-width interval. Optional reference_temperature_c preserves source context; no thermal model is implied.

An executable record requires conversion_eligible true, review_version at least 1, positive representative density and explicit source_volume_ml establishing the original volume basis. That field is evidence, not a reader setting. A directly sourced g/mL density can declare a 1 mL source basis. These checks cannot replace human verification of the source and method. Legacy reference_density remains unchanged and is never automatically promoted into this contract.

The pure convertIngredientMeasurement helper accepts validated observations and an explicit canonical target, amount, from/to units, condition and optional product scope. It converts volume to grams or grams to volume; a g-to-g request bypasses density. Conditions match exactly; scoped records require the matching product scope. Cup/tablespoon/teaspoon mL definitions must be supplied explicitly, independently of authoring locale. Presentation values in cups or tablespoons are derived from the observation and chosen unit basis; canonical culinary/bulk density remains g/mL. No match, missing unit basis or multiple applicable records returns a reason rather than a guess. The conservative selection policy rejects multiple applicable observations even when one is provisional: editorial selection is required. Source approximation, unknown uncertainty and ranges propagate approximation. formatMeasurement provides modest approximate display precision; arithmetic results remain separate. General unit conversion and reader UI are outside this helper.

The brown-sugar observation retains the published 213 g per packed cup, but has no value or source_volume_ml and remains conversion-ineligible. No 236.6/240/250 mL assumption is made. Other conditions or product scopes receive no inferred density. Provisional evidence renders distinctly from eligible observations; eligible does not mean every recipe request is applicable.

Nutrition, dietary guarantees, automatic substitution, full translation/taxonomy, commerce, thermal modelling, process execution and global Reading settings UI remain deferred. Core reference projection and escaped HTML expose the new content without modifying the sibling site or inferring usage from associations.

Reference enrichment may optionally include `hero` metadata: a local `references/` asset,
source page/file, creator, licence and licence URL, attribution, alt text, dimensions,
review date and derivative changes. Images never determine publication eligibility.
The host supplies `heroUrl` when rendering and copies the corresponding asset locally;
without that callback the image is omitted. Image selection evidence and separate
third-party terms live in `assets/references/`. Image review dates do not promote
culinary content maturity.

Enriched reference pages show the page review version in a banner, retaining field
versions in data and displaying them only when different or inside provenance.
The `::` section labels are presentation, not recipe grammar. Image credits,
measurement evidence and source-check scope remain available in expandable details;
canonical identity metadata and part anchors are retained.

### Browsing categories v1

Categories answer where a cook would look, not what an ingredient biologically is. Membership is explicit and never inherited through families or parts. For example, brown-sugar belongs to sugars-and-sweeteners and baking-ingredients; hand-mixer belongs to mixing and appliances. The ingredient registry includes nuts-and-seeds alongside the initial practical food groups. Existing process category IDs are retained: mixing-and-emulsifying displays as Mixing & aeration, preparation-and-cutting as Preparation & knife skills; coating-and-breading and fire-and-smoke remain useful distinct groups. The exported processCategories API remains available.

The site exposes non-empty public category pages at /ingredients/category/{id}/, /processes/category/{id}/ and /equipment/category/{id}/ beneath its configured base path. Counts are public reference entries, not assignment totals; recipe usage remains the existing count of distinct explicit recipe uses. A–Z always includes uncategorised public entries. reference:false never gains a page through membership. Enrichment remains a separate optional layer.

## Authored commercial selection

Ingredient tokens may carry `product: { name, strength, raw, span }`, with strength `specified`, `approximate` or `exact`. This is recipe occurrence data, not an ingredient vocabulary field. See [commercial selection syntax](../SPEC.md#commercial-product-and-expression-selection). A product label and an ingredient type/part remain separate; resolution of the culinary identity does not consume the product name. There is no product registry, inferred brand hierarchy, alias or substitution rule in v1. HTML reference links continue to identify the culinary ingredient.

### Cocktail foundation prose

Optional `types` and `brands` editorial roles provide explanatory prose. `::types` describes culinary styles/types/subtypes. `::brands` optionally describes representative commercial products or expressions where formulation matters. Brands are not types, a listing is not automatically a recommendation, and products in one broad category may differ greatly. This is not a shopping or affiliate ranking list; it creates no inferred equivalence or resolver aliases. These roles do not create canonical types or commercial identities. All new cocktail enrichment is version 0.1 and remains machine generated and not human reviewed. The existing Beverages, Beverage & bar and Coffee & bar browsing categories are reused.

### equipment: steaming-basket

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. The basket supports food above the water while allowing steam through; a lid and suitable pan complete the cooking arrangement. A colander can drain food, but that alone does not establish that it fits a covered pan or is suitable for heating.

### equipment: thermometer

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. The measurement location matters as much as the display. An appliance thermometer describes the surrounding cooking environment; a food probe describes the region around its sensing area. These readings answer different questions, so an oven reading does not replace a measurement within the food.

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Thin, repeated vegetable slices are useful in fermented-vegetable preparation as well as salads. Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Covering a roasting vessel changes how moisture escapes and introduces a trapped-steam environment. Browning an exposed surface and retaining moisture under a lid are different aims; a recipe may deliberately move between them.

### process: braise

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. A covered cooking stage and an uncovered sauce-finishing stage can belong to the same dish. Removing the lid encourages evaporation; this explains why the sauce may be reduced separately after the food is tender.

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Kneading develops a dough’s structure; pastry lamination preserves distinct layers of dough and fat through rolling and folding. Both involve working dough, but continuous mixing is not a substitute for the layer-building operation.

### process: reduce

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Adding a thickener and evaporating water can both change consistency, but they do not do the same work. Reduction removes liquid rather than adding body to it. A recipe’s target volume and its texture cue should therefore be read together.

Evidence: [Culinary Institute of America: Lid or No Lid?](https://www.ciafoodies.com/lid-or-no-lid/). Status: 0.1 draft/generated. Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

### process: poach

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Deep poaching fully surrounds the food with cooking liquid. The liquid can contribute flavour through stock, aromatics or wine, while a serving sauce may be prepared separately. Poaching does not require turning all of the cooking liquid into the final sauce.

Evidence: [Culinary Institute of America: Deep Poaching: A Healthy Technique for Delicious Foods](https://www.ciafoodies.com/deep-poaching-a-healthy-technique-for-delicious-foods/). Status: 0.1 draft/generated. Editorial comparison; no universal operating limits inferred.

### process: score

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Surface scoring and dough docking both make openings, but docking uses small punctures to limit puffing. Do not treat a decorative or expansion-guiding slash as equivalent to pricking the dough across its surface.

### process: blind-bake

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Docking controls puffing by making small holes; blind-baking cooks an empty pastry case. They can occur together, but one is a preparation and the other a baking stage. Docking a crust does not mean that it has already been blind-baked.

Improved existing draft; no earlier content removed. Fermentation names the microbial transformation, not a promise that living organisms remain in the finished food. Later processing can change that. The process name alone does not establish a product’s storage conditions or a health benefit.

## Existing drafts improved

- **equipment/scraper:** A bench knife can portion a dough into pieces before shaping. The scraper name alone does not specify a cutting edge suitable for that job; choose the rigid bench form when portioning is the task. Source: [King Arthur Baking: Bench Knife](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/bench-knife). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/grater:** A rasp form gives access to a small curved surface such as citrus peel. That access is a separate consideration from the size of its teeth; grater shape and the fineness of the result are not the same property. Source: [Microplane: Premium Classic Zester Grater](https://www.microplaneintl.com/en/our-products/premium-classic-series/zester-grater). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/zester:** A rasp-style zester can also grate hard cheese. This overlap explains why zesting tools appear among graters without making every grater a tool for removing only the outer citrus peel. Source: [Microplane: Premium Classic Zester Grater](https://www.microplaneintl.com/en/our-products/premium-classic-series/zester-grater). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/pasta-machine:** The roller description above concerns the sheet-making form. A separate cutter determines noodle width; changing roller thickness does not change the width of a cutter. Extrusion machines are another form of pasta machine, not another setting on a sheet roller. Source: [KitchenAid: Pasta Roller KSMPSA](https://www.kitchenaid.com/countertop-appliances/stand-mixers/attachments/p.pasta-roller.KSMPSA.html). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/rolling-pin:** End guides can limit the thickness of a dough sheet, but they do not guarantee a chosen diameter. If a dough portion reaches the guide thickness first, its final outline may remain smaller than the recipe requires. Source: [King Arthur Baking: The best rolling pin, based on what you like to bake](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2024/10/30/best-rolling-pin). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/kitchen-shears:** Snipping herbs, cutting kitchen twine and shaping parchment are different uses of the same shears. A pull-apart joint aids access for cleaning, but it is a design feature to check rather than a property of every pair. Source: [Williams Sonoma: WÜSTHOF Pull-Apart Shears](https://www.williams-sonoma.com/products/wusthof-pull-apart-kitchen-shears/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/chopping-board:** Deep grooves and excessive wear can make a board difficult to clean effectively. Cleaning routines do not remove that physical damage; USDA advises replacing worn boards with hard-to-clean grooves. Source: [USDA FSIS: Cutting Boards](https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/cutting-boards). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/knife:** Separate usable vegetable trim from waste as you cut. Squaring food for regular cuts creates offcuts that may suit stock or sauce; a precise presentation need not mean discarding all the remaining edible material. Source: [Culinary Institute of America / David Kamen: Five Knife Skills Every Chef Must Have!](https://www.ciachef.edu/blog/5-knife-skills-every-chef-must/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/paring-knife:** Peeling and trimming should remove the unwanted layer without taking an unnecessary amount of flesh. A short blade can work around small irregular areas; a large, tough rind calls for a different tool choice. Source: [Culinary Institute of America: Home School: Prepping Vegetables](https://www.ciafoodies.com/home-school-prepping-vegetables/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/sieve:** A support loop lets the illustrated strainer rest across a bowl while liquid drains. This support arrangement is separate from mesh fineness: both the opening size and how the sieve sits on the receiving vessel matter. Source: [OXO: 8-inch Double Rod Strainer](https://www.oxo.com/8-strainer.html). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/chop:** Rough chopping still benefits from reasonably similar piece sizes when the pieces will cook together. Irregular outlines and wildly different sizes are separate issues; a rustic cut need not mean uneven doneness. Source: [Culinary Institute of America: Home School: Prepping Vegetables](https://www.ciafoodies.com/home-school-prepping-vegetables/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/dice:** Brunoise is a particular small, regular dice. The general instruction to dice does not automatically request brunoise, so preserve any size cue in the recipe rather than inferring the finest cut. Source: [MICHELIN Guide / Rachel Tan: Kitchen Language: Know Your Knife Cuts](https://guide.michelin.com/en/article/dining-in/knife-cut-types). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/mince:** For herbs, an initial coarse cut can be followed by repeated cuts to reach the intended fineness. Mincing does not require preserving the regular faces of a dice; its endpoint is the small-piece texture required by the dish. Source: [Culinary Institute of America: Home School: Prepping Vegetables](https://www.ciafoodies.com/home-school-prepping-vegetables/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/julienne:** Cross-cutting julienned strips produces brunoise. Batonnet stops at a thicker stick; these names distinguish the resulting shapes and sizes, not different knives that must be purchased. Source: [MICHELIN Guide / Rachel Tan: Kitchen Language: Know Your Knife Cuts](https://guide.michelin.com/en/article/dining-in/knife-cut-types). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/slice:** Slicing can be an intermediate stage before sticks or dice. The first slices set one dimension of the later pieces, so inconsistent thickness at that stage carries through to the finished cut. Source: [Culinary Institute of America: Home School: Prepping Vegetables](https://www.ciafoodies.com/home-school-prepping-vegetables/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/grate:** Fine grating can distribute hard cheese or citrus peel as small particles rather than visible strips. A tool capable of both tasks does not make their ingredients interchangeable; the recipe still determines what is being grated. Source: [Microplane: Premium Classic Zester Grater](https://www.microplaneintl.com/en/our-products/premium-classic-series/zester-grater). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/zest:** Zesting keeps the coloured peel, whereas supreming citrus keeps the flesh and removes peel and segment membranes. These preparations use different parts of the fruit and should not be treated as alternate names for peeling. Source: [Noble Citrus: How to Cut Citrus for Salads with Chef Justin](https://noblecitrus.com/recipes/how-to-cut-citrus-for-salads-with-chef-justin/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/fold:** Folding pastry into layers during lamination is a different context from gently folding a foam mixture. A recipe must supply that context; repeated pastry folds are not an instruction to beat or stir a foam. Source: [King Arthur Baking: How we make puff pastry at the King Arthur bakery](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2013/08/02/puff-pastry-layer-it-like-the-pros). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/dock:** A dough docker repeats the puncturing action across a sheet. Its purpose differs from the continuous cut made by a pastry wheel: cutting the outline of a pastry piece does not dock its surface. Source: [Ateco: Ateco catalogue: pastry wheels and dough docker, pages 73–76](https://www.atecousa.com/assets/ateco_catalog.pdf). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/laminate:** Rolling sets the dimensions of the sheet between folds. A pin with thickness guides controls one dimension, not the full rectangle, so check the required shape as well as thickness when building layers. Source: [King Arthur Baking: The best rolling pin, based on what you like to bake](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2024/10/30/best-rolling-pin). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.

## Existing drafts improved

- **equipment/colander:** A colander receives food and liquid poured into it. A spider strainer instead lifts portions out of the cooking vessel, leaving most liquid in place. These are different ways to drain food, even if either can handle a large pasta shape. Source: [OXO: Scoop And Strain Skimmer](https://www.oxo.com/oxo-good-grips-scoop-and-strain-skimmer.html). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/steaming-basket:** Bamboo dim sum sets may combine several baskets and a separate cover. The basket, lid and water-heating vessel are distinct parts of the arrangement; selecting a basket alone does not establish the fit of the complete stack. Source: [Town Food Service: 3 Piece Bamboo Steamer Set](https://townfood.com/product/bamboo-steamer-set-3-piece/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/baking-paper:** Baking parchment can form a folded cooking parcel as well as line a tray. In a papillote, the joined edges help retain moisture; laying a loose sheet over food does not reproduce the same enclosure. Source: [Chef Simon: Pliage d’une papillote](https://chefsimon.com/gourmets/chef-simon/recettes/pliage-d-une-papillote). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/butchers-twine:** Twine can hold an external layer of fat against a roast during barding. Its role there is fastening the covering, whereas larding introduces fat into the meat itself. The same string can support different preparations without making them equivalent. Source: [Chef Simon: Barder](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-barder). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/pie-dish:** The dish supports the pastry through either a partial or a full preliminary bake. Which endpoint is needed depends on whether the filling will be baked later; the vessel alone does not determine that sequence. Source: [King Arthur Baking School: Holiday Pie Workbook: partial and full baking](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/content/class-pdfs/Holiday-Pie-Workbook-King-Arthur-Baking.pdf). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/pastry-brush:** Applying egg wash changes the finish of the dough surface. The brush distributes the chosen wash, but it does not determine its ingredients: retain the recipe’s wash composition rather than treating every brushing liquid as egg wash. Source: [King Arthur Baking School: Fruit Pies Workbook: egg wash](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/content/class-pdfs/Fruit-Pies-Workbook-King-Arthur-Baking.pdf). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/electric-kettle:** A stovetop kettle requires an external burner or hob; an electric kettle contains its own heating system. A whistling lid describes a signal mechanism, not a shared heating method or proof that the vessels can be exchanged between heat sources. Source: [Le Creuset: Classic Whistling Kettle](https://www.lecreuset.com/classic-whistling-kettle-matte-white/40114260431241.html). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/thermometer:** A stem thermometer may sense along a length of probe rather than only at its tip. The displayed number can therefore represent a region of food; follow the instrument’s sensing-area guidance instead of assuming that touching a point measures only that point. Source: [USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service: Food Thermometers](https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/food-thermometers). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/skewer:** In a tandoor, skewers support food within a deep heated chamber. That use needs a length and construction suited to the oven; a short serving pick and a cooking skewer do not become interchangeable because both are pointed rods. Source: [GULATI: Tandoori clay ovens](https://www.tandoors.com/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **equipment/food-mill:** Changing the perforated disc changes the texture of what passes through: the documented mill uses different discs for smooth sauces and coarser potato preparations. This is mechanical selection, not merely running the same blade for longer. Source: [OXO: Food Mill Use and Care](https://www.oxo.com/media/wysiwyg/PDF_Files/1071478_foodmill.pdf). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/blind-bake:** Par-baking also applies to foods such as bread rolls. Blind-baking describes the absence of the eventual filling, while par-baking describes an incomplete bake; an empty crust may be either partly or fully baked. Source: [King Arthur Baking: Homemade Brown and Serve Rolls](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/recipes/homemade-brown-and-serve-rolls-recipe). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/bake:** A cake’s surface colour, spring and interior crumb provide different cues. Inserting a tester inspects a small part of the crumb; read that result with the recipe’s other cues rather than treating one clean probe as a universal endpoint for every baked food. Source: [King Arthur Baking: How to tell when cake is done](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2019/07/01/how-to-tell-when-cake-is-done). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/fillet:** Pin-boning can follow the removal of a fillet. It removes small bones retained within the flesh rather than separating the main slab from the skeleton; the two operations belong to different stages of fish preparation. Source: [Taylor Foods / Direct Seafoods: Fish preparation and filleting guide](https://www.taylorfoods.co.uk/our-seafood/preparation/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/debone:** Fish pin-boning is one narrower deboning task. It can involve extracting individual small bones from an already cut fillet, unlike cutting an intact piece of meat away from a large central bone. Source: [Taylor Foods / Direct Seafoods: Fish preparation and filleting guide](https://www.taylorfoods.co.uk/our-seafood/preparation/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/steam:** A covered bamboo basket is one equipment arrangement for steaming. Its slatted base admits steam while holding the food; the basket is not immersed like the food in a pot of boiling water. Source: [Town Food Service: 3 Piece Bamboo Steamer Set](https://townfood.com/product/bamboo-steamer-set-3-piece/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/blanch:** A lifting strainer can remove a batch of food while retaining the blanching water in the pot. This differs from draining the whole pot through a colander and can be useful when the recipe calls for successive batches. Source: [OXO: Scoop And Strain Skimmer](https://www.oxo.com/oxo-good-grips-scoop-and-strain-skimmer.html). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/stir-fry:** Velveting can prepare a protein before the final stir-fry. The initial treatment and the later mixing with vegetables or sauce are separate stages; a finished stir-fry need not obtain all of its texture from the final toss in the wok. Source: [The Woks of Life: How to Velvet Chicken for Stir-fry](https://thewoksoflife.com/how-to-velvet-chicken-stir-fry/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/marinate:** A velveting marinade may include starch as part of a coating before cooking. This is a particular texture-oriented use of marinating, not a reason to add starch or baking soda to every marinade. Source: [The Woks of Life: How to Velvet Chicken for Stir-fry](https://thewoksoflife.com/how-to-velvet-chicken-stir-fry/). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/score:** Bread scoring creates planned places for a loaf’s surface to open during oven expansion. A bread lame provides a controlled blade for that purpose; scoring the surface does not divide the dough into separate portions. Source: [King Arthur Baking: Bread Slashing Lame](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/bread-slashing-lame). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
- **process/truss:** Trussing holds the shape of a bird, whereas tying on a bard holds an external covering of fat. Both can use kitchen twine, but the shared fastening tool does not make barding and trussing the same preparation. Source: [Chef Simon: Barder](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-barder). Existing draft improved; not newly human reviewed.
