## New identities

### larding-needle (equipment)

A tool for drawing strips of fat into meat during larding. Its purpose differs from a trussing needle, which carries thread to fasten a shape; neither is a generic synonym for every kitchen needle.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Larder](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-larder).

### fish-bone-tongs (equipment)

Gripping tongs designed to extract individual bones from fish flesh. The gripping edges grasp the bone rather than cut a fillet away from the skeleton. Shape and size vary; ordinary serving tongs are not necessarily suitable.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Subtype of tongs. Source: [Triangle Flat Edge Fish Bone Tongs](https://matferbourgeatusa.com/product/triangle-flat-edge-fish-bone-tongs/).

### oyster-knife (equipment)

A short, sturdy knife designed to open oyster shells. Its blade works at the shell joint rather than slicing a piece of food; the specialised construction should not be inferred from the word knife alone.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Subtype of knife. Source: [Oyster Knife](https://www.oxo.com/oyster-knife.html).

### cherry-pitter (equipment)

A tool that holds a cherry while a plunger pushes out its stone. Some designs also accommodate olives, but that capability does not make every fruit pitter interchangeable or establish an unrestricted olive-pitter alias.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Cherry & Olive Pitter](https://www.oxo.com/oxo-gg-cherry-and-olive-pitter-black.html).

### fat-separator (equipment)

A vessel that lets fat rise above cooking juices and dispenses the liquid beneath it. A lower outlet or suitable spout separates the layers; a top strainer removes solids, which is a different task from separating fat.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Good Gravy Fat Separator](https://www.oxo.com/good-gravy-fat-separator-4-cup.html).

### bulb-baster (equipment)

A tube with a squeezable bulb for drawing up cooking juices and releasing them over food. It transfers liquid onto the surface; it is not a syringe for injecting liquid into the interior.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Angled Baster With Cleaning Brush](https://www.oxo.com/angled-baster-with-cleaning-brush.html).

### egg-slicer (equipment)

A hinged slicer with a holder for an egg and a set of parallel cutting wires. It portions a cooked egg into slices; it does not separate raw egg white from yolk. Slice thickness depends on the tool.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [Egg Slicer](https://www.oxo.com/egg-slicer.html).

### julienne-peeler (equipment)

A hand tool with a divided cutting edge that draws narrow strips from vegetables. It produces strips rather than a broad peel; their dimensions depend on the blade, so the tool name does not promise a particular classical knife-cut size.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Subtype of vegetable-peeler. Source: [Julienne Peeler](https://www.oxo.com/shop/kitchenware/utensils/julienne-peeler.html).

### piping-tip (equipment)

A shaped outlet fitted to a piping bag. Round, star and other openings shape the material leaving the bag; the tip is distinct from the bag itself.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: piping nozzle. Source: [Ateco catalogue: pastry wheels and dough docker, pages 73–76](https://www.atecousa.com/assets/ateco_catalog.pdf).

### cake-turntable (equipment)

A rotating platform that supports a cake during decoration. Rotation brings successive surfaces within reach without repeatedly lifting the cake.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: revolving cake stand. Source: [Ateco catalogue: pastry wheels and dough docker, pages 73–76](https://www.atecousa.com/assets/ateco_catalog.pdf).

### tart-ring (equipment)

An open-bottomed frame supporting the sides of a tart or assembled pastry. It needs a separate supporting surface beneath it; it is not a pie dish with an integral base. Ring dimensions and shapes vary.

Category: bakeware. Aliases: none. Source: [Matfer Bourgeat catalogue: frames and rings, page 49](https://matferbourgeatusa.com/catalog-2019/Matfer_Bourgeat_Inc_2019_Catalog_LR.pdf).

### pie-weights (equipment)

Weights placed over a liner in an unfilled pastry case during baking. They support the base and sides against puffing or slumping. Coverage matters: weighing down only the centre does not necessarily support the walls.

Category: bakeware. Aliases: none. Source: [Baking trials: prepping a pie crust for prebaking](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2025/10/08/prebake-pie-weights).

### silicone-baking-mat (equipment)

A reusable silicone baking liner laid on a tray. It is distinct from a pastry cloth used for rolling dough and from disposable baking paper.

Category: bakeware. Aliases: none. Source: [Ateco catalogue: pastry wheels and dough docker, pages 73–76](https://www.atecousa.com/assets/ateco_catalog.pdf).

### pastry-cloth (equipment)

A fabric work surface for rolling pastry or dough. A matching rolling-pin cover is a separate piece; the cloth is not an oven liner.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Subtype of cloth. Source: [Ateco catalogue: pastry wheels and dough docker, pages 73–76](https://www.atecousa.com/assets/ateco_catalog.pdf).

### cannoli-form (equipment)

A cylindrical form supporting a cannoli shell during shaping and cooking. The removable form establishes the hollow centre; it is not part of the finished food.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Ateco catalogue: pastry wheels and dough docker, pages 73–76](https://www.atecousa.com/assets/ateco_catalog.pdf).

### fraisage (process)

Smear portions of pastry dough against the work surface with the heel of the hand to combine its ingredients, then gather them together. This short blending operation differs from prolonged bread kneading aimed at developing elasticity.

Category: baking-and-pastry. Aliases: none. Source: [Fraiser](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-fraiser).

### make-roux (process)

Cook flour with fat to prepare a base for thickening a sauce or soup. The chosen colour affects flavour and thickening strength. This is different from adding a raw flour slurry or finishing a sauce by emulsifying butter into it.

Category: general-cooking. Aliases: none. Source: [Professional Cooking, ninth edition: roux, page 178](https://resources.escoffier.edu/textbooks/gisslen/professional_cooking_09.pdf).

### mount-with-butter (process)

Incorporate pieces of butter into a sauce to form a smooth emulsion as a finishing step. It differs from cooking flour in fat for a roux or simply melting butter on its own; excessive heat can separate the finished emulsion.

Category: mixing-and-emulsifying. Aliases: monter au beurre. Source: [Monter au Beurre, Glorious French Food](https://app.ckbk.com/reference/glor42769c00s001e028/monter-au-beurre).

### devein-prawns (process)

Remove the intestinal tract from a prawn along its back. This preparation is distinct from removing its shell or butterflying the flesh, even when those operations occur in the same sequence.

Category: preparation-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [How to devein a prawn](https://www.greatbritishchefs.com/how-to-cook/how-to-devein-a-prawn).

### shuck-oysters (process)

Open an oyster shell and release the flesh from its attachment using an oyster knife. This is a preparation operation, not cooking or a guarantee that an oyster is safe to eat raw. The scoped name avoids conflating it with husking corn.

Category: preparation-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [How to open an oyster](https://www.greatbritishchefs.com/how-to-cook/how-to-open-an-oyster).

### make-tangzhong (process)

Cook a portion of a bread recipe’s flour and liquid together into a paste before incorporating it into the dough. This pre-gelatinises starch; it differs from making yudane by pouring boiling water over flour. Neither method is a fermented starter.

Category: baking-and-pastry. Aliases: none. Source: [A closer look at tangzhong](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2021/02/05/tangzhong-method-soft-pillowy-cinnamon-rolls).

### make-yudane (process)

Scald a portion of flour with boiling water to prepare an addition to bread dough. Unlike tangzhong, this method uses the poured hot water rather than cooking a flour-liquid mixture together in a pan. Recipe proportions remain important; the two pastes are not automatic one-for-one substitutes.

Category: baking-and-pastry. Aliases: none. Source: [A closer look at tangzhong](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2021/02/05/tangzhong-method-soft-pillowy-cinnamon-rolls).

### beat-to-ribbon (process)

Beat an egg mixture, commonly eggs and sugar, until it becomes pale and voluminous and falls from the whisk in trails that briefly remain visible. This observable endpoint differs from stiff peaks in egg whites; elapsed beating time alone does not establish it.

Category: mixing-and-emulsifying. Aliases: none. Source: [What does ribbon stage mean?](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2020/09/16/what-does-ribbon-stage-mean).

## Existing drafts improved

- **equipment/piping-bag:** The bag holds the mixture; a fitted tip shapes its exit. Changing the tip changes the pattern without changing the bag. Source: [Ateco catalogue: pastry wheels and dough docker, pages 73–76](https://www.atecousa.com/assets/ateco_catalog.pdf).
- **equipment/baking-paper:** When blind-baking, a paper liner separates pastry from loose weights and helps lift the weights out. The liner itself supplies little support; the weight and its distribution perform that job. Source: [Baking trials: prepping a pie crust for prebaking](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2025/10/08/prebake-pie-weights).
- **equipment/pie-dish:** A tart ring supplies side support without a base. A pie dish supports both base and sides, so replacing it with a ring also requires a suitable surface beneath the pastry. Source: [Matfer Bourgeat catalogue: frames and rings, page 49](https://matferbourgeatusa.com/catalog-2019/Matfer_Bourgeat_Inc_2019_Catalog_LR.pdf).
- **equipment/vegetable-peeler:** A julienne blade divides the removed layer into narrow strips. A plain peeling blade removes a broader ribbon; the same hand motion does not make the resulting cuts equivalent. Source: [Julienne Peeler](https://www.oxo.com/shop/kitchenware/utensils/julienne-peeler.html).
- **equipment/tongs:** Fish-bone tongs use gripping edges to hold individual bones. Serving tongs are designed around holding larger pieces of food, so a generic tongs reference does not establish the precision needed for bone removal. Source: [Triangle Flat Edge Fish Bone Tongs](https://matferbourgeatusa.com/product/triangle-flat-edge-fish-bone-tongs/).
- **equipment/knife:** An oyster knife opens a shell joint under leverage. A thin slicing blade is a different tool; the shared label knife should not be read as approval to use any knife for shucking. Source: [How to open an oyster](https://www.greatbritishchefs.com/how-to-cook/how-to-open-an-oyster).
- **equipment/egg-separator:** Separating raw white from yolk and slicing a cooked egg are different operations. An egg slicer portions the whole cooked egg; it does not replace a separator in preparing a raw egg mixture. Source: [Egg Slicer](https://www.oxo.com/egg-slicer.html).
- **equipment/ladle:** Ladling fat from the surface and dispensing liquid from beneath a settled fat layer approach separation from opposite sides. A fat separator is designed for the latter; an ordinary ladle does not provide its lower outlet. Source: [Good Gravy Fat Separator](https://www.oxo.com/good-gravy-fat-separator-4-cup.html).
- **equipment/whisk:** The ribbon test observes mixture falling from a lifted whisk and briefly marking the surface. It describes the mixture’s condition, rather than a particular whisk design or a fixed number of strokes. Source: [What does ribbon stage mean?](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2020/09/16/what-does-ribbon-stage-mean).
- **equipment/hand-mixer:** An electric mixer can reach ribbon stage faster than hand whisking, but the endpoint remains visual. A speed setting or a timer alone does not confirm that the egg mixture has enough volume and body. Source: [What does ribbon stage mean?](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2020/09/16/what-does-ribbon-stage-mean).
- **process/knead:** Fraisage briefly smears pastry to bring its ingredients together. It should not be treated as a request for the sustained kneading used to develop a bread dough’s elasticity. Source: [Fraiser](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-fraiser).
- **process/emulsify:** Mounting a sauce with butter is one finishing application of emulsification. It incorporates butter into the liquid rather than using flour to bind it, and the resulting sauce can separate if its emulsion is disrupted. Source: [Monter au Beurre, Glorious French Food](https://app.ckbk.com/reference/glor42769c00s001e028/monter-au-beurre).
- **process/reduce:** A roux thickens through cooked flour, whereas reduction concentrates liquid by evaporation. Choosing one does not silently authorise the other: reducing a sauce also changes its concentration. Source: [Professional Cooking, ninth edition: roux, page 178](https://resources.escoffier.edu/textbooks/gisslen/professional_cooking_09.pdf).
- **process/melt:** Melting butter changes its physical state; mounting a sauce with butter also disperses it into another liquid. A pool of melted butter is therefore not proof that the finishing emulsion has formed. Source: [Monter au Beurre, Glorious French Food](https://app.ckbk.com/reference/glor42769c00s001e028/monter-au-beurre).
- **process/butterfly:** Removing a prawn’s intestinal tract does not by itself butterfly the flesh. Treat deveining as a separate preparation decision rather than silently inferring a wider opening cut. Source: [How to devein a prawn](https://www.greatbritishchefs.com/how-to-cook/how-to-devein-a-prawn).
- **process/peel:** For prawns, removing the shell and removing the intestinal tract address different structures. A peeled prawn is not necessarily already deveined. Source: [How to devein a prawn](https://www.greatbritishchefs.com/how-to-cook/how-to-devein-a-prawn).
- **process/blind-bake:** Weights need to support the pastry sides as well as restrain the base. A small pile in the middle can leave the walls free to slump; docking and weighting perform different jobs. Source: [Baking trials: prepping a pie crust for prebaking](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2025/10/08/prebake-pie-weights).
- **process/whip:** Ribbon stage describes an egg mixture falling in trails that linger briefly on its surface. It is not the same visual test as peaks formed by whipped whites or cream. Source: [What does ribbon stage mean?](https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2020/09/16/what-does-ribbon-stage-mean).
- **process/autolyse:** A tangzhong or yudane paste is prepared with heat before entering the dough. This is distinct from an autolyse rest; resting flour and water alone does not reproduce the cooked paste. ## New identities

### pour-over-dripper (equipment)

A holder that supports a coffee filter and grounds while poured water drains through them into a vessel below. Its shape and openings influence the flow; the dripper is distinct from the filter it holds.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Source: [V60 Ceramic Coffee Dripper](https://www.hario-usa.com/products/v60-coffee-dripper-02-ceramic).

### french-press (equipment)

A coffee brewer with a vessel and plunger-mounted filter. Grounds steep in the water before the filter is lowered to retain them for pouring. This immersion arrangement differs from water passing through a separate pour-over dripper.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Source: [French press coffee maker instructions](https://d9pl0lig74xnv.cloudfront.net/product_manuals/z/p/zp2019-000001_frenchpress_coffeemakers_v1-20190308_pages.pdf).

### coffee-grinder (equipment)

A tool that reduces roasted coffee beans to particles for brewing. Grind adjustment and mechanism vary; a grinder prepares grounds but does not brew the drink. The documented burr grinder is one example, not a definition of every coffee grinder.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Source: [Encore product specifications, March 2020](https://ep-shopify.s3.amazonaws.com/related-documents/baratza/encore/baratza-encore-specs.pdf).

### espresso-machine (equipment)

A machine that extracts coffee by passing pressurised hot water through prepared grounds. A steam wand, when fitted, performs a separate milk-texturing task. A built-in grinder or automatic milk system is not implied by the name.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Source: [The Bambino espresso machine](https://www.breville.com/en-us/product/bes450).

### milk-frothing-jug (equipment)

A handled jug used to hold milk during texturing and pour it into a drink. A shaped spout helps control pouring; the jug itself is distinct from the steam wand or powered frother that aerates the milk.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Subtype of jug. Source: [Temp Control Milk Jug](https://www.breville.com/en-us/product/bes003xl).

### tea-infuser (equipment)

A perforated holder that keeps loose tea together while water circulates through it during steeping. It can be removed with the leaves inside. This differs from catching leaves in a strainer as already brewed tea is poured.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Source: [Twisting Tea Ball](https://oxoaustralia.com.au/products/twisting-tea-ball).

### bakers-couche (equipment)

A cloth folded into channels to support shaped bread dough during its final rise. The dough is then transferred to a baking surface. Its proofing role differs from a pastry cloth used under a rolling pin.

Category: bakeware. Aliases: none. Subtype of cloth. Source: [Baker’s Couche](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/bakers-couche).

### baguette-pan (equipment)

A baking pan with long channels supporting baguettes. Perforated examples let moisture escape through the pan; not every pan shares the same material or coating. It is a baking vessel, unlike a cloth used only for proofing.

Category: bakeware. Aliases: none. Subtype of baking-pan. Source: [French Baguette Pan](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/french-baguette-pan).

### madeleine-pan (equipment)

A baking pan containing shallow shell-shaped cavities for madeleines. The cavities form the characteristic outline and ridges; their count and capacity vary. A muffin tin does not provide the same shape.

Category: bakeware. Aliases: none. Subtype of baking-pan. Source: [Madeleine Pan](https://www.usapan.com/madeleine-pan-1297md).

### boning-knife (equipment)

A narrow-bladed knife for working closely around bones and trimming meat. It separates flesh from bone through controlled cuts; its name does not imply a heavy blade for chopping through bones.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Subtype of knife. Source: [Knife Finder: boning and fillet knives](https://www.wusthof.com.au/pages/knife-finder).

### fillet-knife (equipment)

A long, narrow-bladed knife suited to following a fish’s backbone and separating or skinning fillets. Flexibility varies with design. It is distinct from gripping tongs used to extract individual pin bones.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: fish filleting knife. Subtype of knife. Source: [Knife Finder: boning and fillet knives](https://www.wusthof.com.au/pages/knife-finder).

### meat-cleaver (equipment)

A broad, sturdy knife intended for heavy chopping during meat preparation. It differs from a thin slicing knife with a similar rectangular outline. Bone-cutting suitability depends on the particular blade; the unqualified word cleaver is not treated as a universal synonym.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Subtype of knife. Source: [7-inch Cleaver](https://wusthof.com/products/7-inch-cleaver).

### pizza-wheel (equipment)

A handled circular blade that rolls through pizza crust and toppings. Wheel size and clearance matter for thick toppings. Its rolling action resembles a pastry wheel, but the two tool identities are not automatically interchangeable.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Subtype of cutter. Source: [4-inch Pizza Wheel](https://www.oxo.com/4-in-pizza-wheel.html).

### ice-cube-tray (equipment)

A tray divided into cavities for freezing water into separate pieces of ice. Cavity shape and size vary; a cover is an optional design feature. The tray shapes ice but does not itself provide refrigeration.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Subtype of tray. Source: [Ice Cube Tray](https://www.oxo.com/shop/coffee-beverage/barware/ice-cube-tray.html).

### chocolate-dipping-fork (equipment)

A small supporting fork for lowering a centre into chocolate, lifting it out and releasing it onto a setting surface. It supports the centre while surplus coating drains, rather than piercing it like a serving fork.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Subtype of fork. Source: [Hand-dipped chocolates: how to](https://www.callebaut.com/en-GB/hand-dipped-chocolates-how).

### enrobe-chocolate (process)

Cover a prepared centre with a chocolate shell. Hand dipping is one way to apply the coating; the chocolate’s fluidity and removal of excess affect shell thickness. Applying the shell is distinct from tempering the chocolate beforehand.

Category: coating-and-breading. Aliases: none. Source: [Hand-dipped chocolates: how to](https://www.callebaut.com/en-GB/hand-dipped-chocolates-how).

### seed-temper-chocolate (process)

Temper melted chocolate by stirring in previously tempered chocolate that supplies suitable cocoa-butter crystals. The seed’s condition matters; this is not simply adding any cold chocolate. Check the resulting temper rather than relying only on temperature.

Category: baking-and-pastry. Aliases: none. Source: [Tempering: seeding method](https://guittard.com/chocolate-studio/fundamentals/tempering).

### table-temper-chocolate (process)

Move part of the melted chocolate over a cool worktop until it begins to crystallise, then combine it with the remaining chocolate. Time, temperature and movement work together; spreading chocolate out to cool is not by itself proof of successful tempering.

Category: baking-and-pastry. Aliases: none. Source: [Tempering: tabling chocolate](https://www.callebaut.com/en-RU/chocolate-video/technique/tempering/table).

### make-beurre-manie (process)

Work softened butter and flour together without first cooking them into a roux. The resulting paste can be incorporated into a sauce for thickening. Preparing this paste and cooking out the flour in the sauce are separate stages.

Category: general-cooking. Aliases: none. Source: [Beurre manie](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-beurre-manie).

### cook-choux-panade (process)

Cook flour into the hot liquid-and-fat mixture that forms the first stage of choux pastry, stirring until the paste comes together and loses moisture. Eggs are incorporated later; this operation is not the final bake of the shaped pastry.

Category: baking-and-pastry. Aliases: none. Source: [Baking and Pastry Arts 2024: Pate a Choux](https://www.skillsusa.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/2024_3-Pate-a-Choux.pdf).

### make-french-meringue (process)

Whip egg whites with sugar without a preliminary heating stage. The foam is then baked or used as directed in the recipe. This method differs from heating whites with sugar or adding hot syrup during whipping.

Category: mixing-and-emulsifying. Aliases: none. Source: [Different Types of Meringue](https://www.chsugar.com/baking-tips-how-tos/different-types-meringue).

### make-swiss-meringue (process)

Warm egg whites and sugar together over hot water to dissolve the sugar, then whip the mixture. The heating sequence distinguishes this preparation from French and Italian meringue; the method name alone does not certify pasteurisation.

Category: mixing-and-emulsifying. Aliases: none. Source: [Different Types of Meringue](https://www.chsugar.com/baking-tips-how-tos/different-types-meringue).

### make-italian-meringue (process)

Whip hot sugar syrup into beaten egg whites to form a meringue. The syrup is prepared separately, unlike Swiss meringue’s combined heating step. Syrup temperature alone does not establish the final egg mixture’s safety.

Category: mixing-and-emulsifying. Aliases: none. Source: [Different Types of Meringue](https://www.chsugar.com/baking-tips-how-tos/different-types-meringue).

## Existing drafts improved

- **equipment/coffee-filter:** A dripper supports the filter and the bed of grounds. The filter retains particles, while the supporting dripper supplies the shape and drainage opening; naming one does not necessarily identify the other. Source: [V60 Ceramic Coffee Dripper](https://www.hario-usa.com/products/v60-coffee-dripper-02-ceramic).
- **equipment/tea-strainer:** An infuser holds leaves during their contact with water. A strainer can instead catch leaves when the brewed tea is poured; these are different positions in the brewing sequence. Source: [Twisting Tea Ball](https://oxoaustralia.com.au/products/twisting-tea-ball).
- **equipment/moka-pot:** An espresso machine supplies controlled pressurised extraction and may provide a separate steam wand. Do not infer those capabilities merely because a stovetop coffee pot produces a concentrated drink. Source: [The Bambino espresso machine](https://www.breville.com/en-us/product/bes450).
- **equipment/spice-grinder:** Coffee grinders may provide adjustments intended for particular brewing methods. A shared grinding action does not establish that a spice grinder offers the same particle-size control or is an equivalent coffee-brewing accessory. Source: [Encore product specifications, March 2020](https://ep-shopify.s3.amazonaws.com/related-documents/baratza/encore/baratza-encore-specs.pdf).
- **equipment/jug:** A milk-frothing jug is a specialised holding and pouring vessel with a spout suited to controlled pouring. The vessel is separate from the device supplying steam or agitation; a jug alone is not a powered frother. Source: [Temp Control Milk Jug](https://www.breville.com/en-us/product/bes003xl).
- **equipment/proving-basket:** A folded couche can support several elongated dough pieces in adjacent channels before transfer to a baking surface. That arrangement differs from the shaped enclosure of a proving basket. Source: [Baker’s Couche](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/bakers-couche).
- **equipment/pastry-cloth:** A couche supports already shaped dough during proofing, whereas a pastry cloth provides a surface for rolling. Shared fabric construction does not make their preparation roles identical. Source: [Baker’s Couche](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/bakers-couche).
- **equipment/loaf-tin:** A baguette pan provides long channels for narrow loaves, often with a perforated surface. Pan geometry affects the supported shape; a loaf tin and a baguette pan are not equivalent merely because both hold bread dough. Source: [French Baguette Pan](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/french-baguette-pan).
- **equipment/chef-knife:** Boning and filleting knives use narrower blades to follow bones closely. A general chef’s knife may perform many preparation tasks, but its broad profile does not duplicate those specialist blade shapes. Source: [Knife Finder: boning and fillet knives](https://www.wusthof.com.au/pages/knife-finder).
- **equipment/fork:** A chocolate dipping fork supports a centre from below so excess coating can leave it before placement. This differs from using table-fork tines to pierce food; support and release are the important operations. Source: [Hand-dipped chocolates: how to](https://www.callebaut.com/en-GB/hand-dipped-chocolates-how).
- **process/temper-chocolate:** Tabling cools and moves part of the chocolate on a worktop before recombining it. Seeding instead introduces already crystallised chocolate. These are method choices within tempering, not aliases for simply melting chocolate. Source: [Tempering: tabling chocolate](https://www.callebaut.com/en-RU/chocolate-video/technique/tempering/table).
- **process/melt:** Melting chocolate can remove the crystal structure needed for a well-set coating. Seeding deliberately introduces suitable crystals afterwards, so fluid melted chocolate is not necessarily ready for moulding or coating. Source: [Tempering: seeding method](https://guittard.com/chocolate-studio/fundamentals/tempering).
- **process/coat:** Chocolate enrobing is a specific coating task in which the excess is controlled before the shell sets. Covering a food with chocolate and preparing that chocolate’s temper remain separate operations. Source: [Hand-dipped chocolates: how to](https://www.callebaut.com/en-GB/hand-dipped-chocolates-how).
- **process/dip:** Hand dipping a chocolate centre includes lifting it out and shedding excess coating before placement. The amount left on the centre depends on handling and chocolate fluidity, not just whether it was submerged. Source: [Hand-dipped chocolates: how to](https://www.callebaut.com/en-GB/hand-dipped-chocolates-how).
- **process/whip:** French, Swiss and Italian meringues all use whipping, but place sugar and heat into the sequence differently. Whipping alone does not specify which meringue method is intended. Source: [Different Types of Meringue](https://www.chsugar.com/baking-tips-how-tos/different-types-meringue).
- **process/beat:** In Italian meringue, beaten whites receive separately prepared hot syrup. This differs from the combined warming of whites and sugar used for Swiss meringue. Source: [Different Types of Meringue](https://www.chsugar.com/baking-tips-how-tos/different-types-meringue).
- **process/make-roux:** Beurre manie combines flour and softened butter without preliminary cooking. Roux cooks the flour-fat mixture before it is used; similar ingredients do not make these preparations the same stage or technique. Source: [Beurre manie](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-beurre-manie).
- **process/pipe:** Choux is cooked first as a panade, then eggs are incorporated before the finished paste is shaped. Piping controls the shape of that prepared paste; it does not replace the earlier pan-cooking step. Source: [Baking and Pastry Arts 2024: Pate a Choux](https://www.skillsusa.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/2024_3-Pate-a-Choux.pdf).
- **process/prove:** A couche supports shaped baguettes during the final rise and is followed by transfer to a baking surface. Supporting the dough during proofing is a separate function from containing it during baking. Source: [Baker’s Couche](https://shop.kingarthurbaking.com/items/bakers-couche).
- **process/fillet:** A narrow fillet knife can follow the backbone and separate a fish fillet. Removing small retained bones afterwards is another task; the blade operation does not guarantee that every pin bone has been extracted. Source: [Knife Finder: boning and fillet knives](https://www.wusthof.com.au/pages/knife-finder).

## New identities

### corkscrew (equipment)

A tool with a spiral worm that engages a cork so it can be withdrawn from a bottle. Lever and winged mechanisms provide different ways to lift it. Removing a cork is distinct from levering off a crown cap.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Source: [Which Type of Wine Bottle Opener is Right for You?](https://www.oxo.com/blog/coffee-and-beverages/which-wine-opener-is-right-for-you).

### bottle-opener (equipment)

A tool for lifting a crown cap from a bottle. Some designs also carry a can-piercing point; that additional feature does not make every opener a can opener or a corkscrew.

Category: coffee-and-bar. Aliases: none. Source: [Steel Bottle Opener](https://www.oxo.com/oxo-stl-bottle-opener.html).

### apple-corer (equipment)

A tool with a cutting ring that removes the central core of an apple. It leaves the surrounding fruit largely intact; a combined divider that also cuts wedges performs an additional operation.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Kitchen Utensils and Cookware 2023: fish scaler and fruit corer](https://www.roesle.com/media/fe/fe/1f/1673941906/ROESLE_Katalog_Kueche_2023_ENG_ohne_Preise.pdf).

### splatter-screen (equipment)

A perforated cover placed above a pan to intercept cooking splashes. Its openings distinguish it from a solid lid. Fit and handle design vary; it is not a sealed cooking enclosure.

Category: cookware. Aliases: none. Source: [Splatter Screen With Folding Handle](https://www.oxo.com/shop/kitchenware/cooking-baking/cookware/oxo-gg-splatter-screen.html?yoReviewsPage=3).

### sushi-rolling-mat (equipment)

A flexible mat used to support and shape a sushi roll as it is rolled up. Bamboo is a common construction. The mat is a shaping aid rather than a serving placemat or a baking surface.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Bamboo Sushi Mat](https://townfood.com/product/bamboo-sushi-mat-9-1-2x9-1-2/).

### wok-spatula (equipment)

A shovel-shaped cooking utensil used with a wok. Its head moves and lifts food, while a wok ladle has a bowl for holding liquid. Tool size should suit the wok; regional names are not assumed to be universal aliases.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Subtype of spatula. Source: [How to accessorize your wok range](https://townfood.com/wok-range/how-to-accessorize-your-wok-range/).

### wok-ladle (equipment)

A long-handled, bowl-headed utensil used in wok cooking. It can carry liquid as well as move ingredients. A wok shovel and a wok ladle are separate tools even when sold as a matched set.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Subtype of ladle. Source: [How to accessorize your wok range](https://townfood.com/wok-range/how-to-accessorize-your-wok-range/).

### meat-grinder (equipment)

A device that cuts meat and forces it through a perforated grinding plate. Plate openings influence the resulting texture. It may be a separate machine or an attachment; grinding and filling sausage casings are distinct operations.

Category: appliances. Aliases: none. Source: [Food Grinders](https://www.kitchenaid.co.uk/mixers/food-grinders).

### sausage-stuffer (equipment)

A device that feeds prepared sausage mixture through a tube into a casing. A stuffer may attach to a grinder, but the filling tube performs a different task from the grinding plate. No curing or cooking step is implied.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Using with the Sausage Stuffer Attachment](https://www.kitchenaid.com/content/dam/global/documents/202404/product-guide-w11668759-revA.pdf).

### cheese-plane (equipment)

A handled tool with a slotted cutting blade drawn across cheese to produce thin slices. Suitability depends on the cheese texture and blade. This identity covers the plane form, not every wire or knife sold as a cheese slicer.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [Cheese Slicer Amigo](https://www.boska.com/en/products/cheese-slicer-amigo).

### fish-scaler (equipment)

A toothed or serrated tool that loosens scales from the outside of a fish. It works on the skin surface, unlike a fillet knife or fish-bone tongs. Removing scales is not the same operation as removing the skin.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Source: [Kitchen Utensils and Cookware 2023: fish scaler and fruit corer](https://www.roesle.com/media/fe/fe/1f/1673941906/ROESLE_Katalog_Kueche_2023_ENG_ohne_Preise.pdf).

### carving-knife (equipment)

A long, relatively narrow knife used to cut slices from a roast or other large food. Its shape favours slicing strokes rather than heavy chopping. A carving knife is distinct from a cleaver or a narrow boning knife.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Subtype of knife. Source: [Classic Ikon 9-inch Carving Knife](https://wusthof.com/products/classic-ikon-9-inch-carving-knife).

### grilling-basket (equipment)

A basket that supports small pieces of food on a grill. Openings admit heat while the sides help contain the pieces. Construction and grill compatibility vary; it does not replace the grill that supplies heat.

Category: cookware. Aliases: none. Source: [Deluxe Grilling Basket](https://www.weber.com/US/en/accessories/grill-tools-and-cookware/deluxe-grilling-basket-6434/6434.html).

### vegetable-spiralizer (equipment)

A cutting device that turns vegetables against blades to form long spirals or ribbons. Blade choice changes the shape. It cuts existing vegetable flesh rather than extruding a mixed pasta dough.

Category: knives-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [Tabletop Spiralizer](https://www.oxo.com/tabletop-spiralizer.html).

### pasta-extruder (equipment)

A device that presses pasta dough through a shaped die. The die forms the cross-section and a cutter controls length. This differs from thinning a sheet between pasta rollers before cutting it.

Category: preparation-tools. Aliases: none. Subtype of pasta-machine. Source: [Gourmet Pasta Press](https://www.kitchenaid.com/countertop-appliances/stand-mixers/attachments/p.gourmet-pasta-press.KSMPEXTA.html).

### glaze-vegetables (process)

Cook vegetables with a small amount of liquid, butter and sugar so the reducing liquid forms a coating. The endpoint may be pale or browned. This scoped method is distinct from icing a cake or brushing a glaze onto cooked meat.

Category: moist-heat-cooking. Aliases: none. Source: [Glacer](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-glacer).

### salt-drain-vegetables (process)

Salt prepared vegetables to draw out some of their water, then drain as the recipe directs. This moisture-removal step differs from simply seasoning the finished dish. Rinsing and final seasoning remain recipe-specific; no preservation guarantee is implied.

Category: preparation-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [Degorger](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-degorger).

### singer (process)

Sprinkle flour over ingredients already cooked in fat, cook the flour briefly, then add liquid to form a thickened sauce. The sequence distinguishes this method from flouring raw food before frying or preparing a separate roux.

Category: general-cooking. Aliases: none. Source: [Singer](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-singer).

### make-starch-slurry (process)

Disperse starch in cold liquid before incorporating it into a hot preparation for thickening. Preparing the dispersion is separate from the later cooking stage. The starch type and recipe determine proportions and treatment.

Category: general-cooking. Aliases: none. Source: [Liaison](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-liaison).

### coil-fold-dough (process)

Use coil folds to build structure in bread dough during bulk fermentation. This gentle folding method is distinct from stretching an edge over the dough or laminating it out broadly. It is a dough-development step, not the final shaping of the loaf.

Category: baking-and-pastry. Aliases: none. Source: [Bulk Fermentation Handling](https://thesourdoughjourney.com/faq-bulk-fermentation-handling/).

### extrude-pasta (process)

Press pasta dough through a shaped die and cut the emerging pasta to length. The die determines the profile. Rolling a sheet and cutting strips can produce pasta too, but uses a different forming method.

Category: preparation-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [Gourmet Pasta Press](https://www.kitchenaid.com/countertop-appliances/stand-mixers/attachments/p.gourmet-pasta-press.KSMPEXTA.html).

### spiralize-vegetables (process)

Cut vegetables into long spiral strands or ribbons by turning them against a suitable blade. The vegetable itself supplies the strand; this is not extrusion of flour-based dough, even when the result is served like noodles.

Category: preparation-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [Tabletop Spiralizer](https://www.oxo.com/tabletop-spiralizer.html).

### stuff-sausage-casings (process)

Feed prepared sausage mixture through a filling tube into a casing while guiding the casing as it fills. Grinding the ingredients precedes this forming step where needed. Stuffing alone neither cooks nor preserves the sausage.

Category: preparation-and-cutting. Aliases: none. Source: [Using with the Sausage Stuffer Attachment](https://www.kitchenaid.com/content/dam/global/documents/202404/product-guide-w11668759-revA.pdf).

## Existing drafts improved

- **equipment/can-opener:** A bottle opener releases a crown cap; a can-piercing point may be included on the same tool. A combined design does not make those operations equivalent to cutting around a can lid. Source: [Steel Bottle Opener](https://www.oxo.com/oxo-stl-bottle-opener.html).
- **equipment/ladle:** Wok ladles are sized for wok cooking and differ from shovel-headed utensils used alongside them. A shared handle style does not make a ladle bowl and a lifting blade interchangeable. Source: [How to accessorize your wok range](https://townfood.com/wok-range/how-to-accessorize-your-wok-range/).
- **equipment/frying-pan:** A perforated splatter screen intercepts splashes while leaving openings. A solid lid provides a different enclosure; selecting one in place of the other changes how the vessel is covered. Source: [Splatter Screen With Folding Handle](https://www.oxo.com/shop/kitchenware/cooking-baking/cookware/oxo-gg-splatter-screen.html?yoReviewsPage=3).
- **equipment/wok:** Wok shovels and ladles have different head shapes, and manufacturers offer sizes matched to different wok arrangements. The pan name alone does not specify a suitable utensil size. Source: [How to accessorize your wok range](https://townfood.com/wok-range/how-to-accessorize-your-wok-range/).
- **equipment/pasta-roller:** An extruder forms dough through a die; a roller thins dough between rollers. Both prepare pasta, but a die profile and a roller gap control different aspects of its shape. Source: [Gourmet Pasta Press](https://www.kitchenaid.com/countertop-appliances/stand-mixers/attachments/p.gourmet-pasta-press.KSMPEXTA.html).
- **equipment/stand-mixer:** A grinder attachment adds cutting and perforated-plate functions to a mixer. Those functions are not supplied by the ordinary mixing bowl and beater, and attachment compatibility must be checked separately. Source: [Food Grinders](https://www.kitchenaid.co.uk/mixers/food-grinders).
- **equipment/julienne-peeler:** A spiralizer forms continuous spiral strands by rotation. Producing narrow strips with a peeler does not establish the same shape or movement, even when both preparations are described as vegetable noodles. Source: [Tabletop Spiralizer](https://www.oxo.com/tabletop-spiralizer.html).
- **equipment/fillet-knife:** A scaler removes scales from the skin surface. Filleting separates flesh from the skeleton; neither tool name implies that the other preparation has already been completed. Source: [Kitchen Utensils and Cookware 2023: fish scaler and fruit corer](https://www.roesle.com/media/fe/fe/1f/1673941906/ROESLE_Katalog_Kueche_2023_ENG_ohne_Preise.pdf).
- **equipment/grill:** A grilling basket holds smaller pieces on the cooking surface. It is an accessory supported by the grill, not an independent heat source; its dimensions and fit remain separate considerations. Source: [Deluxe Grilling Basket](https://www.weber.com/US/en/accessories/grill-tools-and-cookware/deluxe-grilling-basket-6434/6434.html).
- **equipment/paring-knife:** A dedicated corer removes a central section with a shaped cutting tool. Using a knife to cut around a core is another approach, but does not make the two tools identical. Source: [Corer](https://www.oxo.com/corer-475.html).
- **process/glaze:** Vegetable glazing can reduce its cooking liquid into a coating. Cake icing and brushing a cooked roast with juices are other meanings of glaze; the broad verb does not identify one recipe sequence. Source: [Glacer](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-glacer).
- **process/drain:** Salting vegetables can release liquid before draining. Draining removes that liquid, while the preceding salting step changes how much water is available to remove. Source: [Degorger](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-degorger).
- **process/dry-brine:** Salting vegetables specifically to remove released water has its own preparation goal. Do not treat every salt-and-rest instruction as an interchangeable dry-brining method. Source: [Degorger](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-degorger).
- **process/reduce:** Adding a starch slurry thickens by introducing starch rather than by evaporating more liquid. A recipe may use either or both; a thickened sauce is not evidence that it has been reduced. Source: [Liaison](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-liaison).
- **process/dredge:** Singer adds flour after ingredients have cooked in fat and before liquid is added. Dredging food before frying follows a different sequence; both use flour but are not interchangeable instructions. Source: [Singer](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-singer).
- **process/make-roux:** Singer cooks flour around ingredients already in the pan. A separate roux prepares the flour-fat mixture independently before it is combined with liquid or other ingredients. Source: [Singer](https://chefsimon.com/articles/lexique-singer).
- **process/grind:** In a meat grinder, the cutting mechanism and perforated plate produce the ground texture. Changing the plate differs from passing mixture through a sausage-filling tube, whose purpose is to fill the casing. Source: [Food Grinders](https://www.kitchenaid.co.uk/mixers/food-grinders).
- **process/shape:** Sausage stuffing forms a prepared mixture within a casing using a filling tube. Forming a patty by hand follows another method; a shared mixture does not make their shaping instructions equivalent. Source: [Using with the Sausage Stuffer Attachment](https://www.kitchenaid.com/content/dam/global/documents/202404/product-guide-w11668759-revA.pdf).
- **process/stretch-and-fold:** Coil folding is another dough-handling method used during bulk fermentation. It places more emphasis on gentle folding; a recipe may combine methods rather than treating their names as exact synonyms. Source: [Bulk Fermentation Handling](https://thesourdoughjourney.com/faq-bulk-fermentation-handling/).
- **process/laminate:** Bread-dough lamination can be combined with coil folds during bulk fermentation. A broad stretch and folding the dough in place are different handling stages, even when both contribute to dough structure. Source: [Bulk Fermentation Handling](https://thesourdoughjourney.com/faq-bulk-fermentation-handling/).

Unrelated ignored archives are excluded from clean tracked-source exports without weakening the audit or opening or changing those archives. Corpus and Site edits are count expectations for the larger knowledge set, not recipe, application or presentation changes.

## Review backlog and boundaries

The drafts still require human review. Regional cookware and tool names are kept separate where equivalence is unproven; contextual links do not imply substitutions. Safety-sensitive processes do not gain preservation schedules or universal temperature/pressure instructions. Broad terms such as electric beaters, tamis and china cap remain unresolved; cold-smoking and flash-frying need focused scope/safety work. Some earlier deferred concrete tools were subsequently researched and added, as the individual ledgers show. Prioritise review and enrichment of the 128 remaining equipment/process pages before another large expansion of identities.

## Smallest reliable autocomplete architecture

Use Core as the sole vocabulary owner. A small provider can enumerate Vocabulary.entries (kind, ID, canonical_name, names, plural_names, aliases, reference, categories and type_of), use the existing resolver for equivalence, and use parsed declarations for local scope. JSON transport already preserves these fields; no new schema or language server is necessary for a first provider. The Node loader supplies indexed YAML to editor integrations; browser clients can consume the serialised vocabulary.

For equipment declarations suggest canonical equipment types with aliases as searchable labels, deduplicated by kind+ID. Within a recipe, rank already declared equipment first and insert its authored local name; do not replace flour bowl with a global bowl suggestion. Within angle brackets suggest process/action heads only. Give meaningful culinary techniques and observed ordinary actions appropriate context-based ranking; downrank enjoy/eat and composite compatibility heads. Reference false must not mean invalid or automatically excluded. Use Corpus frequency as a secondary ranking signal, never as proof of identity or a universal popularity ranking.

Acceptance targets: no cross-domain suggestions in typed contexts; one candidate per identity; exact authored local labels retained; no suggestion silently turns an ambiguous term into an alias; source unchanged until the author accepts a completion. Lexical cursor/context detection must tolerate incomplete syntax, then reuse Core parsing once viable rather than build a second recipe parser. Prototype this separately in the existing VS Code extension; no editor changes were made here.

## Process/action review

Ten generic heads are marked reference:false: move, open, close, use, wait, insert, lift, slide, handle and test. Each retains its canonical ID, names, syntax and resolver identity. They express ordinary manipulation, instruction or waiting rather than a distinct technique needing a knowledge page; test does not prescribe a technique or endpoint by itself. Their action parameters remain literal. Roast, ferment and emulsify are retained and tested; borderline rest, heat, drain, line, shape and similar techniques are not blanket-suppressed.

Site previously only handled the lemon-juice compatibility route. Batch 1 reuses that small static-page pattern: each /opensaucefood/processes/<id>/ URL still returns an explanatory noindex HTML page, canonicalizing/linking to the process index. This is a compatibility landing page, not an HTTP redirect or a replacement culinary entry. Removed entries are absent from indexes, canonical reference projections and new recipe links. The list is exported from Core reference utilities so Site and tests share it. No server routing framework, production configuration or generic verb vocabulary is added.

| Action | Corpus occurrences before suppression | Decision |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| move | 7 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| open | 2 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| close | 2 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| use | 2 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| wait | 5 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| insert | 1 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| lift | 2 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| slide | 3 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| handle | 0 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |
| test | 2 | Generic; keep compatibility URL and action identity |

## Eight equipment category decisions

| Record | Evidence / scope | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cooking-wood | baby-back-ribs:29; smoking fuel, not a tool/container | Deferred: no suitable fuel/fire category; do not force cookware |
| cutter | Existing observed qualifiers round / 5cm; generic cutting implement | knives-and-cutting; does not imply a knife or narrow cookie-cutter alias |
| dish | bread-pudding:31/48 and pulled-rabbit:62; general containing vessel | storage-and-containers; do not promise oven safety |
| grease-pan | creme-brulee:35/45–47; pan containing ramekins and water in oven | bakeware; no speculative rename to roasting pan |
| plate | Existing serving/holding uses across recipes | Deferred: tableware is not well represented; avoid storage-only classification |
| soup-plate | Existing pudding serving/holding evidence | Deferred with plate; no new category in this batch |
| tray | pho-soup:43; potato-and-eggplant-curry:37; differing uses | storage-and-containers, not blanket oven-safe bakeware |
| vessel | pretzels:36 explicitly heat-safe/chemically non-reactive | storage-and-containers; qualifiers remain author responsibility |

Secondary fixes: explicit baking trays/baking sheets plural_names on baking-tray; paper towels on paper-towel. Generic cup, cauldron, clay casserole, flour bowl, work surface and oven dish remain unresolved rather than receiving guessed aliases. Electric beaters remains deliberately unresolved.

## Validation

Core: typecheck, build, 559 tests, documentation checks and quality audit passed. Corpus: 395 existing integration tests passed. Site: 128 integration tests passed, including full generated link/path validation and the ten new noindex compatibility-page assertions. Focused Core tests cover 24 cases, source preservation, exact part anchors, retained distinctions, malformed plural rejection, collision rejection, action semantics and categories. Full browser acceptance is not claimed; static generation/routing tests cover this batch. The working-tree public-source check stopped on the pre-existing ignored examples/open-sauce-chatgpt-batch-1.zip. That user archive remains untouched; a clean approved-source export is audited separately without weakening the checker. Final diff checks passed. The unchanged Core checker passed against a clean approved-source export (1,035 files, 810 vocabulary records, 14 curated samples), using existing Core dependencies without installing anything. Site type checking and its local build/full link validation also passed. Integrity hashes confirm all 2,265 Corpus files and seven known user files unchanged.

## Reproduction

The audit scripts remain outside repositories in _work/audits. vocabulary-quality-v1-measure.mjs and vocabulary-quality-v1-measure-after.mjs are the original knowledge-base-v1-audit.mjs with only output JSON filenames changed. Before/after snapshots preserve file hashes, all ranked queues and metrics. The before run used the baseline data above; do not overwrite it by running the before script on modified data. The after script reads the current checked-out Core and unchanged Corpus.

Run pnpm check, pnpm build, pnpm test, pnpm docs:check and pnpm quality:audit in Core; pnpm test in Corpus and Site. Integration commands create ignored test workspaces. No network or dependency installation is needed with the installed dependencies. No recipe sources are modified.

## Next: Processes & Equipment v1

Measured post-batch gaps remain 295 equipment occurrences / 105 distinct forms and 269 action occurrences / 98 forms. Equipment resolution is about 90% by usage but only 60% by distinct form, so it is not close to reliable broad autocomplete completeness. Actions resolve about 94% by usage but 70% by distinct head; frequent everyday verbs dominate, while missing techniques and multiword forms remain. Neither domain has a defensible universal completeness percentage.

Propose a bounded 20–30 equipment-term review (plural forms, vessels, cookware, local roles), a 20–30 action-head review (put/return versus roll out, rise, warm, and alternative heads), and a tableware/fuel category decision. Use completion candidates only from explicitly accepted names; keep generic actions distinguishable from page-eligible techniques and never infer culinary equivalence from similar words. Review remaining generic pages and compatibility URLs before broader publication. Confirm scope/aliases, source evidence and ambiguity tests per term. No autocomplete/LSP implementation belongs to this batch.
